- **Today**: the gate itself is sound and stays — `HeliosWaitFrameComplete` does `ExecuteFlush` then sleeps on DXVK's submission-fence condition variable with a bounded timeout, i.e. a real event wait with a safety bound, not a delay faking ordering. The defect is reporting: `EXT_FLIP_GATE_TIMEOUTS` increments only when `is_vehicle_present`, so an expiry on the **direct-primary path — the one that ships —** increments nothing on the Rust side and logs nothing; the only trace is the aggregated C++ `present-gate: ... timeouts=` line every 128 presents. `dxgi_present1`'s multi path ignores the boolean entirely. A gate expiry means the present is published while DXVK still has queued work — exactly the producer race the gate exists to close.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: steady-state gate expiry on the direct primary (the 10 ms bound being hit every frame under load) is indistinguishable from a healthy run in the guest counters, so the stale-frame symptom gets blamed on the KMD marker or the host.
- **Change**: add `PRESENT_GATE_TIMEOUTS` and increment it for every non-confirmation regardless of path (keep the vehicle-specific counter, or fold both into one with a path tag), and rate-limit-log the first few. Wrap the bridge call in `#[must_use] enum GateOutcome { Completed, Expired }` and convert both call sites, including `dxgi_present1`. Document the counter as "gate did not confirm completion" rather than "timed out": `present_frame_gate` also returns false when `impl`/`context` is missing or an exception was caught (`dxvk_bridge.cpp:1756`, `:1795-1801`), so a nonzero count folds those in.
- **Static guarantee**: real. `#[must_use]` makes the Present1 drop site a compiler warning instead of a silent discard.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit (counter + `must_use` wrapper + both call sites). Independent of the present-tail dedup (u-forward-b-04, T7) — do not wait for it.
- **Risk**: low.
- **Validation**: the counter reads 0 on a healthy DWM session and is proven to MOVE this boot by setting `PresentGateUs=1`; the C++ `present-gate:` line's `timeouts=` field must agree with it.

### R415. Replace the vehicle present protocol's three thread-locals with one state enum plus a device-liveness check

- **Finding**: u-forward-b-05, merges x-ordering-14.
- **Where**: `umd/src/forward.rs:8131-8149` (the three `thread_local` cells), `:8255-8296` (`set_present_source`, whose refusal at `:8264-8270` logs but counts nothing), `:8298-8317` (`wait_last_present`, the SAFETY comment and `&*(dev_ptr as *const HeliosDevice)`), `:8323-8338` (`take_present_result`), `:9286-9294` (`LAST_VEHICLE_DEVICE` set to `h.pDrvPrivate` after a minted present), `:9065-9068` and `:9126-9127` (the only two clear sites); ICD side: `icd/mesa/src/vulkan/wsi/wsi_common_win32.cpp:745-753` (`vehicle_finish` releases `v->dev`), `:1647` (the `vehicle_finish` call), `:2139-2161` (SUCCESS-but-not-displayed statuses fall through), `:2218-2231` (`get_result` -> `-1` -> `wait_present`).
- **Today**: `PRESENT_SOURCE`, `LAST_VEHICLE_DEVICE` and `PRESENT_RESULT` encode a four-step cross-DLL protocol (set-source -> Present -> get-result -> optional wait) whose ordering is enforced only by comments and by counters that fire after the fact. `LAST_VEHICLE_DEVICE` stores a `*const HeliosDevice` as a `usize`; it is set on every minted vehicle present and cleared only on the two failure paths inside `dxgi_present`. Nothing clears it at `destroy_device` (grep: no other writer) and nothing ties it to the device's lifetime — the pointer is runtime-owned private memory dxgkrnl may free and reuse. The SAFETY comment asserts a same-thread, immediately-after contract that the *ICD*, not this code, is responsible for honouring.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: the vehicle D3D11 device is per-swapchain and is released on the ICD worker thread. Chain A presents (`LAST_VEHICLE_DEVICE` = A) -> chain A is destroyed and device A released on that worker -> a new chain B is created on the same worker -> B's first `Present()` returns a SUCCESS-but-not-displayed status (`DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED`, explicitly handled at `:2139-2161`) so dxgkrnl never calls our present DDI and the TLS slot is neither updated nor cleared -> `get_result` returns `-1` -> `v->wait_present(...)` -> `&*(dev_ptr as *const HeliosDevice)` dereferences the freed private block of device A and calls through `dev.dxvk`.
- **Change**: collapse the three cells into `thread_local! { static VEHICLE: RefCell<VehicleSlot> }` with `enum VehicleSlot { Idle, Armed(PresentSource), Minted { device: usize, result: Option<(u32, u64)> } }`. Add a process-global liveness registry of live `HeliosDevice` pointers (`Mutex<HashSet<usize>>` written at `CreateDevice` and `ddi_destroy_device` — the lock is taken once per wait, never on a per-draw path) and have `wait_last_present` refuse (`-1`, counted) when the recorded pointer is not currently live. **Do not** use a single global epoch bumped on any destroy: a stale-epoch refusal returns `-1`, which the ICD treats as "no gate" and then performs no wait at all (`wsi_common_win32.cpp:2226-2231`), reintroducing the 21st-session torn-copy class for unrelated devices. Also add the missing counter for `set_present_source`'s refusal path.
- **Static guarantee**: the exhaustive enum makes "result pending with no device" and "device recorded with no present" unrepresentable — real. The liveness check is a runtime-guarded refusal, not a proof: a true compile-time lifetime is not achievable across the C export boundary, so name it as such.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the ICD may still call on a thread whose device dies between the liveness check and the dereference; only single-threaded-per-device DDI discipline prevents that, and it cannot be encoded across an `extern "system"` boundary.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit touching `set_present_source`, `wait_last_present`, `take_present_result`, the `dxgi_present` prologue/epilogue, `CreateDevice` and `ddi_destroy_device`. Land after R412 and R414 (all three edit `dxgi_present`; this one edits its prologue/epilogue, they edit the middle).
- **Risk**: medium — the new refusal path must not start eating valid waits.
- **Validation**: `EXT_OVERWRITES` / `EXT_RESULT_MISSES` / `EXT_RESULT_OVERWRITES` hold their current values over a dcomp-vehicle run (`HELIOS_WSI_DCOMP_PRESENT=1`) and the vehicle present ordinal log is unchanged; ICD-side `helios_vehicle_gate_fallbacks` and `helios_vehicle_wait_timeouts` must not increase — that is the proof the refusal did not start replacing real waits with no wait.

### R416. Resolve the seven ICD exports into a process-wide table that caches successes only

- **Finding**: u-bridge-04. It subsumes the export-cache half of R417.
- **CORRECTED ON HARDWARE 2026-07-27 (T2 implementation):** this is NOT "the largest measured per-frame win in the tranche" — it is not a per-frame cost at all in the shipping configuration. The claim rests on `residOf` running on the present thread once or twice per frame, but all three `present_sync_publish` call sites are gated on `present_sync_publish_enabled()`, which reads `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Helios!PresentSyncPublish` and defaults to 0 — and that key does not exist on the live box (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Helios` itself is absent). Same-boot evidence with a QPC accumulator around `residOf`: **2432 dwm presents produced zero `resid-lookup:` lines and zero `present_sync_publish` markers.** The measurable cost is at RESOURCE CREATE (`get_resource_memory_info` ×2 lookups, ~118 calls over a boot plus two DComp probe runs) and at device create. The unbounded `LoadLibraryA` refcount growth is real regardless and is what the gate's "module count flat" check covers. The item is still worth doing; the headline is wrong.
- **Where**: `umd/bridge/dxvk_bridge.cpp:64-82` (`find_export_in_loaded_modules`: full `TH32CS_SNAPMODULE` snapshot + `GetProcAddress` per module, no cache), `:260-288` (`find_export_via_vulkan_icd_manifests`: manifest walk + `LoadLibraryA` with **no** `FreeLibrary`; `find_helios_icd_export` composes the two), `:290-306` and `:321-345` (the two ctx-id readers), `:485-544` (the five memory/ownership wrappers, each resolving on every call), `:1275` (`open_kmd_scanout_target`'s `helios_venus_query_scanout` lookup), `:1100-1103` (`get_resource_memory_info` does TWO lookups per call), `:1885-1897` (`residOf` falls back to `venus_memory_resource_id_from_handle` whenever `sharing.heliosResourceId` is 0), `dxvk-helios/src/d3d11/d3d11_texture.cpp:85` (the ONLY assignment of `sharing.heliosResourceId`, on the import arm — verified by grep across the fork), `umd/src/forward.rs:8461`, `:9109`, `:10020` (the three `present_sync_publish` call sites, all per-present), `:861` + `:757-766` (`publish_dwm_composition` -> `ensure_kmd_scanout_target`, per present on DWM).
- **Today**: `find_helios_icd_export` caches nothing. Every call takes a full process module snapshot and calls `GetProcAddress` on every loaded module until it reaches the Mesa ICD, which is late in the load order so most of the list is walked; on a miss it then walks the Vulkan ICD manifest list, reads and parses JSON from disk, and `LoadLibraryA`s each candidate with no matching `FreeLibrary`, so a persistent miss also grows module refcounts without bound. Because `sharing.heliosResourceId` is written only on the import arm, every *created* surface (the DWM scan-out primary, the vehicle backbuffer) takes `residOf`'s fallback, so the snapshot runs on the present thread every frame — once or twice depending on whether `dst` is distinct. `get_resource_memory_info` costs two lookups per resource create. A third per-present instance: on DWM, `ensure_kmd_scanout_target` retries the `helios_venus_query_scanout` lookup on every present until the import caches.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a — this is a cost defect, not an ordering one. Steady-state 60 fps = 60-120 `CreateToolhelp32Snapshot` calls per second per presenting device, each iterating `Module32Next` + `GetProcAddress` over every loaded module, on the exact path the PSC stage measures for present-to-scanout latency.
- **Change**: add `struct HeliosIcdExports { std::atomic<Fn> ... };` with a `HeliosIcdExports& helios_icd()` accessor behind a function-local static, holding all seven exports (`helios_venus_current_ctx_id`, `helios_venus_instance_ctx_id`, `helios_venus_memory_id`, `helios_venus_memory_res_id`, `helios_venus_memory_transfer_resource_ownership`, `helios_venus_memory_alloc_info`, `helios_venus_query_scanout`). Keep the discovery order exactly as it is so a resolution that works today still works. **CRITICAL: cache only successful resolutions, per export.** A plain `std::call_once` or magic static over the resolution would freeze an early `nullptr` — the Mesa ICD is not loaded until `new dxvk::DxvkInstance` at `:2215`, and `query_scanout` in particular can legitimately miss before the KMD has a bound primary — and would permanently disable the venus identity plumbing for the process. Retry on failure exactly as today. Rate-limit the per-call "export unavailable" logs (they are themselves per-call file I/O, see R426).
- **Static guarantee**: real in the sense that matters: the per-slot `std::atomic<Fn>` makes "has this been resolved" a single load instead of a per-call module walk, removes six duplicated resolution wrappers and removes the unbounded `LoadLibraryA` refcount growth. The atomic (rather than a plain member) is what keeps retry-on-failure race-free without a mutex.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the exports are still `__cdecl` pointers `reinterpret_cast` from `GetProcAddress`; the signature contract with the Mesa ICD stays a hand-mirrored ABI.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit — add the table + accessor, rewrite the six wrappers and `open_kmd_scanout_target`'s inline lookup to read from it. No call-site signature changes. Land after R411 so the bodies being edited are already guarded.
- **Risk**: low-medium. The failure mode to avoid is exactly the latched-nullptr one above; a review checklist item is "no code path stores nullptr into a slot".
- **Validation**: **measure first** (PSC rule): add a QPC-stamped accumulator around `residOf` before the change and record present-thread microseconds per frame in `umd-<pid>.log`; after the change that number must drop and the `copy-lat:` / `present-gate:` histograms must show equal-or-better `avg_us` with an identical desktop screenshot. Functional proof: `get_resource_memory_info` returns the same `venus_id`/`res_id` for the same resources (diff the log lines across the change), and a cold-boot run must still log `resolved helios_venus_query_scanout via ICD manifest ...` (or its in-module equivalent) **after** a first failed attempt, proving retry-on-failure survived. Module count for dwm.exe stable over a 10-minute session (proves the `LoadLibraryA` leak is closed).

### R417. Give the legacy LINEAR scanout probe a negative cache so it stops re-running on every bind and flush

- **Finding**: u-forward-a-06.
- **Where**: `umd/src/forward.rs:757-802` (`ensure_kmd_scanout_target`; the only positive short-circuit is `scanout_import.borrow().is_some()` at `:764-766`), `:817-825` (the `direct_primary` guard whose `||` short-circuit evaluates the probe), `:4436` (unconditional `track_dwm_composition_target` from `set_render_targets`), `:3310-3324` (`flush` -> `publish_dwm_composition` -> `ensure_kmd_scanout_target`, plus the refresh-marker submission at `:3320`), `:9070`, `:9120`, `:9410`, `:9918`, `:10012` (the five present-side `publish_dwm_composition` calls), `:861` (`publish_dwm_composition` calls the probe unconditionally); the probe body: `umd/bridge/dxvk_bridge.cpp:1275-1279` -> `icd/mesa/src/virtio/vulkan/vn_renderer_helios.c:1251-1292` (a `D3DKMTEscape`, `HELIOS_ESCAPE_QUERY_SCANOUT`, under `helios_current_renderer_lock` **and** `helios->dev_mutex`) -> `kmd_render/src/ddi/escape.rs:98-125` (which adds a virtio `resource_is_live` round-trip whenever a resource id is published).
- **Today**: the frozen baseline says DWM renders directly into the Windows-designated OPTIMAL primary with no guest primary-to-scanout copy, yet the whole LINEAR-copy cluster is still on the active path. `set_render_targets` calls `track_dwm_composition_target` unconditionally, and for any RTV0 with a non-zero resource pointer that is not a recorded direct-scanout primary the `||` chain at `:823` evaluates `ensure_kmd_scanout_target`. That function short-circuits **only** when `scanout_import` is already `Some` — there is no negative cache — so whenever the probe fails it re-runs on every bind. The probe is an uncached toolhelp module walk (with an ICD-manifest disk-parse fallback) followed by a kernel escape taken under two ICD locks whose KMD handler adds a virtio round-trip. `publish_dwm_composition` re-runs the same probe from `flush()` and from five present sites. The probe also has a side effect inside a boolean guard: it overwrites six device scanout `Cell`s at `:788-796`.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a — cost and dead weight, not an invalid state. The failure mode is unbounded repetition rather than a one-time cost: any of (a) `primary_scanout_resource == 0`, (b) `resource_is_live` false, (c) `open_ddi_texture2d` returning 0 leaves `scanout_import` `None` and re-arms the whole walk-plus-escape for the next `OMSetRenderTargets`.
- **Change**: three commits, in this order. (1) Replace `scanout_import: RefCell<Option<ID3D11Resource>>` plus implicit retry with `enum KmdScanoutTarget { Unprobed, Unavailable { at_generation: u32 }, Ready(ImportedScanout) }` on `HeliosDevice`, so the probe runs at most once per scanout generation, and log the `Unavailable` transitions. Pair it with a re-arm on generation change so a LINEAR target that appears later is still picked up. (2) The bridge-side export cache — **this is R416**; do not implement it twice. (3) Only then consider moving composition-target selection off the bind path. **Correction to the obvious step (3):** `set_render_targets` cannot simply stop calling `track_dwm_composition_target` — that call is the ONLY writer of `dev.composition_source`, which `publish_dwm_composition` reads at `:867-871`. Deleting it silently disables the entire legacy LINEAR copy *and* the `flush()` refresh-marker submission at `:3320`. Retiring the cluster is owner-gated and evidence-gated: the LINEAR path is still the fallback when the direct primary cannot be bound.
- **Static guarantee**: real. The tri-state makes "we already decided this is unavailable" representable, which `Option` cannot express (absent is indistinguishable from unprobed). `Ready(ImportedScanout)` should own `resource_raw`/`resource_id`/`width`/`height`/`pitch`/`format` as one validated struct instead of six independent `Cell`s (that field consolidation is u-forward-a-10's, in T3).
- **Remaining unsafe**: the imported `ID3D11Resource` COM ownership from `open_kmd_scanout_target` stays a raw `usize` across the cxx boundary; cxx cannot express COM ownership transfer.
- **Atomic boundary**: commit (1) here — enum + generation re-arm. Commit (2) is R416. Commit (3) needs owner sign-off; do not combine.
- **Risk**: medium — a previously-retrying probe stops retrying, which is the point, so the generation re-arm is the load-bearing part of the diff.
- **Validation**: before/after counts of `DWM KMD scanout import ready` and `helios_venus_query_scanout export unavailable` per second in dwm's UMD log, and of `HELIOS_ESCAPE_QUERY_SCANOUT` arrivals in the KMD diag ring per second — both must drop to a bounded number. DComp probe fps before/after. Behaviour gate: desktop visible, `ScanoutDiag` absent, `VpSA=1`, `ScSet=1`, rapid cursor motion with no trails; and the LINEAR fallback must still engage when the direct primary cannot bind.

### R418. Count open_kmd_scanout_target's three refusals, consume the fields the ICD returns, and make entry into the copy path loud

- **Finding**: u-bridge-09.
- **Where**: `umd/bridge/dxvk_bridge.cpp:1260-1311` (the whole function: `:1276-1279` logged refusal, `:1282-1284` unlogged refusal, `:1294-1295` unlogged refusal, none counted), `:1286-1293` (the literal `87` substituted for `info.dxgiFormat`), `:1306` (`info.planeOffset` printed and otherwise ignored), `:347-358` (`HeliosVenusScanoutInfo` including `dxgiFormat` and `planeOffset`, `static_assert` 40), `icd/mesa/src/virtio/vulkan/vn_renderer_helios.c:239-263` (the matching struct and its `_Static_assert(sizeof == 40)`), `umd/src/forward.rs:757-766`, `:774-780`, `:817-823`, `:858-887`, `:3312`, `:9070`, `:9120`, `:9410`, `:9918`, `:10012` (the reachability chain).
- **Today**: this is the entry point for the guest primary-to-scanout LINEAR copy target, and it is **not** only reached on an exact-primary miss: `publish_dwm_composition` calls `ensure_kmd_scanout_target` unconditionally from six present/flush paths, gated only by `is_dwm_process()` and short-circuited once the import exists. The `direct_primary` test at `forward.rs:817-823` gates only the *selection* of a composition source, not whether this function runs. Three defects inside it: (a) it fetches `info.dxgiFormat` and `info.planeOffset` from the ICD and discards both, substituting the literal `87` and ignoring the plane offset entirely; (b) it returns 0 for "not yet available", "export missing" and "import failed" with a named counter for none of them; (c) it is an unsealed fallback — nothing prevents this LINEAR copy target from becoming the presented primary when the direct-primary bookkeeping mismatches, which is precisely the silent-regression shape (a working-looking desktop on the retired path) the stage exists to eliminate.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: a direct-primary allocation is created but its handle is not recorded in `direct_scanout_allocations` (a bookkeeping miss) -> `track_dwm_composition_target`'s `direct_primary` test fails -> `composition_source` gets selected -> `publish_dwm_composition` starts doing a per-frame `CopySubresourceRegion` into the LINEAR alias -> the desktop still appears, so the regression from the direct path to the copy path is invisible except in one log line.
- **CORRECTED ON HARDWARE 2026-07-27 (T2 implementation):** item (3)'s loud line must sit at the COPY, not at the import. Opening the LINEAR target only arms the fallback; `publish_dwm_composition` copies through it only once a composition source has been selected. Same-boot evidence: `DWM KMD scanout import ready` fires 5× and `open_kmd_scanout_target` 2× on a healthy boot while `DWM desktop->LINEAR scanout copy` and `DWM composition target selected` are both **zero** and the direct primary is created 9×. A warning on the import therefore fires every boot in the healthy configuration — noise, not signal.
- **Change**: (1) three distinct named counters for the three refusal reasons plus a rate-limited log for the two silent ones; (2) consume `info.dxgiFormat` instead of the literal 87, and either honour or explicitly refuse a non-zero `info.planeOffset`; (3) make entry into the COPY path loud — a one-time warning-level line plus a monotonic counter, so a silent switch away from the direct primary is visible in triage; (4) the per-present re-query is R417's negative cache — do not re-solve it here. Keep the fallback: it is a live safety net.
- **Static guarantee**: real, and it is the sealing this tranche can afford: make the direct scan-out resource and the LINEAR fallback alias **distinct Rust types** (`DirectPrimary` / `LinearCopyTarget`) instead of two `Option<ID3D11Resource>` fields (`device_funcs.rs:105` `scanout_import`, `:113` `composition_source`) on the same struct, so the present path can only accept the former and the fallback has to be an explicit, visible conversion. Today both are the same type selected by a boolean.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the KMD's scanout generation counter is still consumed as a bare `u32` with no validity typestate; a stale generation can be detected, not prevented.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit for the counters + field consumption inside `open_kmd_scanout_target`; the Rust-side type sealing is a second commit that has to move with R417's enum.
- **Risk**: low-medium — consuming `info.dxgiFormat` changes the alias format if the ICD ever reports something other than 87; refuse anything not in the `28|87|88` scan-out set rather than passing it through blind.
- **Validation**: on the current stack the new COPY-entry counter must stay 0 across a DWM boot while the desktop is visible in the VNC screenshot and `ScanoutDiag` is absent; the three refusal counters tell you for the first time whether the query is failing every frame. Force the fallback once (mismatch the direct allocation deliberately) to prove the counters move and the copy path still produces a visible desktop.

### R419. Move the noop-stub and table-audit I/O behind trace_enabled and make the hit counters per-slot

- **Finding**: u-core-16.
- **Where**: `umd/src/device_funcs.rs:281-292` (`ddi_noop_device`), `:294-306` (`ddi_noop_dxgi`), `:266-279` (`log_backtrace`: 32 frames, formatted), `:355-404` and `:406-463` (the two auditors: per-slot log lines plus the `value < 0x0000_0001_0000_0000` heuristic), `umd/src/lib.rs:992-1011` (`log_line`: global `Mutex<File>`, unbuffered `writeln!`).
- **Today**: `ddi_noop_device` does a heap-allocating `format!` plus an unbuffered write under a process-global mutex from inside the runtime's call, and the very first hit additionally captures and formats 32 stack frames with `RtlCaptureStackBackTrace` — none of it behind `trace_enabled()`, unlike the rest of the repeat traffic. The counter is process-global rather than per-slot, so 512 hits of one slot hide every other slot's first hit, defeating the stated purpose of driving noop hit counts to zero (ROADMAP WS3). Corrected headline figure: `ddi_noop_device` does **not** occupy ~130 slots — diffing the assigned names against the generated `D3DWDDM1_3DDI_DEVICEFUNCS` field list leaves exactly **11** noop slots (`pfnCreateDeferredContext`, `pfnCreateCommandList`, `pfnDestroyCommandList`, `pfnAbandonCommandList`, `pfnCommandListExecute`, `pfnRecycleCommandList`, `pfnRecycleCreateCommandList`, `pfnRecycleCreateDeferredContext`, `pfnRecycleDestroyCommandList`, `pfnAssignDebugBinary`, `pfnDynamicConstantBufferMapNoOverwrite`), ten of which are unreachable while THREADING caps = 0 and `AssignDebugBinarySupport` = 0 — the single ungated per-frame slot is the one R403 fixes. `ddi_noop_dxgi` is unreachable altogether: `install_dxgi`/`install_dxgi_1_1`/`install_dxgi_1_3` overwrite all 7/8/18 slots of every DXGI table (verified by name diff against the generated structs). The auditors add a full-table scan with per-slot log lines on every fill and classify any slot value below `0x1_0000_0000` as "suspicious", which is an ASLR assumption rather than a fact.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: an app maps a dynamic constant buffer with `WRITE_NO_OVERWRITE` on a `>=11.1` device -> every one of the first 512 maps takes the global log mutex and writes to disk from inside the runtime's call (on top of the corruption R403 fixes) -> measured frame time regresses and the log obscures which other slots were ever hit.
- **Change**: keep a per-slot `AtomicU32` hit counter (an array indexed by slot, sized at table-fill time) and log only the first hit per slot, gated on `trace_enabled()`. Replace the `< 0x1_0000_0000` heuristic with an exact comparison against the two known stub addresses, which the auditor already has in scope. Leave `ddi_noop_dxgi`'s **deletion** to T6 (it is proven-dead code, and T6 owns deletions) but add a one-line comment recording the proof so the next reader does not re-derive it.
- **Static guarantee**: partial. Giving the stub table a real type (`struct NoopSlot { index: u16 }` generated per slot) makes "which DDI was it" answerable by construction instead of by a backtrace, and R403 is the payoff case for the fuller version: a table-shape descriptor that requires every slot of the negotiated table to be classified (real handler | intentionally-noop-with-reason | calc stub) makes "a writer DDI silently left on the uniform stub" unrepresentable. The substantive part of *this* commit is moving I/O off the call and making counters per-slot.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: commit 1 — gate the noop and audit logging on `trace_enabled()` (pure telemetry). Commit 2 — per-slot counters + exact stub-address comparison in the auditors.
- **Risk**: low.
- **Validation**: with `UmdTrace` absent, `umd-<pid>.log` contains no `DDI noop` or `suspicious slot` lines and the DComp probe fps is >= today's ~63 fps; with `UmdTrace=1` the same slots are reported as before, with per-slot first-hit lines replacing the global sequence.

### R420. Move the UMD's per-op log lines behind trace_line! and replace the 33 ad-hoc throttles with one type

- **Finding**: x-dup-dead-26, merges u-forward-a-11.
- **Where**: `umd/src/forward.rs:4598-4638` (`log_draw_state`; the throttle is `:4606-4608`, the 21-argument `format!` is `:4614-4637`), `:4642`, `:4655`, `:4676`, `:4703`, `:4724`, `:4736`, `:4769` (all seven draw entry points), `umd/src/lib.rs:992-1011` (`log_line`), `:1013-1018` (the `UmdTrace` doc that already prescribes the split), `:1312-1321` (`trace_line!`, which does not evaluate its arguments when tracing is off); the throttle escapes on the *unconditional* writer: `forward.rs:3006` (`resource_copy`, `|| dst_alloc != 0 || src_alloc != 0`), `:4438` (`set_render_targets`, `|| rt0.0 != 0`), `:4997` (`create_srv`, `|| allocation != 0`), `:5957` (`resource_update_subresource`, `|| alloc != 0`); `:3181` (`resource_map`) has the same escape shape but is already inside `trace_line!`.
- **Today**: `log_draw_state` runs from all seven draw variants. For the first 1024 draws it performs a heap-allocating 21-argument `format!` plus a mutex-guarded unbuffered file write; after that it still does so on every 1024th draw forever, and pays an atomic `fetch_add` on every draw. It uses `log_line`, not the `UmdTrace`-gated `trace_line!`, so the knob documented as covering "known-hot repeat traffic" does not cover the hottest path in the driver. Measured counts in `forward.rs`: **267** `log_line` versus **27** `trace_line!` call sites, and **33 distinct** `*_LOG_COUNT` throttle statics across **102** references, each an independently tuned magic threshold (`n < 8`, `< 16`, `< 32`, `< 64`, `< 128`, `< 256`, `< 512`, `< 1024`, `n % 512`, `n % 600`, `n % 1024`) — and four of those budgets are defeated outright by an `|| <handle> != 0` disjunct that removes the cap for exactly the WDDM-allocation-backed resources that are touched most often.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a — cost. A game issuing 2000 draws per frame at 60 fps performs ~120 file writes per second from the draw path after warm-up, and 1024 back-to-back writes during the first frames, which is exactly the startup window where idle-to-active latency is measured.
- **CORRECTED ON HARDWARE 2026-07-27 (T2 implementation):** step (2) as written is not implementable. "Instantiated per site with the site's current numbers so no site's cadence changes" assumes one static per site, but **eleven of the 37 statics are SHARED by sites with different budgets** — `SHADER_BIND_LOG_COUNT` is used with both `< 128` and `< 256`, `MPO_LOG_COUNT` with `< 16`, `< 64` and `< 128`, `VIEW_LOG_COUNT` with `< 128` and `< 256`, `RASTER_LOG_COUNT` with `< 64` and `< 128`, `DRAW_LOG_COUNT` with `< 2048` and a `% 1024` shape. Giving each site its own counter changes the cadence at every one of them, which is the one thing the item forbids. As implemented, `LogThrottle` owns the counter (shared exactly as today) and the budget is a CALL argument, with three methods because `n % every` and `(n + 1) % every` are different cadences. Cadence identity was verified by dumping the pre-change (static, threshold, phase) triple for all 69 sites and diffing it against the post-change call arguments.
- **Change**: (1) convert `log_draw_state` and every other per-op site to `trace_line!` so `UmdTrace=0` makes them free — the macro already avoids evaluating its arguments, so the `format!` and the `dev.ia.borrow()` both disappear. (2) Replace the 33 ad-hoc statics with `struct LogThrottle { count: AtomicUsize, first: usize, every: usize }` and `fn should_log(&self) -> bool`, instantiated per site with the site's current numbers so no site's cadence changes. (3) Keep `log_line` unconditional only for errors, one-shots and refusals, exactly as `lib.rs:1015-1017` already prescribes. `trace_enabled()` already exists, so this does **not** depend on the knob-reader dedup (u-core-06, T7).
- **Static guarantee**: real if `trace_line!` becomes the only path that can format a per-op message — narrow `log_line`'s signature to an error/one-shot form (or introduce `log_error!`) so a per-op site cannot reach the unconditional writer by accident.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: three commits — draw/dispatch/map/copy paths first (highest value, smallest diff), then the view/state setters, then the `LogThrottle` type. **Prerequisite, corrected 2026-07-26:** an earlier draft made this "confirm with the owner which triage recipes grep these lines". That was overstated and asked a person for something the repo answers. Use R406's method instead — grep `tools/`, `*.ps1`, `*.md`, `*.py`, `*.sh` for each line's text before converting it. Verified result at the time of writing: **nothing automated reads a UMD log line.** The only line a documented procedure depends on is `present-gate:`, which is emitted from `dxvk_bridge.cpp` (C++, prefix `[dxvk-bridge]`) and is NOT in this item's scope; `res_id=` is a grep target flagged by a separate item (the T4b field rename), also not converted here. The residual judgement — whether the four escape-clause sites should keep firing unconditionally for allocation-backed resources — is a one-line question for the owner, not a blocker: `UmdTrace=1` restores every converted line, and step (3) keeps errors, one-shots and refusals unconditional by construction.
- **Risk**: medium — not to the driver, to triage. A recipe that silently stops matching is worse than a slow log.
- **Validation**: per the stage charter, before/after numbers: `UmdTrace=0` log-file growth per minute at an idle desktop and during a Fire Strike run (target: no growth from per-op lines), DComp cadence near 63 fps, and a 3DMark or dxvk-tests frame time. Then confirm with `UmdTrace` absent that the UMD log still records every error line, and with `UmdTrace=1` that each converted site prints the same text at the same cadence as before.

### R421. Compute UpdateSubresource's pixel probes inside the log gate

- **Finding**: u-forward-b-09.
- **Where**: `umd/src/forward.rs:5924-5955` (`resource_summary`, `resource_parent_handles` and the two `read_unaligned` probes, all unconditional; the probe block is `:5939-5955`), `:5956-5987` (the gate `n < 1024 || alloc != 0` and the 21-argument log with two `String` allocations), `umd/src/lib.rs:992-1011` (`log_line`).
- **Today**: the two `read_unaligned` probes — plus `resource_summary` and `resource_parent_handles` — are computed unconditionally, so every BGRA/RGBA tex2d update pays two dependent cache misses into the caller's buffer purely to produce a log field. The gate's `alloc != 0` disjunct then removes the rate cap for exactly the shared/primary/present resources that update most often, so a steady stream of updates to a WDDM-allocated texture writes one 21-argument formatted line, plus two `String` allocations, per call through the unconditional mutex-serialised writer.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a.
- **Change**: two commits. (a) Behaviour-preserving: move `source_samples` (and, if convenient, the summary and parent-handle reads) inside the log gate so the common path pays nothing; the emitted fields stay identical. (b) Declared diagnostic change: change the gate to `n < 1024 || (alloc != 0 && n % 512 == 0)` so allocation-backed updates stay observable without being unbounded, and count the suppressed ones. Do not bundle (b) into (a).
- **Static guarantee**: `none - a rate limiter is a runtime construct`. The `LogBudget`/`LogThrottle` helper from R420 removes the copy-paste at ~30 sites but encodes no invariant; the runtime check that stays is the gate itself, which is correct once the expensive operands live inside it.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the probe reads at `(h/2)*row_pitch + (w/2)*4` inside a buffer whose size is only implied by the caller's box; that trust survives, but it is at least no longer paid on every call.
- **Atomic boundary**: commit (a) touches only `resource_update_subresource`'s prologue; commit (b) touches the gate and adds the counter. Lands after R420's throttle type if you want (b) expressed through it.
- **Risk**: low.
- **Validation**: identical log lines for the first 1024 updates after (a); measure an UpdateSubresource-heavy workload (3DMark) frame time before/after, per the measure-before-optimizing rule.

### Minor items

Low-severity items, compressed. Each is a real defect or a real cost, but small enough that the full template would be padding.

### R422. Bound the DXBC total-size dword before building a shader slice
- **Where**: `umd/src/forward.rs:3467-3485` (`shader_code_len`: the DXBC arm returns `*code.add(6)` unbounded and reads dword 6 before knowing the container size, while the SHDR arm bounds the token count to `1 << 20` dwords); the ten consumers that build the slice are `:3528`, `:3566`, `:3800`, `:3899`, `:3940` (this one reads `a.pShaderCode`, not `code`), `:3988`, `:4029`, `:4070`, `:4111`, `:4153`.
- **Change**: bound the DXBC arm the same way the SHDR arm is bounded — require at least the 32-byte container header and at most `1 << 20` dwords, log and return 0 on rejection (every caller already handles `len == 0` with an explicit failure log). Behaviour changes only for blobs that are already corrupt. The `ShaderBytes<'a>` validated-slice type that would remove all ten `from_raw_parts` sites belongs with the handle work in T5; do not block the bound on it.
- **Validation**: all shader creates still succeed under DWM and 3DMark; the new rejection log must never fire (the DDI contract hands the driver raw SHDR/SHEX token streams, so the DXBC arm is a defensive branch with no demonstrated source for a bad size).

### R423. Bounds-check isgn_lookup's name offset so a malformed container cannot panic the draw path
- **Where**: `umd/src/forward.rs:7389-7429` (`isgn_lookup`; the unchecked `nstart = data + name_off` and `&dxbc[nstart..nend]` are `:7417-7422` — `&v[a..a]` with `a > len` is out of bounds in Rust, and every *other* offset in the function is checked); the only caller is `bind_input_layout` at `:7615-7634`, gated on `is_dxbc`.
- **Change**: add `if nstart >= dxbc.len() { return None; }` before the scan, as its own commit under the never-panic-in-a-DDI invariant. Do **not** also change the "name runs to the end of the blob without a NUL" case in the same commit — today `CString::new` succeeds on the tail bytes and a layout is still built, so tightening that is a separate behaviour change. Reachability is narrow: d3d11.dll strips the container before the UMD sees bytecode, so `is_dxbc` is true only for blobs Helios produced itself (the in-process selftests' `D3DCompile` output at `:6944` and `:7156`).
- **Validation**: new host-target unit test asserting `isgn_lookup` returns `None` (no panic) for a `name_off` past the chunk; `selftest_triangle` still returns 0. **NOT ADDABLE IN T2 (2026-07-27):** `umd` is `crate-type = ["cdylib"]`, so `cargo test` has no lib target; adding `rlib` makes the harness fail to link because `build.rs` passes the DXVK static archives through `cargo:rustc-link-arg-cdylib`, and this cargo rejects `rustc-link-arg-tests` as an invalid instruction. Switching to a plain `rustc-link-arg` would change the SHIPPING cdylib's link line. A host-testable UMD crate (the analogue of T0's `kmd_logic`) does not exist; creating one is a T8-shaped file split. The bounds check itself is landed.

### R424. Widen the signature-word length check before adding, and bound each entry count
- **Where**: `umd/bridge/dxvk_bridge.cpp:1483` (`sig_words_len != 2 + std::size_t(n_in + n_out) * kSigEntryWords` — the sum is evaluated in `std::uint32_t` and only then widened), `:1542` (the same with three addends), `:605` (`const std::uint32_t entries_size = count * 24u;`, a u32 multiply), `:613-618` and `:636-668` (the indexing that depends on that check being sound).
- **Change**: `std::size_t(n_in) + std::size_t(n_out)` (and the three-addend form), plus an explicit upper bound on each count — D3D11 has at most 32 input/output registers per stage, so a few hundred is generous — with a named refusal counter; same for the 24-byte entry size in `append_signature_chunk`. Not reachable today: the Rust caller `flatten_stage_io_signatures` (`forward.rs:3587-3628`) derives both counts and the vector from the same runtime arrays, so a wrap would need a 2^32-entry allocation first. This is hardening of the only bounds check standing between caller-supplied counts and the indexing.
- **Validation**: dump wrapped bytecode for the full shader set before and after with `ShaderBytecodeDumpPath`; the `.dxbc` files must be bit-identical, and the new refusal counter must stay 0 through a DWM boot plus dxvk-tests.

### R425. Give the wedge watchdog the same alive-checked fence read that signalTo uses
- **Where**: `umd/bridge/dxvk_bridge.cpp:2042-2047` (the watchdog reads `*ctx->cpuVa` with neither the mutex nor an `alive` check) versus `:963-974` (`signalTo`: `lock_guard`, `if (!alive || !signal) return;`, then reads `*cpuVa`), `:866-879` (the comment claiming `alive` "fences every touch of the runtime callback after device teardown"), `:1021-1033` (the destructor's set-alive / set-stop / join sequence that is the only thing keeping the mapping valid), `:2043` (the 250 ms sleep the join must wait out).
- **Change**: add `std::optional<std::uint64_t> HeliosFlipWaitCtx::readFenceValue()` that takes the mutex, checks `alive` and returns the value; route both readers through it and exit the watchdog loop on `nullopt`. Precisely: the mutex does not protect the mapping's *contents* (kernel-written, read through a volatile pointer) — it protects `alive`/`signal`/`hFence`, and the missing `alive` test is the real gap. Optionally replace the 250 ms sleep with a condition-variable wait on `stop`; that **is** a behaviour change (it removes up to 250 ms from `DestroyDevice`'s join) and must be stated, not smuggled in. Not constructible today — the join runs inside `DestroyDevice` while the mapping is still live — so this is hardening against the watchdog ever being detached or the join being moved.
- **Validation**: the `flip-kwait WEDGE:` path still fires when provoked (stall the copy chain; the unwedge counter increments and the line appears), and teardown still completes: destroy a vehicle device with no hang, no new counter movement, and a measurably shorter `DestroyDevice` if the cv change is taken.

- **Where**: `umd/bridge/dxvk_bridge.cpp:397-406` (`umd_log_file`: a lazy `static char path[MAX_PATH]` guarded by `if (path[0] == 0)` — an unsynchronised write to shared storage), `:408-420` (`umd_log`: `_fsopen` + `fprintf` + `fclose` per line), `:422-436` (`shader_bytecode_dump_path`, a correct magic static in the same anonymous namespace — the file contradicts itself), and the unconditional per-create call sites `:1069-1074`, `:1113-1123`, `:1160-1167`, `:1188-1194`, `:1238-1244`, `:1327-1333`, `:1378-1382` (seven, not the three originally cited: `open_ddi_texture2d` and `create_ddi_scanout_texture2d` each log twice).

- **Where**: `umd/src/forward.rs:8483-8486` (`maybe_log_present_readback` opens with an uncached `std::env::var_os("HELIOS_PRESENT_READBACK")`), `:8672-8675` (`maybe_force_present_alpha_opaque`, same shape), `:9132-9133` (both called on every present), `:9238-9242` (`env_flag("HELIOS_PRESENT_OPTIMIZE_COMPOSITION")`, a third lookup per present), `:153-155` (`env_flag` is uncached `var_os`), `umd/src/lib.rs:1127-1310` (every registry knob uses `OnceLock`); the fourth lookup at `:9337` is **inside** the `ordinal < 64 || (ordinal + 1) % 512 == 0` gate at `:9327` and is paid only on logged frames — leave it or route it through the same accessor.

### R430. Fix RotateSample's three unchecked assumptions and report skipped slots
- **Where**: `umd/bridge/dxvk_bridge.cpp:1681-1691` (the `RotateSample` registry gate; `s_sampleEvery` stays 0 when the key is absent, so the block is not entered — this is off by default and is not a live cost), `:1704-1712` (`sd = td` then `sd.MipLevels = 1; sd.ArraySize = 1;`, overriding the source desc), `:1713-1718` (`CreateTexture2D` -> `CopyResource` -> `Map` -> `base = map.pData` with no null check), `:1720-1732` (rows reinterpreted as `const std::uint32_t*`, i.e. 32bpp assumed), `:1609-1620` (the comment recording the two rejected drain designs at 15-25 ms and up to 1.9 s — which this instrument reintroduces when enabled).
- **Change**: null-check `map.pData`; copy `MipLevels`/`ArraySize` from the source desc instead of forcing 1 and skip the slot (counted) when the source is not a single-subresource 32bpp texture; name the skipped slots in the log line so an all-zero report cannot be confused with a skipped copy. Two of the assumptions are actively misleading: with `ArraySize > 1` the descriptions mismatch, `CopyResource` is a silent no-op and the tool reports `nonzero=0/N` — the exact false conclusion ("the composition draws write nothing") it exists to test for; and with a 16bpp ring the 4-byte column stride reads past the last row, so it is a potential OOB read, not merely a wrong number.
- **Validation**: with `RotateSample` unset the block is not entered at all (verifiable: `s_sampleEvery` stays 0), so behaviour is unchanged. With it set to 1, the `rotate-sample:` lines must still report non-zero pixel counts for a composited desktop — the instrument's own ground truth — and any skipped slot must say so.
