## T3 - Encode the display/scanout invariants: programming guard, lock tokens, validated descriptors

This tranche turns the display half's hand-maintained contracts into types: the two PASSIVE mutexes hand out proof
tokens the way `WddmNotifyGuard` already does, `WddmNotifyGuard` starts branding its own adapter and owning the
transport borrow, the `vidpn_programming` gate becomes one RAII interval instead of nine `store(0)` sites plus a DPC
clear, `apply_vidpn_source_address_locked` collapses to a single exit returning `Result<ProgrammedPrimary,
ScanoutReject>` with a counter per refusal class and a retry contract, `ScanoutInfo` splits into a Windows-supplied
identity and a validated scan-out target, scan-out format identity collapses to one enum, the async scanout notify can
only be attached to the ring that honours it, `StartDevice`/`StopDevice` stop forming `&mut AdapterContext` while three
concurrent agents hold `&AdapterContext` to the same object, and the VidPn mode-set acquire/release pairs become guards.
It sits after T1a/T1b because k-display-01 and k-display-03 must fix the two live gate leaks by hand first - the RAII
guard would otherwise silently fix them and destroy their before/after evidence - and because the refusal-counter work
assumes T1b's counter conventions. It does NOT change the direct-primary path's shape (no guest primary-to-scanout copy
is introduced), does NOT touch the Venus wire-fence watermark refresh marker or its lock order, does NOT touch the UMD,
does NOT rename or repurpose any existing registry knob, counter or breadcrumb value, and does NOT delete the
`ScanoutDiag` knob (that is an owner decision recorded elsewhere in the plan).

### R501. Hand out a scanout-lifecycle proof token instead of documenting the lock in prose

- **Finding**: x-ordering-05 (with k-display-09 and k-lifecycle-06 commits 1-2 folded).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:1067-1087` (`with_scanout_lifecycle`), `:428-448` (`WddmNotifyGuard`, the
  in-tree pattern to mirror), `:736-743` (`queue_active_scanout_refresh` / `_locked`), `:1094-1160`
  (`retire_scanout_allocation`), `:1162-1178` (`with_venus_client`), `:1029-1042` (`init_kernel_events`, where the
  "distinct lock order ... never hold this while acquiring it recursively" prose lives);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:885` and `:900` (the two acquire sites), `:905`
  (`apply_vidpn_source_address_locked`), `:61-146` (`production_linear_scanout`);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/create_allocation.rs:466-473` (`submit_primary_scanout_copy`), `:744` (the retire call from
  `destroy_allocation_ctx`); `kmd_render/src/ddi/hpd.rs:146`.
- **Today**: `scanout_mutex` is a `SynchronizationEvent` initialised signaled (`adapter.rs:1036`) used as a
  non-recursive mutex through an infinite non-alertable `KeWaitForSingleObject` (`:1074-1082`). The whole contract -
  hold it before the venus mutex before the virtio spinlock, never re-enter, PASSIVE only - is a doc comment. The
  `_locked` suffix on `queue_active_scanout_refresh_locked` and `apply_vidpn_source_address_locked` is the only marker,
  and the helpers those functions call (`production_linear_scanout`, `submit_primary_scanout_copy`) are `pub(crate)`
  and callable from anywhere. Defect class: a single new call to `queue_active_scanout_refresh()` or
  `retire_scanout_allocation()` from inside an already-locked closure is a permanent PASSIVE self-deadlock of the HPD
  worker - no bugcheck, no counter, the desktop just stops. Verified there is no such recursion today, and the
  documented order does hold (`display.rs:885` -> `:961` -> `:95` `with_venus_client`).
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `adapter.with_scanout_lifecycle(|| adapter.retire_scanout_allocation(h, rid))` -
  exactly what a DestroyAllocation-during-SetVidPn refactor would write - compiles and wedges the HPD worker forever on
  `KeWaitForSingleObject`.
- **Change**: add `pub(crate) struct ScanoutGuard<'a> { adapter: &'a AdapterContext, _not_send: PhantomData<*const ()> }`
  next to `WddmNotifyGuard` in `adapter.rs` (private fields, no `Copy`/`Clone`). Change
  `with_scanout_lifecycle<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&ScanoutGuard<'_>) -> R) -> R`. Give `&ScanoutGuard<'_>` as a
  parameter to `queue_active_scanout_refresh_locked`, `apply_vidpn_source_address_locked`, `production_linear_scanout`
  and `submit_primary_scanout_copy`, and extract the 59-line closure body at `adapter.rs:1101-1159` into
  `retire_scanout_allocation_locked(&self, lock: &ScanoutGuard<'_>, ..)`. Add
  `ScanoutGuard::with_venus_client(&self, f) -> Result<R, DriverError>` forwarding to `AdapterContext::with_venus_client`,
  and use it at the two venus sites reached under the lock (`display.rs:95`, `create_allocation.rs:498`).
  Two corrections to the finding's proposal: (a) `crate::virtio::ctrl::set_scanout_blob` must NOT take the token - it
  has seven call sites and five of them (`ctrl.rs:779`, `scanout_diag.rs:267/325/459/516`) run outside the lock;
  (b) `AdapterContext::with_venus_client` must stay public - eleven of its thirteen callers
  (`create_allocation.rs:757/776/818/826/941/977/1017`, `display.rs:460`, `scanout_diag.rs:364/449`) legitimately hold
  no scanout lock. `request_scanout_refresh` (`adapter.rs:579`) stays token-free: it is deliberately callable from
  inside the lock (`:1156`) and from DISPATCH (`interrupt.rs:45/61`, `submit_command.rs:332/459`).
- **Static guarantee**: a caller that does not hold the lock cannot manufacture a `ScanoutGuard`, so "call only under
  `scanout_mutex`" becomes a signature rather than a suffix, and the scanout->venus order gets one enforced path.
  `PhantomData<*const ()>` makes the guard `!Send`, documenting that the guarded work never crosses threads. It does
  NOT make recursion unrepresentable - the guard is handed to the very closure that could call the re-acquiring
  wrapper - so keep the "callers must not invoke it recursively" note, now on the guard type, and if recursion
  detection is actually wanted it has to be a debug-only owner-thread field, not a type.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the PASSIVE-only IRQL precondition; stable Rust cannot type an IRQL, so the existing runtime
  `KeGetCurrentIrql` checks stay where they are. A `VenusGuard`-mediated `with_virtio` is deliberately NOT proposed:
  `with_virtio` has 92 call sites, so encoding venus-before-virtio that way would rewrite most of the transport for a
  guarantee the frozen baseline already gets from the two-site venus surface.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit. The generated critical sections are byte-identical; the diff is signatures plus one
  function extraction.
- **Risk**: medium - the `retire_scanout_allocation` extraction moves 59 lines containing the DestroyAllocation cancel
  CAS and the re-arm at `:1155-1157`; a transcription error there is a scanout-lifetime bug, so diff it line by line.
- **Validation**: `RfCnt` (`adapter.rs:873`) keeps advancing and `ScSet`/`ScFlu`/`ScRet` keep the same values across a
  DWM session with window churn (which drives DestroyAllocation against a live scanout); `ScDead` stays absent; no
  HPD-worker stall (if the worker wedges, `RfCnt` freezes while `VsCnt` keeps climbing - that pair is the diagnostic).

### R502. Brand `WddmNotifyGuard` with its adapter and make it the only path to the notify-ordered transport methods

- **Finding**: k-lifecycle-05 (with k-gputransport-06 folded).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:428-448` (`WddmNotifyGuard`), `:1224-1234` (`with_wddm_notify_lock`),
  `:1259-1275` (`with_virtio`); `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:1713-1716` (`note_scanout_refresh` and the over-claiming
  doc at `:1710-1712`), `:1730-1733` (`take_ready_scanout_refresh`), `:1771-1778` (`note_wddm_submission`),
  `:1820-1824` (`take_ready_wddm`), `:1850` (`preempt_flush`); call sites `kmd_render/src/ddi/interrupt.rs:42` and
  `:54`, `kmd_render/src/ddi/submit_command.rs:319`, `:455`, `:561`, `:581`,
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/scheduler.rs:117`.
- **Today**: the guard is genuinely unforgeable (private `adapter` field, no `Copy`/`Clone`, constructed only at
  `adapter.rs:1230`), so "the notify lock is held somewhere" is proven. But all five consumers name the parameter
  `_notify_guard` and never read it, and `gpu.rs:1710-1712` claims the token makes "the lock order (`wddm_notify`
  before `virtio`) part of the type contract". It does not: the guard carries no relationship to the `&mut VirtioGpu`
  being mutated. Defect class: a type that claims more than it delivers - reviewers stop checking. Correction to the
  finding: there are **seven** guard-scoped `with_virtio` sites in three files, not six (`interrupt.rs` x2,
  `submit_command.rs` x4, `scheduler.rs` x1); `submit_command.rs:221` takes the notify lock but calls no transport
  method and is not converted.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `adapter_a.with_wddm_notify_lock(|g| adapter_b.with_virtio(|v| v.note_wddm_submission(g, ..)))`
  compiles and mutates B's fence FIFO under A's lock. Symmetrically, `adapter.with_virtio(|_| adapter.with_wddm_notify_lock(|_| ()))`
  compiles and takes the two (different) spinlocks in the inverse of the documented order; run concurrently with the
  normal order on another CPU that is an AB-BA hang at DISPATCH_LEVEL with no bugcheck attributable to it. This is a
  lock-order inversion, not a self-deadlock - the two are separate `KSPIN_LOCK`s and nesting them is legal.
- **Change**: add `impl WddmNotifyGuard<'_> { pub(crate) fn with_virtio<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&NotifyOrdered<'_>, &mut VirtioGpu) -> R) -> Result<R, DriverError> }`
  that forwards to `self.adapter.with_virtio`, plus `pub(crate) struct NotifyOrdered<'a>` (private field, no
  `Copy`/`Clone`) mintable only inside that method. Change the five `gpu.rs` methods' first parameter from
  `&WddmNotifyGuard<'_>` to `&NotifyOrdered<'_>` and rename it from `_notify_guard` to `_order` (it stays unread - the
  point is that it cannot be obtained any other way). Convert the seven call sites to
  `guard.with_virtio(|o, v| v.method(o, ..))`. Keep `AdapterContext::with_virtio` public for the other 85 sites. Fix
  the doc at `gpu.rs:1710-1712` to state what is now true. Binding negative constraint from k-gputransport-06: do NOT
  introduce a combined `with_notify_then_virtio` holding both locks for one closure - `interrupt.rs:40-76`
  deliberately makes two separate `with_virtio` calls inside one notify scope and runs `request_scanout_refresh()`
  (`:45`, `:61`) and `signal_dma_completed_locked()` (`:66-72`, which raises to the device DIRQL via
  `DxgkCbSynchronizeExecution`) between them; folding those into one transport critical section would change frame-path
  timing.
- **Static guarantee**: adapter identity becomes structural (the same `&self` mints both borrows, so the
  cross-adapter call stops compiling), and notify-before-virtio becomes structural for these five methods (a
  `NotifyOrdered` exists only inside a notify critical section, and the `with_virtio` closure never receives an
  `&AdapterContext`, so it cannot re-enter the notify lock). Honest gap: a caller already holding `virtio_lock` that
  calls `guard.with_virtio` recursively acquires it and self-deadlocks; Rust cannot see that, so it stays a comment.
- **Remaining unsafe**: `wddm_notify_lock` is still a raw `UnsafeCell<KSPIN_LOCK>`, and the closure's "no waits, no
  allocation, no pageable code at DISPATCH" obligation is not encodable without an IRQL effect system.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit - pure signature churn, identical generated critical sections and lock durations.
  Do not fold multiple `with_virtio` calls into one while converting.
- **Risk**: low. The failure mode this lock exists to prevent is bugcheck 0x119/1 (invalid fence id) and the
  DMA_PREEMPTED one-fence-leap; if a conversion accidentally widens or drops a critical section that resurfaces.
- **Validation**: run the existing GDI/paging + DWM soak: `DmStl`, `WfDone`, `SaCnt` unchanged, fence monotonicity
  intact, no 0x119 bugcheck, `IrqN`/`DpcN` still advancing at the same rate.

### R503. Collapse scan-out format identity into one `ScanoutFormat` enum

- **Finding**: k-display-10 (with x-dup-dead-V02 folded).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:52-59` (`virtio_scanout_format`), `:109` (function-local
  `const DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM: u32 = 87`), `:118` and `:137` (the two uses of it), `:959`
  (`matches!(source.dxgi_format, 28 | 87 | 88)`), `:990-994` (conversion + `ScFmt` refusal);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/create_allocation.rs:486-496` (three more local consts and a three-way `!=` chain gating the
  copy path, `CpFmt` refusal).
- **Today**: the same three-value fact is spelled four times with bare DXGI integers, and the converter and the
  direct-scanout allowlist already disagree about format 0 (accepted by the converter, rejected by the validator).
  Corrections to the finding: `scanout_diag.rs:26-32` is **not** a fourth DXGI mapping - `scanout_format(mode)` is
  keyed on the *diag mode* and returns a virtio constant directly (five call sites: `:166`, `:209`, `:298`, `:457`,
  `:514`); and `create_allocation.rs:243-251` (`resolved_dxgi_format`) plus `venus.rs:581-594`
  (`PresentPixelFormat::from_dxgi`) answer different questions (D3DDDIFMT->DXGI, and the wider render-side set) and
  must NOT be merged in. Defect class: a format addition made in three of four places surfaces as an opaque
  `ScSet=0xE3` or `ScFmt` trace.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a - the converter's `0 =>` arm has no reachable producer (a direct-scanout primary
  always carries the UMD's exact DXGI format from the same private-data record, and the LINEAR arm's format is the
  hard-coded 87 at `display.rs:118`/`:137`), so the disagreement is latent drift, not a reachable state.
- **Change**: add `pub(crate) enum ScanoutFormat { Bgrx8, Bgra8, Rgba8 }` with `from_dxgi(u32) -> Option<Self>`,
  `virtio(self) -> u32` and `dxgi(self) -> u32`, defined once (`create_allocation.rs` next to `ScanoutInfo`, or the
  new host-buildable logic crate from T0 so it can be unit-tested). Rewrite `virtio_scanout_format`, the `:959`
  allowlist (becomes `ScanoutFormat::from_dxgi(source.dxgi_format).is_some()` - or better, the parsed value threaded
  forward per R507), the two `:118`/`:137` uses of the local const, and the `create_allocation.rs:486-496` copy gate.
  `scanout_diag`'s mode selector may consume `ScanoutFormat::Bgrx8.virtio()` / `Bgra8.virtio()` but keeps its own
  mode-keyed shape. Keep the `0 -> Bgrx8` mapping exactly as today; deleting it is a separate, counter-backed commit.
- **Static guarantee**: one total function converts DXGI to the wire format, so the acceptance set and the conversion
  set cannot drift, and (once R507 threads the parsed value) a format that passes the gate but has no virtio encoding
  becomes unrepresentable instead of failing at the last step.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit.
- **Risk**: low - only that a transcription slip changes which formats are accepted.
- **Validation**: host-target unit test over `{0, 28, 87, 88, 10, 24, 91, 93, other}` asserting the exact same
  mapping as the four current sites; on hardware `ScSet=1` with `ScFmt` and `CpFmt` absent through a normal DWM boot,
  and `ScPub`/`ScRid` unchanged.

### R504. Replace the nine `vidpn_programming` clear sites with one RAII `ProgrammingInterval`

- **Finding**: k-display-02 (with x-ordering-01 folded).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:863` (the single set site), `:869-870` (the bare `irql != 0`),
  `:905-1101` (`apply_vidpn_source_address_locked`, whose nine `store(0)` sites are at `918`, `943`, `962`, `971`,
  `992`, `1019`, `1063`, `1070`, `1096`), `:1077-1100` (the fallback arm that returns SUCCESS with the gate still
  raised); `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:1439` (the asynchronous clear through `NonNull<AtomicU32>`);
  `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:329-334` (the field and its contract); `kmd_render/src/ddi/start_device.rs:309-314` (the
  VSync consumer); `kmd_render/src/ddi/build_paging_buffer.rs:109` and
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/cpu_host_aperture.rs:96` (the two existing module-local `const PASSIVE_LEVEL_IRQL: u8 = 0`).
- **Today**: the gate is raised at exactly one place and lowered at nine hand-written sites inside a 196-line function
  plus one asynchronous site in the used-ring DPC. Every future early return in that function is a potential permanent
  display stop: `vsync_dpc_routine` returns at `start_device.rs:309` on every tick while the gate is set, so no
  CRTC_VSYNC is delivered and dxgkrnl never retires the queued flip. k-display-01 and k-display-03 (T1a) are two exits
  that already got this wrong. The IRQL split is comment-only: `irql != 0` compares against a bare literal while two
  other modules in this crate already name the same constant.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: any new `return` added between `display.rs:915` and `:1100` that omits the
  `store(0)` compiles and silently disables the VSync heartbeat for the rest of the boot; recovery is only partial
  (the DPC's `pending_vidpn_allocation != 0` branch at `:310` signals the HPD worker, so it needs a *subsequent*
  SetVidPnSourceAddress to re-publish a pending handle).
- **Change**: add `#[must_use] pub(crate) struct ProgrammingInterval<'a> { gate: &'a AtomicU32, _not_send: PhantomData<*const ()> }`
  to `adapter.rs` with `ProgrammingInterval::adopt(&adapter.vidpn_programming)`, a `Drop` that stores 0 `Release`, and
  `fn transfer_to_completion(self)` that `core::mem::forget`s it. The token is *adopted* at the top of
  `apply_vidpn_source_address_locked`, not constructed at the set site: the raise happens in the DIRQL DDI and the
  lower happens in the worker's call stack, so a token cannot span the deferral without becoming a flag again. Delete
  all nine `store(0)` lines; the fallback arm calls `transfer_to_completion()` on the `Ok(fence)` branch at
  `display.rs:1087-1092` (the `Err` branch just drops). Separately, hoist one crate-level
  `const PASSIVE_LEVEL_IRQL: u8 = 0` (do NOT assume `wdk-sys` emits `PASSIVE_LEVEL` - it is a C macro), centralising
  the two module-local copies and replacing `display.rs:870`; and split the DDI into
  `set_vidpn_source_address_dirql` (atomics only, `display.rs:840-875`) and the PASSIVE continuation so the two halves
  cannot be mixed by accident. Ordering is preserved: every arm records its diag value before lowering the gate today,
  and a drop at end of scope keeps that order; the same-resource success arm stores `last_primary_address`
  (`:1058-1060`) before the clear, which the drop also preserves.
- **Static guarantee**: inside `apply_vidpn_source_address_locked` the nine exits collapse into one compiler-inserted
  drop, so "cleared on every path" is a property of the function, and the single legitimate hand-off to the completion
  DPC becomes one greppable `transfer_to_completion()` call instead of an absence. `#[must_use]` plus the private field
  stop the token being ignored or stored; `PhantomData<*const ()>` keeps it `!Send`. It canNOT express the
  DIRQL-set/PASSIVE-clear split, and it canNOT cover the DestroyAllocation cancel path - k-display-01's clear (T1a)
  stays an explicit, counter-backed hand-off.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the transfer crosses into a raw `NonNull<AtomicU32>` held by the transport
  (`ctrl.rs:1469`, cleared at `gpu.rs:1439`), so the compiler cannot prove the DPC ever runs. A lost completion still
  leaves the gate raised; that residual keeps a named counter (R509 turns it into a detectable mismatch).
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit. It MUST land after T1a's k-display-01 and k-display-03, or the refactor silently
  fixes two live bugs and destroys the before/after evidence for both. Note in the commit message that
  T1a's k-lifecycle-V01 reset touches `vidpn_programming` too and will be touched again by R509.
- **Risk**: medium - a mis-placed `transfer_to_completion()` on the fallback arm either strands the gate (display
  stops) or clears it too early (a CRTC_VSYNC reports the old address mid-programming). The fallback arm is the one
  the direct-primary baseline never executes, so it needs a forced-fallback build to exercise.
- **Validation**: `VpDSt`, `ScSet`, `ScRid`, `ScFlu`, `ScCpy` sequences identical over a fixed 60 s desktop session
  before and after; `VsCnt` (`adapter.rs:898`) advancing at the same ~60/s rate; force each refusal exit in a
  scratch build and confirm the gate reads 0 afterwards (`VsCnt` keeps moving) in all of them.

### R505. Give the deferred programming path one exit, a reject enum, and a counter per refusal class

- **Finding**: k-display-12 (BUG - observability half; folds the `ScUnav` counter requested by the unassigned
  k-display-05).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:915-920` (unresolvable `hAllocation` -> `ScRid=0` -> `STATUS_SUCCESS`, no
  counter), `:869-875` (the DIRQL path already returned SUCCESS before any of this runs), `:892-894` (`VpDSt`: one
  overwritten DWORD for every deferred failure), `:942`, `:961`, `:970`, `:991`, `:1018`, `:1069`, `:1095` (the seven
  post-resolution refusal classes, each a single overwritten `record_named_bytes`);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/hpd.rs:153-155` (the `Unavailable` arm: a comment, no counter);
  `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:864-892` (the existing ~10 s telemetry tick that the new counters flush from).
- **Today**: three swallow sites. (1) An `hAllocation` that does not resolve returns `STATUS_SUCCESS` with no counter -
  the OS believes the primary was programmed and the only trace, `ScRid=0`, is overwritten by the next successful bind.
  (2) When the DDI ran at DIRQL the return value is already SUCCESS, so every later failure (extent `0xD`, invalid
  direct layout `0xE3`, unsupported format `ScFmt`, LINEAR allocation `0xE1`, `SET_SCANOUT_BLOB` `0xE`, missing target
  image `0xE2`, copy submit `ScCpy=0xE`) is visible only as `VpDSt`, a single overwritten DWORD - no per-class counter,
  which violates the project's loud-failure rule. (3) `hpd.rs:155` drops the dirty bit on
  `ScanoutRefreshQueue::Unavailable` silently.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: Windows names a primary the KMD cannot resolve -> the DDI returns SUCCESS ->
  dxgkrnl believes the flip was programmed against a scanout that was never programmed -> the next
  SetVidPnSourceAddress overwrites `ScRid`, so post-mortem cannot tell the failure happened at all.
- **Change**: add `enum ScanoutReject { BadAlloc, Extent, Layout, Format(u32), LinearAllocFailed, SetFailed, NoTarget, CopyFailed }`
  with `fn record(self)` reproducing today's exact (name, value) pairs - `BadAlloc` -> `ScRid=0`, `Extent` ->
  `ScSet=0xD`, `Layout` -> `ScSet=0xE3`, `Format(f)` -> `ScFmt=f`, `LinearAllocFailed` -> `ScSet=0xE1`, `SetFailed` ->
  `ScSet=0xE`, `NoTarget` -> `ScSet=0xE2`, `CopyFailed` -> `ScCpy=0xE` - and `fn counter(self) -> &'static AtomicU32`
  naming eight new saturating statics (`ScBadAlc`, `ScBadExt`, `ScBadLay`, `ScBadFmt`, `ScLinErr`, `ScSetErr`,
  `ScNoTgt`, `ScCpyErr`; all <= 14 chars for `record_named_bytes`). Convert
  `apply_vidpn_source_address_locked` into an inner `fn ... -> Result<ProgrammedPrimary, ScanoutReject>` (the Ok type
  arrives in R506; until then `Result<(), ScanoutReject>`) plus a thin outer wrapper that does
  `record()` + `counter().fetch_add(1)` + maps to today's NTSTATUS. Add `ScUnav` for `hpd.rs:155`. Flush all nine from
  the existing `n == 1 || (n % 600) == 0` block at `adapter.rs:870-892` - a PASSIVE site inside the same lock - never
  from the refusal path itself (a registry write per refusal would be the exact per-frame tax T1b is removing
  elsewhere). Keep `STATUS_SUCCESS` for `BadAlloc`: returning `STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER` there is a separate,
  hardware-proven decision, not part of this commit.
- **Static guarantee**: with one exit typed `Result<_, ScanoutReject>`, "every refusal is recorded and counted" is
  enforced by construction - the only way to leave the function unhappily is to produce a variant, and the variant
  owns both its breadcrumb and its counter. Adding a refusal without a counter stops compiling.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit, immediately after R504 - both rewrite the same 196-line body, so the body is
  rewritten once. R504 first, because the reject enum's single exit is what makes the RAII drop point unambiguous.
- **Risk**: low - the risk is a mis-mapped (name, value) pair changing a breadcrumb the owner debugs with. Diff the
  eight pairs against the seven current sites plus `:917` by hand.
- **Validation**: all nine new counters read 0 across a clean 10-minute desktop session (proving no silent refusals
  today) while `ScSet`/`VpDSt`/`ScRid` keep their current values; then force one refusal (a bogus mode) in a scratch
  build and confirm the matching counter moves *this boot* (registry counters persist across boots - verify movement,
  not presence).

### R506. Make a failed deferred programming publish no address and re-enter a bounded retry

- **Finding**: k-display-V01 (BUG - forward-progress half; behaviour-changing).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:869-875` (DIRQL path returns SUCCESS before programming),
  `:941-945`, `:960-964`, `:969-974`, `:990-994`, `:1017-1021`, `:1067-1072`, `:1094-1098` (the seven failure exits,
  none of which touches `last_primary_address`), `:1058-1060` and `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:1432-1437` (the only
  two publishers, both success-only), `:884-895` and `kmd_render/src/ddi/hpd.rs:143` (the worker consumes the pending
  handle once, with no retry), `kmd_render/src/ddi/start_device.rs:315-320` (the DPC reports
  `last_primary_address` as the display engine's authoritative state), `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:317-322` (the
  field's documented contract), `:1106-1113` (the DestroyAllocation cancel CAS that makes a re-arm safe).
- **Today**: on the DIRQL-deferred path the OS is told SUCCESS before any programming happens. Every failure exit then
  clears the gate, records one overwritten value, and returns - without updating `last_primary_address` and without
  re-arming the pending handle (the worker's swap at `:886` already zeroed it). Since `last_primary_address` is
  precisely what the CRTC_VSYNC packet carries, the heartbeat keeps reporting the previously displayed address forever:
  the flip queued for the failed primary can never retire, dxgkrnl stops issuing new source addresses, and the desktop
  freezes with two overwritten DWORDs as the only trace. Defect class: a failure that is indistinguishable from a
  hang. The freeze is derived from the driver's own documented model (`adapter.rs:317-322`,
  `start_device.rs:304-320`), not from a hardware observation - say so in the commit message.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `SetVidPnSourceAddress(A)` at DIRQL -> SUCCESS returned, gate=1, pending=A -> worker
  swaps A out and calls the continuation -> `production_linear_scanout` fails (`CpErr=1`) -> `ScSet=0xE1`, gate=0,
  `VpDSt=<status>`, pending already 0 -> nothing ever retries A -> every subsequent CRTC_VSYNC reports the OLD
  address -> dxgkrnl never retires A's flip -> no further `SetVidPnSourceAddress` -> frozen desktop.
- **Change**: type the success path as `struct ProgrammedPrimary { address: u64 }`, constructible only after
  `SET_SCANOUT_BLOB` has succeeded for that exact source, and make it the only argument of a new
  `AdapterContext::publish_displayed_primary(&self, p: ProgrammedPrimary)` that performs the
  `last_primary_address.store(.., Release)` at `display.rs:1058-1060`. Add `ScanoutReject::retryable(self) -> bool` -
  true for `LinearAllocFailed`, `SetFailed`, `NoTarget`, `CopyFailed` (transport/allocation failures), false for
  `BadAlloc`, `Extent`, `Layout`, `Format` (validation rejects that will never succeed for that allocation). Give the
  retry policy to the single caller, `process_deferred_vidpn_source_address` (`display.rs:884-895`): on a retryable
  reject it restores `pending_vidpn_allocation` to that exact handle, keeps the programming interval raised via a new
  `ProgrammingInterval::retain_for_retry(self)` (a second `mem::forget` disposition, distinctly named from
  `transfer_to_completion`), and returns - the VSync DPC's `pending_vidpn_allocation != 0` branch
  (`start_device.rs:310-312`) then signals the worker, which is the existing wake path. Bound it with a per-interval
  attempt budget plus two named counters (`ScRetry`, `ScGaveUp`); on exhaustion drop the interval (gate clears,
  VSync resumes with the truthful old address) and count loudly. Never publish `source.primary_address` on a failed
  bind. The re-arm is safe against DestroyAllocation because it happens inside `with_scanout_lifecycle`, the same lock
  that `retire_scanout_allocation`'s cancel CAS (`adapter.rs:1106-1113`) and the worker's swap (`display.rs:886`)
  hold - state that in the SAFETY comment.
- **Static guarantee**: "a failed programming publishes no address" becomes a property of the signature - there is no
  value other than a `ProgrammedPrimary` from which a publication can be made, and the failure type cannot produce
  one. Partial, honestly: `last_primary_address` must stay `pub(crate)` because `ctrl.rs:1468` takes a `NonNull` to it
  for the DPC, so the field can still be stored to directly from within the crate; the guarantee covers the KMD-side
  publication, and R509 gives the DPC side its own ticket check. The retry budget stays a runtime counter.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none beyond the existing raw-handle deref in `scanout_alloc_info`.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit on top of R505 (same function, same enum, same single exit). Retry classification
  must be explicit per variant - no blanket `retryable()`.
- **Risk**: medium - a retryable reject that is actually permanent burns the budget every VSync tick (bounded, but it
  holds the gate and therefore suppresses CRTC_VSYNC for the duration); pick a budget of a few attempts, not hundreds,
  and verify `VsCnt` keeps advancing during a forced-failure run.
- **Validation**: with R505's counters in place all reject counters read 0 over a clean session; then force a
  retryable failure (exhaust the Venus LINEAR allocation) in a scratch build and confirm `ScRetry` moves, `SaCnt`
  (`adapter.rs:902`) keeps advancing, `VsCnt` keeps advancing, and the desktop recovers instead of freezing with a
  fixed `SaLo`/`SaHi` pair; then force a permanent reject and confirm `ScGaveUp` moves once and the gate clears.

### R507. Split `ScanoutInfo` into a Windows-supplied identity and a validated scan-out target

- **Finding**: k-display-11.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/create_allocation.rs:305-328` (`ScanoutInfo`, all fields `pub`), `:361-383`
  (`scanout_alloc_info`, the only Windows-sourced constructor), `:466-473` and `:477-496`
  (`submit_primary_scanout_copy`, which re-derefs the handle and re-checks geometry/format itself);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:79-92` and `:132-145` (the two `ScanoutInfo` literals whose `primary_*` fields are
  zeros), `:941-945` (extent check), `:951-964` (pitch/offset/size/format checks, direct arm only), `:980-984` (the
  pitch substitution that runs *after* those checks), `:1058-1060` and `:1084` (both read `source.primary_address`,
  never `target`'s).
- **Today**: one type carries two unrelated things - the geometry/layout of some scan-out surface, and the
  Windows-supplied `PrimarySegment`/`PrimaryAddress`/`Flags` identity of a specific `hAllocation`.
  `production_linear_scanout` returns a value whose `primary_*` fields are meaningless zeros (twice), and
  `apply_vidpn_source_address_locked` then juggles `source` and `target`, whose fields are valid in different subsets.
  Correctness rests on the author remembering to read the address from `source`. Validation is likewise scattered
  across three places, with the pitch fallback applied after the checks that would have used it. Defect class: a
  partially-initialised descriptor whose invalid combinations are representable.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: latent, not present today - an edit that writes
  `adapter.last_primary_address.store(target.primary_address, ..)` compiles and publishes 0 as the displayed address,
  making the flip unretirable; and a `ScanoutInfo` built by `production_linear_scanout` can be passed anywhere a
  Windows-supplied one is expected.
- **Change**: two types in `create_allocation.rs`. `WindowsPrimary { alloc: HANDLE, segment: u32, address: u64, flags: u32, resource_id: u32, extent, pitch, plane_offset, venus_alloc_size, memory_type_index, dxgi_format, direct_scanout }`
  produced only by `scanout_alloc_info`; and `ScanoutTarget { resource_id, width, height, pitch, plane_offset, venus_alloc_size, memory_type_index, format: ScanoutFormat }`
  with private fields and exactly two constructors returning `Result<Self, ScanoutReject>`:
  `ScanoutTarget::from_direct_primary(&WindowsPrimary)` (running today's `:955-959` checks verbatim, then the
  `:980-984` pitch resolution) and `ScanoutTarget::adapter_linear(..)` (the LINEAR path, same pitch resolution so the
  behaviour is identical on both arms even though the LINEAR pitch is never 0). `apply_vidpn_source_address_locked`
  then reads the address from `WindowsPrimary` and the layout from `ScanoutTarget`; the extent check at `:941-945`
  stays in the caller because it compares against `display_mode()`, not against the allocation. Change
  `submit_primary_scanout_copy` to take `&WindowsPrimary` instead of `(h, primary_address)`. The `direct_scanout` bool
  disappears from the target - the arm is the constructor - but keep it on `WindowsPrimary`, since `:1026` still
  branches on it to decide whether to publish the fallback cache.
- **Static guarantee**: a validated descriptor downstream code cannot partially initialise: no public fields,
  constructors return `Result`, the zeroed `primary_*` fields become unrepresentable, and the primary address lives on
  a type the fallback path cannot construct. This is the "validate format/extent/pitch/offset/size once" guarantee.
  Real but it fixes no live bug (nothing publishes `target.primary_address` today and the fallback pitch is never 0).
- **Remaining unsafe**: `scanout_alloc_info` still dereferences a dxgkrnl-supplied `HANDLE` guarded only by
  `ALLOCATION_CTX_MAGIC`; dxgkrnl owns that handle's validity, so the check stays a runtime one.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit, after R503 (the constructors take a `ScanoutFormat`) and after R505/R506 (the
  constructors return `ScanoutReject`, and the body has already been rewritten once). Do not attempt it before them -
  three findings rewrite the same 196 lines and the body must be rewritten once.
- **Risk**: medium - the direct-arm checks are the guard that keeps QEMU from reading past a blob (the undersize-guard
  lesson from the 38th session); move them verbatim, do not "simplify" the saturating arithmetic at `:952-958`.
- **Validation**: the `ScSet` error codes `0xD`, `0xE3`, `0xE1`, `0xE`, `0xE2` must be emitted for exactly the same
  inputs - drive a resolution change and a DWM restart and diff the `Sc*` sequence against a pre-refactor boot;
  `ScPch` must still read 7680 (not `width*4`) for the 1896-wide primary; host-target unit tests for both constructors
  over the pitch/offset/size/format matrix.

### R508. Make the async scanout notify constructible only for the ring that honours it

- **Finding**: k-gputransport-08.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:1204-1212` (`enqueue_async_submit`: independent `ring_idx: u32` and
  `scanout_notify: Option<AsyncScanoutNotify>`), `:1426-1443` (the drain's `if ring_idx == 1 { if let Some(notify) }`),
  `:531-542` (`AsyncScanoutNotify`: `derive(Clone, Copy)`, four `NonNull` fields plus `primary_address`);
  `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:1466-1479` (the sole notify construction, ring 1 hard-coded at `:1478`), `:1423` and
  `:1508` (the other two `enqueue_async_submit` sites, both `None`);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/start_device.rs:309-314` (VSync suppressed while the gate is set).
- **Today**: the ring and the notify are independent parameters but the drain only honours a notify on ring 1. A
  notify attached to any other ring is silently discarded at completion - no counter, no error - and because
  `gpu.rs:1439` is the ONLY clear of `vidpn_programming` on the copied-primary path, that leaves the gate at 1 and the
  VSync path refuses to sample `last_primary_address` indefinitely. Verified not live: the only construction
  hard-codes ring 1, and `display.rs:1094-1098` does clear the gate when the enqueue itself fails. Defect class: a
  representable-invalid-state in a transport API whose misuse is a silent display stop.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `enqueue_async_submit(ctx, 0, meta, venus, len, Some(notify))` - the signature
  permits it, no caller does it - completes through the `ring_idx != 1` path, the notify is dropped,
  `vidpn_programming` stays 1, `start_device.rs:309` suppresses every further CRTC_VSYNC, and no counter names the
  cause.
- **Change**: split the entry point. Keep `enqueue_async_submit(ctx_id, ring_idx, meta, venus, venus_len)` with no
  notify parameter (callers `ctrl.rs:1423`, `:1508`), and add
  `enqueue_scanout_submit(ctx_id, meta, venus, venus_len, notify: ScanoutNotify)` which hard-codes `ring_idx = 1`
  internally; the `InFlightKind::AsyncVenus` drain arm keeps its `ring_idx == 1` test but the notify now lives in a
  variant that only that entry point can create. Make the notify constructible only by the adapter:
  `AdapterContext::scanout_notify(&self, primary_address: u64) -> ScanoutNotify`, so the four pointers always come
  from the same adapter and cannot be mixed. Deliberate deviation from the finding's proposal: do NOT relocate the
  four fields into a `#[repr(C)] ScanoutNotifyBlock` embedded in `AdapterContext` - `scanout_refresh_pending`,
  `last_primary_address`, `vidpn_programming` and `hpd_event` have readers all over the crate (`hpd.rs:98/128/145/151`,
  `adapter.rs:542-543/1148`, `start_device.rs:309/315`, plus T1a's k-lifecycle-V01 reset list), and nesting them would
  turn a transport-API fix into a crate-wide rename. The single-construction-site rule buys the same same-adapter
  guarantee at a fraction of the blast radius. Preserve exactly: the store order at `gpu.rs:1432-1440`
  (`displayed_primary`, then `pending`, both `Release`, then `programming = 0`, then `KeSetEvent`) and the asymmetry
  that `displayed_primary`/`pending` are stored only when `response_ok` while `programming` is cleared unconditionally.
- **Static guarantee**: the ring becomes an implicit property of the entry point, so the `(ring, notify)` mismatch
  leaves the type space entirely, and the notify's four raw pointers get one construction site instead of being
  assemblable field by field. What remains unencodable is the self-referential lifetime: `VirtioGpu` lives inside the
  `AdapterContext` it points back into.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the four `NonNull`s' validity rests on the adapter outliving the transport, which
  `StopDevice` enforces by ordering (`set_virtio(None)` after cancel/join at `start_device.rs:345-368`), and on
  `init_kernel_events` having run before any `KeSetEvent` on `hpd_event`. Both stay comment-level, documented once on
  `ScanoutNotify` instead of on four fields.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit - `gpu.rs` (the split entry point + the in-flight variant), `ctrl.rs` (the three
  async submit helpers: `submit_venus_async`, `submit_venus_async_scanout`, `submit_venus_async_present`),
  `adapter.rs` (the constructor). Land after R504 so the `transfer_to_completion()` hand-off already exists and the
  two changes to the same hand-off are not interleaved.
- **Risk**: medium - this is the frame-path enqueue; an accidental change to the `Release` store order or to the
  `response_ok` asymmetry breaks the VNC sampling contract (host samples ahead of the copy).
- **Validation**: `ScSet`/`ScCpy`/`ScFlu` breadcrumbs and `ScanoutDiag` absence unchanged;
  `RING_SUBMIT_COUNT == RING_COMPLETE_COUNT` still tracks (`AsSub`/`AsDone`); the exact-primary path still takes the
  direct branch at `display.rs:1045` (`ScCpy=2`, `ScFlu=3`); steady-state DComp cadence unmoved near 63 fps.

### R509. Tag the programming gate with a generation so a stale completion cannot clear a newer interval

- **Finding**: k-display-18 (behaviour-changing; low severity - reachable only on the non-direct fallback path).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:1432-1439` (unconditional `programming.store(0)` plus the
  `displayed_primary` store, with no interval identity), `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:1466-1474` (the notify built
  from raw `NonNull`s), `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:1077-1100` (the fallback arm returns SUCCESS with the gate
  still raised, handing it to the DPC), `:863-875` (a DIRQL `SetVidPnSourceAddress` re-raises the gate without taking
  `scanout_mutex`), `kmd_render/src/ddi/start_device.rs:309-320` (the DPC's gate read and the address it reports),
  `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:329-333` (the contract this violates).
- **Today**: nothing identifies which programming interval a completion belongs to. Because the DIRQL half takes no
  lock, a second call can raise the gate for interval N+1 while copy N is still outstanding; copy N's completion then
  clears the gate belonging to N+1, and the next CRTC_VSYNC reports addr(N) while N+1 is still being programmed -
  exactly the state `adapter.rs:329-333` documents as forbidden. Consequence, stated precisely: addr(N) is truthful
  for what the host is scanning out, so dxgkrnl retires N rather than the wrong flip; what breaks is the gate's
  no-stale-report contract, and one flip's completion is signalled early relative to the newer queued flip.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: copy(N) queued on ring 1 with the gate still raised (`display.rs:1100` returns
  SUCCESS without clearing) -> `SetVidPnSourceAddress(N+1)` at DIRQL sets the gate again and stores pending=B, taking
  no lock -> copy(N) completes, stores displayed=addr(N) and clears the gate -> the next VSync DPC passes the gate and
  reports addr(N) although N+1's programming has not run.
- **Change**: widen `vidpn_programming` to `AtomicU64` holding `(seq << 32) | active`, so "raise" and "clear only my
  interval" are single atomic operations rather than two independent stores. The DIRQL raise at `display.rs:863`
  becomes a bounded CAS loop that increments `seq` and sets `active` in one publication (a CAS loop is legal at DIRQL:
  bounded, no allocation, no callbacks). `ProgrammingInterval` (R504) carries its `ProgrammingTicket(u32)` = the seq it
  adopted; both its `Drop` and the DPC's clear become `compare_exchange((seq,1) -> (seq,0))`, and a mismatch
  increments a named counter (`ScStale`) instead of silently clobbering. `ScanoutNotify` (R508) carries the ticket by
  value rather than only a pointer to the gate. `start_device.rs:309` reads the low half.
- **Static guarantee**: pairing the flag with its generation in one word makes "clear the gate that is not mine"
  unrepresentable as a single store - the only clear API takes a ticket. The ticket itself is a value, so a stale
  ticket is detectable rather than impossible; that is the honest limit, hence the counter.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the notify still holds a raw pointer into the adapter; its validity rests on the adapter
  outliving the transport, which `StopDevice`'s ordering enforces and the type system cannot express across the
  C-style in-flight table.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit spanning `adapter.rs` (field type + ticket), `display.rs` (raise + interval),
  `ctrl.rs` (notify), `gpu.rs` (completion), `start_device.rs` (DPC read). Land after R504 and R508. Note in the
  commit message that this is the second touch of T1a's k-lifecycle-V01 reset (which stores 0 into this field) and
  that the same packed word is what keeps k-display-01's cancel-side clear race-free - design them consistently.
- **Risk**: medium - the field is read by the DIRQL DDI, the DISPATCH VSync DPC, the used-ring DPC and the PASSIVE
  worker. An `AtomicU64` is fine on x64, but every reader must be converted; a missed reader compares a packed word
  against 0/1 and either suppresses VSync forever or never suppresses it.
- **Validation**: `ScStale` stays 0 on a normal boot (proving the interleave does not occur today); `VsCnt` cadence
  and `VpDSt`/`ScSet` sequences unchanged; in a forced-fallback (non-direct) session `SaLo`/`SaHi` track the newest
  primary; host-target unit test for the pack/unpack and the CAS transitions.

### R510. Stop forming `&mut AdapterContext` in StartDevice/StopDevice

- **Finding**: k-lifecycle-04 (BUG - `&mut` aliasing UB plus an unguarded torn-read window).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/start_device.rs:117` (the `&mut` from the already-published pointer), `:120` (the
  bulk `DXGKRNL_INTERFACE` store), `:126-133` (knobs), `:135-137` (`paging_ram`), `:170` (`bar_segment`, via
  `setup_bar_segment(&mut ..)` at `:49-51`, which writes `bar_probe_ram`), `:184-186`/`:203-205`/`:212-214`
  (`venus_ctx_id`, `page_table_window`), `:245-256` (`display_w`/`display_h`, `edid`), `:553-574`
  (`QueryDeviceDescriptor`, the EDID's only reader), `:265`/`:272` (`init_vsync`,
  `init_hpd`), `:336`/`:353-354`/`:369` (StopDevice's `&mut` and its three plain-field clears);
  `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:420-426` (the stale `Send`/`Sync` justification);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/interrupt.rs:98-99` (`&AdapterContext` at DIRQL), `:152` (the device DPC reads
  `adapter.dxgkrnl` with NO `isr_status` guard); `kmd_render/src/ddi/start_device.rs:297`/`:301` (the VSync DPC does
  the same); `kmd_render/src/ddi/hpd.rs:59` (the worker builds `&AdapterContext` from the same pointer).
- **Today**: the context pointer is public to dxgkrnl from AddDevice onward and three concurrent agents build
  `&AdapterContext` from it, yet StartDevice takes a unique `&mut` that stays live for the whole function and mutates
  ~a dozen plain fields through it - including `dxgkrnl`, a multi-hundred-byte callback struct read lock-free by the
  ISR and both DPCs. Two distinct defects: (1) `init_vsync()` at `:265` arms a 16 ms timer and `init_hpd()` at `:272`
  starts a thread that both immediately take `&self` from the same address while the outer `&mut` is still in scope,
  and `set_virtio(Some(gpu))` at `:164` enables the device so the DIRQL ISR can fire mid-function - an unambiguous
  Stacked-Borrows violation; (2) the `dxgkrnl` store is non-atomic and the ordering that makes it safe ("a nonzero
  `isr_status` implies a valid callback table", `interrupt.rs:85-88`) is statement order plus a comment, and it covers
  only the ISR - `interrupt.rs:152` and `start_device.rs:301` read `adapter.dxgkrnl` with no `isr_status` guard at all.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: AddDevice publishes the pointer -> StartDevice takes `&mut` ->
  `set_virtio(Some(gpu))` enables the device -> the host pushes a used-ring entry -> the DIRQL ISR builds
  `&AdapterContext` from the same pointer and reads `adapter.dxgkrnl` while the `&mut` is live; later in the same call
  the timer DPC and the HPD worker do the same.
- **Change**: never form `&mut AdapterContext`. Move the post-start-only plain fields into
  `struct StartedState` stored as `started: UnsafeCell<Option<StartedState>>`, published once with a single `Release`
  store, and reached through `AdapterContext::started() -> Option<&StartedState>`. StartedState splits by lifetime:
  the *sticky* half (`dxgkrnl`, `gdi_accel_mode`, `alloc_cached`, `present_probe`, `display_half`,
  `display_w`/`display_h`, `edid`, `paging_ram`, `bar_probe_ram`) and an inner
  `Option<TransportGeneration>` (`page_table_window`, `venus_ctx_id`, `bar_segment`) that StopDevice clears. PRESERVE
  current post-stop behaviour exactly: StopDevice today does NOT clear the knobs, the mode or the EDID, and about two
  dozen sites branch on `display_half` (`display.rs:661/678/690-692/706/736/755/771/788/821/833/1109/1125/1170`,
  `interrupt.rs:183`, `start_device.rs:236/245/298/431/505/542/596`, `create_allocation.rs:1213`,
  `scanout_diag.rs:140/479`, `adapter.rs:761`, `venus.rs:4886`), so clearing the sticky half at StopDevice would flip
  all of them from SUCCESS-shaped answers to NOT_SUPPORTED between StopDevice and RemoveDevice. Convert
  `setup_bar_segment` to take `&AdapterContext` and return `(BarSegment, Option<PagingRam>)` instead of writing
  `bar_probe_ram` through `&mut`. Update the `Send`/`Sync` justification at `adapter.rs:420-426` to name what is
  actually there now.
- **Static guarantee**: the typestate the brief asks for, without generics - `Added -> Started` becomes
  `Option<StartedState>`, and every accessor that needs a started adapter takes `&StartedState`. "Read `dxgkrnl`
  before StartDevice" stops compiling (there is no `StartedState` to borrow) and so does "mutate a started field from
  a DDI" (no `&mut` is reachable). Publishing the whole struct with one `Release` store makes the callback-table
  visibility ordering structural for all three readers, not just the ISR: a reader that has the state has the table,
  so the two unguarded reads at `interrupt.rs:152` and `start_device.rs:301` stop resting on statement order. A type
  parameter on `AdapterContext` is deliberately NOT proposed - dxgkrnl hands the pointer back untyped on every DDI, so
  it would be erased at the boundary and only relocate the cast.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the ISR reads the published slot at DIRQL without a lock, so the slot stays a raw
  `Release`/`Acquire` pointer publish inside an `UnsafeCell`; and `DXGKRNL_INTERFACE` remains a bindgen POD copied out
  of dxgkrnl's buffer.
- **Atomic boundary**: three ordered sub-commits, each preserving field values and call order. (1) `StartedState`
  with the trivially-copied knobs + mode + EDID + `paging_ram`/`bar_probe_ram`, built and published once by
  StartDevice; `setup_bar_segment` converted. (2) `dxgkrnl` and `isr_status` move in, and the `&mut` disappears from
  StartDevice. (3) StopDevice's transport-side clears go through interior mutability, WITHOUT clearing the sticky
  members.
- **Risk**: medium - the blast radius is every `display_half` reader plus `query_adapter_info`'s segment reporting
  (which reads `bar_segment` and `paging_ram`). A slip that makes a display DDI answer NOT_SUPPORTED after StopDevice
  changes restart behaviour, which is exactly what the regression gate's restart-device leg tests.
- **Validation**: same-boot diag equivalence for `GdiM`, `AlcC`, `PBPrEn`, `DspH`, `DspMd`, `BarM`; `IrqN`/`DpcN`
  advance; the EDID served to `QueryDeviceDescriptor` is byte-identical (compare the `0x120E` length breadcrumb at
  `start_device.rs:574` and a guest monitor-EDID dump); `0x0B00_0007` still recorded (venus page-table window);
  desktop screenshot unchanged; and a `pnputil /restart-device` cycle in which the display DDIs answer the same way
  between StopDevice and the next StartDevice as they do today.

### R511. Fold AdapterContext's two-phase construction into one private constructor returning a pointer

- **Finding**: k-lifecycle-13.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/add_device.rs:26-29` (the unreachable `Err` arm) and `:33-39` (`Box::into_raw` then
  `init_kernel_events` at the final address); `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:459-529` (`new`, a single `Ok(Self { .. })`
  with no fallible operation), `:469`, `:480`, `:488`, `:489`, `:524` (five `core::mem::zeroed()` dispatcher
  placeholders - the finding says four but lists five: `scanout_mutex`, `venus_mutex`, `vsync_timer`, `vsync_dpc`,
  `hpd_event`), `:1029-1042` (`init_kernel_events`), `:972-1000` (`init_vsync`, which initialises the KDPC/KTIMER in
  place at StartDevice and requires `dxgkrnl` already saved).
- **Today**: `new` builds five self-referential kernel objects as zeroed placeholders, returns the whole context BY
  VALUE (so it is moved into the `Box`), and relies on a second `unsafe` call at the final address to write the real
  dispatcher headers. Nothing in the type system says that `init_kernel_events` must run before any DDI, that the
  context must never move afterwards, or that `init_vsync`/`init_hpd` need `dxgkrnl` first - all three are `# Safety`
  prose. If `init_kernel_events` were skipped, `with_venus_client` would `KeWaitForSingleObject` on a zeroed
  dispatcher header (typically an unrecoverable hang) with no diagnostic. Compounding it, `new`'s `Result` can never
  be `Err`, so `add_device.rs:28` is dead code.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `let ctx = AdapterContext::new(pdo)?; let boxed = Box::new(ctx); /* no init_kernel_events */ *out = Box::into_raw(boxed);`
  compiles and produces an adapter whose first `with_venus_client` waits on an uninitialised KEVENT. Equally,
  `let moved = *Box::from_raw(raw);` after init moves initialised, self-referential dispatcher objects.
- **Change**: add `pub(crate) fn create(pdo: PDEVICE_OBJECT) -> NonNull<AdapterContext>` that boxes, runs the
  in-place init and returns the raw pointer; make `new` and the struct literal private so no safe caller can obtain an
  `AdapterContext` by value. Drop the vestigial `Result` and delete `add_device.rs:27-29`. Keep the signature
  infallible rather than `Option`: `Box::new` is not fallible today, and an `Option` would imply an allocation-failure
  path that does not exist (if one is wanted later it is a `Box::try_new` change, not a signature change now). Add
  `PhantomPinned` only as a documentation marker if desired - do NOT claim it as the guarantee; `!Unpin` affects only
  the `Pin` APIs and does not stop `Box::new(ctx)` or `*Box::from_raw(raw)` from compiling.
- **Static guarantee**: encapsulation, and that is enough: folding the two phases into one private constructor makes
  the skip unrepresentable for safe callers, and returning only `NonNull` - never `Self` - is what makes the no-move
  invariant hold, because a caller who never obtains the value cannot move it. The `dxgkrnl`-before-`init_vsync`
  ordering becomes structural once `init_vsync` takes `&StartedState` from R510.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the in-place `KeInitializeEvent`/`KeInitializeDpc`/`KeInitializeTimerEx` calls and the
  AddDevice out-pointer write stay `unsafe`; neither is encodable.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit. Land after R510 (the state wants to live in `StartedState`). Deleting the
  now-callerless `DriverError::into_ntstatus` belongs to T6's k-lifecycle-15 - note in the commit message that
  `add_device.rs:28` was its only live caller (`error.rs:26-30` and `:33-38` are the other two references).
- **Risk**: low - same allocation, same init order, no runtime behaviour change.
- **Validation**: the `0x0A00_0001` / `0x0A00_0002` breadcrumbs still bracket AddDevice (DiagLevel=1); the adapter
  binds Code 0; `with_venus_client` still succeeds (`0x0B00_0007` recorded). Verified with `pnputil /restart-device`.

### R512. Make the scan-out mode and its EDID one validated value

- **Finding**: k-lifecycle-20.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:389-400` (`display_w`/`display_h` + `edid`, with the cofunctionality claim in
  the doc), `:626-638` (`display_mode`, with bare `>= 320` / `>= 240` literals);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/start_device.rs:250-256` (the only writers, then `build_edid(display_mode())`), `:553-574`
  (`QueryDeviceDescriptor` serves `adapter.edid`); consumers `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:921` (and the extent
  reject at `:941-945`, `ScSet=0xD`), `kmd_render/src/ddi/vidpn.rs:363` and `:444`,
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/scanout_diag.rs:144`.
- **Today**: the mode is two unvalidated `u32`s plus a 128-byte array, and their mutual consistency ("every VidPn mode
  + the generated EDID derive from this so they stay cofunctional") is a comment. The validation re-runs on every call
  through bare literals, and the EDID is generated once from the result. Verified that the raw fields are read ONLY
  inside `display_mode()` and written only at `start_device.rs:251-252`, and that the EDID has exactly one reader, so
  replacing them is behaviour-preserving - no caller loses access to the unvalidated pair. Defect class: a future
  write to `display_w`/`display_h` without regenerating the EDID produces a monitor whose detailed timing disagrees
  with the modes the VidPn DDIs enumerate - the mismatch class that produced the mode-set retry loops.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: any future assignment to `display_w`/`display_h` after StartDevice (nothing does
  today) leaves `edid` describing the previous mode; `QueryDeviceDescriptor` then serves a stale EDID while
  `EnumVidPnCofuncModality` enumerates the new one.
- **Change**: `struct DisplayMode { width: NonZeroU32, height: NonZeroU32 }` with
  `DisplayMode::from_host(w, h) -> Option<Self>` performing the minimum-size check once behind one named constant, and
  `struct ScanoutMode { mode: DisplayMode, edid: [u8; 128] }` whose only constructor generates the EDID from the mode
  via `vidpn::build_edid`. Store one `ScanoutMode` in R510's `StartedState`; `display_mode()` becomes a field read
  returning the same `(u32, u32)` tuple so the five consumers are untouched. Note for the implementer:
  `AdapterContext::display_mode()` and `VirtioGpu::display_mode()` (`start_device.rs:250`) are different methods with
  the same name - only the former moves.
- **Static guarantee**: the brief's constructor-validates-once shape - there is no way to obtain a `ScanoutMode`
  whose EDID disagrees with its extent, and no way to observe an unvalidated `(0, 0)` mode. Expressible in `no_std`
  with `NonZeroU32` and a fixed array; no alloc.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit, after R510 (the value lives in `StartedState`).
- **Risk**: low - the only hazard is a changed fallback threshold or a differently generated EDID.
- **Validation**: `DspMd` reports the same packed `(w << 16) | h`; the EDID bytes served to `QueryDeviceDescriptor`
  are byte-identical (compare the `0x120E` length breadcrumbs plus a guest-side EDID dump); the flip path's extent
  check still accepts the DWM primary (`ScSet=1`, no `0xD` refusals); host-target unit tests for `from_host` over
  `{(0,0), (320,240), (319,240), (1896,1066), host mode}` and for `build_edid`'s checksum.

### R513. Turn the VidPn mode-set acquire/release pairs into guards and the `fp` integers into a stage enum

- **Finding**: x-ordering-15 (the two-line leak fix itself is T1a's k-display-13 - land that first).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/vidpn.rs:505-712` (`enum_cofunc_modality`'s path loop), `:516-524`/`:585-593` (the
  four-callback tuples), `:556-571` (source: create at `:556`, add at `:561`, `fp = 15` releases at `:564`,
  `fp = 16` at `:567-571` does not), `:623-638` (target: the same shape, `fp = 25` at `:631`, `fp = 26` at
  `:634-638`), `:714-724` (the final cleanup, which releases only `path`), `:418-419` (the doc comment claiming
  otherwise), `:730-741` (the `VpECe`/`VpECf`/`VpECn` breadcrumbs the `fp` values feed).
- **Today**: the function acquires and releases four kinds of OS-owned objects with manual release calls at every one
  of eight numbered `fp` break sites, and the `fp` values are undocumented magic numbers used only as a registry
  breadcrumb. Two arms leak a created-but-unassigned mode set; the neighbouring `fp = 15`/`fp = 25` arms show the
  intended shape, which is what makes the omission clearly unintentional. Defect class: hand-matched ownership across
  a long error ladder, in a function that runs on every mode set and display-topology change.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `pfnAssignSourceModeSet` fails (the OS rejects our mode set) -> break to cleanup ->
  only `path` is released -> the created source mode set is orphaned, and the mode-set retry loop repeats it on each
  retry. (After T1a this is fixed by hand; the guard makes it unrepresentable.)
- **Change**: introduce `SourceModeSet<'a>`, `TargetModeSet<'a>`, `PathInfo<'a>` and `PinnedMode<'a>` in `vidpn.rs`,
  each owning both its handle and its interface reference, with a `Drop` that calls the matching
  `pfnRelease*`, and an `fn assign(self) -> NTSTATUS` that consumes the guard and `mem::forget`s it only on success
  (ownership has moved to the VidPn). Convert the two loops in `enum_cofunc_modality`; `commit_vidpn`'s
  acquire/release pair at `:844`/`:868` and its `PinnedMode` at `:852-864` convert too. Replace the `fp: u32` local
  with `enum CofuncStage` mapped to its existing numeric code in ONE place, so `VpECf` values stay byte-identical -
  10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 30, 31 and the three pre-loop values 1, 2, 3 at `:451`/`:467`/`:501`.
  Do not attempt to unify the source and target halves - the corresponding finding (k-display-14) was dropped.
- **Static guarantee**: RAII removes the possibility of a missed release, and a consuming `assign()` distinguishes
  "ownership handed to the OS" from "must release" at the type level; the guard also removes the
  `(h_set, set_iface)` pairing hazard, since the two can no longer be updated independently
  (`:550-556`, `:617-623` today reassign them as a pair by hand). The stage enum keeps the existing diagnostic values
  while making them exhaustive.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the OS interface pointers stay raw and valid only for the DDI call; the guards' lifetimes
  bound them (R514 makes that lifetime a real borrow).
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit for the guards + the stage enum. It must land after T1a's k-display-13 (the two
  missing `release_*` calls) so the leak fix keeps its own before/after evidence and this commit is provably
  behaviour-preserving.
- **Risk**: medium - a `Drop` that releases a set the OS already owns is a double-release into dxgkrnl; the consuming
  `assign()` is the only thing preventing it, so review every `assign` call site for an accidental `let _ =`.
- **Validation**: `VpECf` stays 0 and `VpECp >= 1` through a mode set; `VpECn` does not advance; display activates
  (`VpSA=1`, `ScSet=1`); repeated resolution changes do not grow the OS object count (drive ten changes and confirm
  `VpECe`/`VpECf` stay clean and the mode set still commits).

### R514. Give the dxgkrnl VidPn interface a real borrow instead of a doc-comment lifetime

- **Finding**: k-display-15 (hardening - no live defect).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/vidpn.rs:162-196` (`vidpn_interface` returns `*const DXGK_VIDPN_INTERFACE`, its
  lifetime stated only in the doc), and its three callers, each re-dereferencing with its own `unsafe { &* }`:
  `:447`+`:456` (`enum_cofunc_modality`), `:753`+`:757` (`topology_path_count`), `:807`+`:816` (`commit_vidpn`);
  `:525-533` and `:594-602` (`h_set`/`set_iface` as two independent locals, dereferenced separately as
  `unsafe { (*set_iface).pfnAcquirePinnedModeInfo }`).
- **Today**: the returned pointer is documented as "borrowed from dxgkrnl, valid for the duration of the DDI call"
  but carries no lifetime, so nothing stops it being stored on the adapter or returned upward, and each caller's
  SAFETY comment restates the assumption rather than establishing it. Correction to the finding: there are three
  callers, not four. Defect class: an unbounded raw pointer to a callback table whose validity window is a comment.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a today - the pinned-mode branches already release the mode info before the set
  (`:574-577`, `:640-643`) and the `(handle, interface)` pair is always reassigned together. This is hardening
  against an edit that stores the interface beyond the call or updates one half of the pair.
- **Change**: replace `vidpn_interface` with `VidPn::open(adapter, h_vidpn, _witness: &DXGKARG_*) -> Result<VidPn<'a>, NTSTATUS>`
  whose lifetime is derived from a borrow of the DDI argument struct the caller already holds (`&*arg` at `:442`,
  `:798`) - NOT `'static`, or the storage hazard returns. `topology_path_count` has no argument struct to borrow, so
  give it the caller's `&AdapterContext` borrow instead and document that it is the weaker of the two proxies.
  `VidPn<'a>` exposes the callbacks as safe field reads on a reference validated once at open, and the mode-set
  guards from R513 hold `&'a VidPn<'a>` so a set can never outlive its VidPn.
- **Static guarantee**: real but proxy-shaped, and worth stating as such: a lifetime derived from the DDI argument
  borrow prevents the interface reference from being stored on the adapter or returned upward, and collapses three
  `unsafe { &* }` sites into one per acquisition. It does not prove dxgkrnl's own validity window - it substitutes a
  Rust-checkable proxy for an unprovable contract.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the initial conversion of the dxgkrnl out-pointer to a reference (non-null and valid for the
  call), now once per acquisition instead of at every use.
- **Atomic boundary**: one commit, after R513 (the mode-set guards are what the `VidPn` borrow parents). No DDI
  signatures change.
- **Risk**: medium - lifetime plumbing through three DDIs; if a borrow is made `'static` to make it compile, the
  guarantee is gone and the item is worse than not doing it. Reject any such shortcut in review.
- **Validation**: identical `VpEC`, `VpECp`, `VpECf`, `VpMM`, `VpCP`, `VpCN`, `VpCW` traces across a mode change and
  a DWM restart - the change is purely how the same pointers are held.

### R515. Replace the HPD prologue's 500 ms stand-in wait and swap the config-change bit before indicating

- **Finding**: k-display-16 (two defects; (b) is a one-line behaviour fix).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/hpd.rs:61-75` (the 500 ms wait on `hpd_event` standing in for "StartDevice has
  returned"), `:76-80` (the stop check), `:81-84` (indicate, then an unconditional `store(0)`), `:135` (the
  steady-state path, which correctly uses `swap`), `:99-108` (the two bounded timeouts that are NOT this defect: the
  4 ms lost-interrupt fallback at `:101` and the 16 ms retry at `:104`);
  `kmd_render/src/adapter.rs:1041` (`hpd_event` is a `SynchronizationEvent`, so a racing signal is consumed by the
  next satisfied wait); `kmd_render/src/ddi/start_device.rs:265-272` (`init_vsync` then `init_hpd` at the end of
  StartDevice).
- **Today**: (a) the prologue's 500 ms relative wait is a delay standing in for an event - nothing observes that
  StartDevice returned. The early wake is deliberate and documented at `:63`, so the defect is the missing real edge,
  not the shortened wait. (b) After indicating, the worker unconditionally stores 0 into `config_change_pending`
  instead of swapping it *before* the indication; an ISR that sets the bit between `:81` and `:84` has it discarded,
  and because the event is auto-reset the next wait is satisfied by the stale signal and the swap at `:135` returns 0.
  The lost item is one `Connected=1` re-indication (the indication carries no mode or EDID data - both are latched at
  StartDevice), it is confined to the one-shot prologue window, and the steady-state loop is already correct - hence
  low severity.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `VIRTIO_GPU_EVENT_DISPLAY` fires while the prologue's `indicate_child_status` call
  is in flight -> the ISR sets `config_change_pending=1` and the DPC signals `hpd_event` -> the worker stores 0 at
  `:84` -> the loop's first wait is satisfied immediately by the stale signal, swaps 0, indicates nothing -> that host
  mode change is never re-reported to the OS.
- **Change**: (b) swap `config_change_pending` to 0 BEFORE calling `indicate_child_status` in the prologue, so a bit
  set during the indication survives to the next iteration. (a) have StartDevice (or the first post-StartDevice DDI)
  set an adapter `start_complete` flag and signal `hpd_event`, and demote the 500 ms to a bounded fallback with a
  named constant rather than the mechanism. Do NOT collapse the loop's four atomic reads into one sampled
  `enum Wake`: the re-reads at `:126-128` deliberately observe state the completion DPC changed DURING the wait, and
  sampling once before the wait would change when `drain_used_and_complete` runs - i.e. change lost-interrupt
  behaviour. Name the three phases and the two remaining timeout constants; that is the enforceable improvement here.
- **Static guarantee**: none - the wake source is a `KEVENT` signalled from a DPC, and "StartDevice has returned"
  cannot be a compile-time fact for a thread StartDevice itself spawned. What replaces the guarantee is an explicit
  runtime edge (`start_complete` + signal) with the timeout demoted to a documented fallback, which is the honest
  distinction the tranche's wait policy demands.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: two commits, not combined. (1) the swap-before-indicate reorder, marked as a behaviour fix.
  (2) the `start_complete` edge plus the constant naming.
- **Risk**: low - the reorder can double-indicate `Connected=1` once at boot if both the prologue swap and the first
  loop iteration see a set bit; `DxgkCbIndicateChildStatus` is idempotent for an unchanged connection state, and
  `HpdN` makes the extra call visible.
- **Validation**: `HpdN` still reaches 1 within ~500 ms of StartDevice on a cold boot (read the registry the same
  boot); a host-side display resize produces an additional `HpdI`/`HpdN` increment; after commit (2) `HpdN` reaches 1
  measurably sooner than the 500 ms fallback (that is the proof the real edge fires).

## T4a - Encode the transport, venus and allocation invariants

This tranche turns the hand-proved invariants of `kmd_render/src/virtio/{venus,gpu,ctrl}.rs` and the
`create_allocation` descriptor into types: the no-panic rule becomes structural (six `expect`/`unwrap`
sites deleted, `Writer` gains a checked API so a 512-byte fixed buffer stops being protected by
arithmetic in a comment), Vulkan object ids and wire fences stop being interchangeable `u64`s,
`VenusClient` stops existing in a half-built state, the descriptor chain and the sync-waiter pairing
stop being three loose fields the drain re-derives by hand, and the four remaining error-contract
defects (a full waiter table reported as a fence TIMEOUT in the counter the project uses as evidence;
three hand-rolled ways to abandon the pending fence FIFO with nothing counting the drop; a ring wedge
that blocks a DDI for 30 s and latches fatal with no named counter; a silent memory-type downgrade)
get the counters and outcome enums the project's own rules require. It sits after T3 because these are
the paths the frozen baseline depends on but that no visible-desktop check exercises hard - a wrong
edit here surfaces as a host decode abort or a corrupt frame, not a blank screen - and after T1a/T1b
because several items sit on lines those tranches already touch. It does **not** change any encoded
byte stream, any wire fence semantics, any registry knob or counter name that already exists (two
counters and one CollectDbgInfo report word are *added*), the direct-primary path's shape, or the ring's
30 s wait budget. `k-ctrlsubmit-07` part B (replacing the enqueue-backpressure sleeps with an event) is
explicitly **out of scope** here: it is a mechanism change on the DWM present path and needs its own
before/after numbers.

Line numbers below were re-opened against the working tree at KMD 22.22.176.0 and corrected where the
source findings were off; three stated dependencies were dropped because their targets live in T8 or
were dropped from the plan entirely (noted per item).

### R601. Delete all six panicking call sites on kernel release paths

- **Finding**: x-ordering-03. BUG (invariant hardening - all six are currently unreachable).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:258` (`ctrl_roundtrip`), `:1417` and `:1420`
  (`submit_venus_async`); `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:356-358`
  (`OptimalPresentImageDesc::pixel_format`), `:458-460` (`PresentBufferDesc::pixel_format`);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/create_allocation.rs:505` (`submit_primary_scanout_copy`). Panic handler:
  `kmd_render/src/lib.rs:17-22` (`extern crate wdk_panic`) with `panic = "abort"` at
  `kmd_render/Cargo.toml:45,50`.
- **Today**: `grep -rn '\.expect(\|\.unwrap()' kmd_render/src` returns exactly these six lines - the
  crate's only runtime panic sources of this class (the remaining `assert!`s are `gpummu.rs` const
  asserts). Three are `Option::take().expect(...)` used only because an enqueue retry loop round-trips
  a `DmaBuffer` through an `Option`; two re-derive a `PresentPixelFormat` the constructor already
  validated (`from_dxgi(...).expect("validated ...")`); one is `prepared.take().unwrap()` guarded by a
  preceding `.map(...).unwrap_or(false)`. Each is a hand-proved invariant. Defect class hidden: a panic
  in any DDI is a `KeBugCheck`, so a future edit that breaks one of these six proofs converts a
  recoverable error path into a stop.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `submit_venus_async` at `ctrl.rs:1414-1440` currently reinitializes
  `meta_slot`/`venus_slot` on the only arm that loops back. Adding a third `continue`-shaped arm (for
  example a `VirtioError::Timeout` retry) that returns the buffers to only one of the two slots
  compiles and panics on the next iteration. Symmetrically, `OptimalPresentImageDesc`'s fields are
  private *outside* `venus.rs`, so a struct literal added inside that module bypasses `new`'s
  `from_dxgi(..).is_some()` check and makes `pixel_format()` bugcheck.
- **Change**: (a) Rewrite both enqueue retry loops to carry the buffers as loop values instead of
  through `Option`: `let mut m = meta; let mut vn = venus; loop { match adapter.with_virtio(move |v| {
  ... enqueue_async_submit(ctx_id, ring_idx, m, vn, venus_len, None) }) { Ok(Err((m_back, v_back,
  VirtioError::QueueFull))) => { m = m_back; vn = v_back; ... } ... } }`. Rust's flow-sensitive move
  checking accepts reinitialize-before-back-edge, and any future arm that fails to reinitialize is a
  *compile* error instead of a runtime panic. Same shape for `ctrl_roundtrip`'s single-buffer loop.
  (b) Add a private `pixel_format: PresentPixelFormat` field to `OptimalPresentImageDesc` and
  `PresentBufferDesc`. `OptimalPresentImageDesc::new` (`venus.rs:328`, private; the two public
  constructors `new_opaque_fd` at `:364` and `new_cross_context_dma_buf` at `:387` both delegate to it)
  currently spends the `from_dxgi` result on an `.is_some()` test - bind it and store it instead.
  `PresentBufferDesc::new` (`:428`) already binds `pixel_format` at `:437` and simply discards it. Then
  make both `pixel_format()` methods a field read. Both structs derive
  `Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq` and so does `PresentPixelFormat`, and the
  format is a pure function of `dxgi_format`, so derived equality (used for the present-image cache
  hit test) is unchanged. (c) Replace the `take().unwrap()` with
  `if let Some(old) = prepared.take_if(|p| p.target_image_id != target_image_id) { ... }` - a bare
  `if let Some(old) = prepared.take()` is **wrong**, it also takes on the cache-hit path. If `take_if`
  is unwanted, the equivalent no-new-API form is `prepared = match prepared { Some(old) if
  old.target_image_id != target_image_id => { ...destroy...; clear_prepared_copy(ctx); None } other =>
  other };`.
- **Static guarantee**: Real and complete for this class. Parse-once/store-the-parsed-value removes the
  fallible re-derivation from the type; the loop rebinding removes the `Option` and therefore the
  `take`. After this commit `grep -rn '\.expect(\|\.unwrap()' kmd_render/src` is empty and can be a CI
  gate. No new `unsafe`, no runtime cost (the format field is one byte in a struct already >= 32 bytes).
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: Three commits, each independently revertible and each verifiable by the grep
  above shrinking: (1) `ctrl.rs` loops; (2) `venus.rs` desc fields; (3) `create_allocation.rs`
  take-then-rematch. Land (3) before R609, which deletes the `scanout_copy_last_fence` read inside the
  same block.
- **Risk**: low. The only behavioral risk is (c): getting the `take` condition wrong changes retarget
  semantics, so diff the three-line block by hand rather than trusting the rewrite.
- **Validation**: KMD builds clean; the grep gate is empty. Boot + composited desktop
  (`helios_paintcap`) exercises (b) on every Present; one 3DMark Fire Strike run plus a DOOM run
  exercises the enqueue-retry arms under real backpressure - `QUEUE_FULL_RETRIES` must move to the same
  order of magnitude as a pre-change run and `PARKED_LEAKS` must stay 0. A retarget (change display
  mode, forcing `target_image_id` to differ) must still produce `CpDrn=1` followed by `CpCpy=1`.

### R602. Give `Writer` a checked API and fix the size comment it is justified by

- **Finding**: k-venus-02. BUG (latent - not reachable without a source edit).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:229-231` (`MAX_CMD_BYTES = 512` and its
  `"largest is vkCreateDevice (~120 bytes)"` comment), `:722-780` (`struct Writer` and every write
  method: `u32` `:735-739`, `u64` `:745-749`, `bytes_padded` `:762-769`, `as_slice` `:777-779`),
  `:4870-4881` (`EXT_FULL`/`EXT_EXPORT`), `:4928-4938` (the ext-list encoding loop).
- **Today**: every `Writer` method writes through an unchecked slice range (`self.buf[self.len..self.len
  + 4].copy_from_slice(..)`), so exceeding 512 bytes is a slice-index panic, i.e. a `KeBugCheck` inside
  a DDI. The comment that sizes the buffer is wrong by 2.7x: hand-encoding the `EXT_FULL` tier of
  `vkCreateDevice` against `venus.rs:4906-4942` gives exactly **332 bytes** (144 bytes of struct plus
  188 bytes of length-prefixed, 4-byte-padded extension strings: 24+28+28+32+36 padded plus five 8-byte
  lengths). The no-panic invariant is therefore enforced by arithmetic performed in a code comment, and
  that arithmetic is already false by 212 bytes.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: 512-332 = 180 bytes of slack, so adding *one* extension string does
  **not** overflow (the original claim that a sixth extension bugchecks the guest is refuted). What
  compiles and bugchecks is: four more `EXT_FULL` strings, or any single encoder growing by ~180 bytes
  - a new `pNext` chain on `VkDeviceCreateInfo`, a multi-region `vkCmdCopyImage`, or a queue-family
  index array. Nothing in the type system, no `debug_assert`, and no counter flags it, and the comment
  a reader would consult to size the change is off by 212 bytes.
- **Change**: Add a sticky `overflow: bool` to `Writer`. Every write method becomes
  `if self.len + n > MAX_CMD_BYTES { self.overflow = true; return; }` before the copy. `as_slice`
  becomes `fn as_slice(&self) -> Result<&[u8], VirtioError>` returning `Err(VirtioError::DeviceError)`
  when `overflow` is set, after `crate::diag::record_named_bytes(b"VnEncOvf", cmd_type)` (read the
  command type back from `self.buf[0..4]`; `record_named_bytes` is *not* `DiagLevel`-gated, unlike
  `diag::record`, so the refusal is visible at `DiagLevel 0`). Mechanically add `?` at the **48**
  `*.as_slice()` call sites in this file (`grep -c '\.as_slice()' kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs` = 48;
  all are `Writer` receivers: 41 `w`, 4 `submit`, and one each `set`, `sub`, `wait`). Keep
  `MAX_CMD_BYTES = 512` so no stream that fits today changes, and rewrite the doc comment to state 332
  bytes and how it was derived.
- **Static guarantee**: Real: overflow becomes a value in the return type instead of a panic path, and
  `as_slice` can only be obtained from a `Writer` that never overflowed. The stronger form -
  `Writer<const N: usize>` with a dedicated `Writer<1024>` for the `vkCreateDevice` encoder - is also
  expressible in `no_std` (plain array field, no alloc) and prevents the ext-list encoder being
  re-pointed at the small buffer; take it only if the 512-byte constant is later raised for one caller.
