- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit (field + 4 method guards + fallible `as_slice` + 48 `?` + the comment
  fix). No encoder byte changes, so it must be diff-reviewable as "48 added `?` and nothing else" in
  the encoder bodies.
- **Risk**: low. The single risk is a missed call site changing an encoder's control flow; the compiler
  catches every one because `as_slice`'s type changes.
- **Validation**: A host-target unit test in the T0 logic crate encodes the `EXT_FULL` `vkCreateDevice`
  stream and asserts `len == 332`, and encodes each of the four `CMD_CREATE_IMAGE` variants and
  `CMD_QUEUE_SUBMIT` asserting byte-equality with a captured pre-change golden. On the guest: `VnEncOvf`
  must be **absent** from the service key after a full StartDevice + DWM composite + Present run
  (absent, not zero - it is created only on overflow). Host `/tmp/helios-qemu-stderr.log` free of venus
  decode errors.

### R603. Route every `fatal` latch through one `latch_fatal(reason)` with named counters

- **Finding**: k-venus-V01. BUG (a wedged ring leaves zero registry evidence on a default boot).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:946` (`publish_and_notify`, `RING_STATUS_FATAL`), `:986`
  (`ring_wait_until`, `RING_STATUS_FATAL`), `:990` (`ring_wait_until`, timeout) - the only three
  `self.fatal = true` sites. Budget constants at `:223-227` (`RING_SPIN_BURST = 50_000`,
  `RING_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`). Reachability: `ddi/display.rs:460` -> `submit_present_blt` ->
  `ensure_present_image` -> `create_optimal_present_image_alias` -> `ring_command_reply` (`:1046`) ->
  `write_to_ring` (`:1001`) -> `ring_wait_until` (`:968`); also `ddi/create_allocation.rs:498-539` and
  `:942`/`:978`. `diag::record` is `DiagLevel`-gated at `diag.rs:165-168`.
- **Today**: a single ring command whose head never advances burns a 50 000-iteration MMIO-read spin
  burst, then 1 ms sleep-polls for up to 30 s, then sets `self.fatal` and returns
  `VirtioError::DeviceError` - with **no** `record_named_bytes`. The two `RING_STATUS_FATAL` latches are
  likewise uncounted. Because `diag::record` is gated off by default, a ring wedge on a production boot
  is indistinguishable from any other `DeviceError`, which violates the project rule that every refused
  path gets a named counter and destroys the post-mortem for exactly the failure the 30 s budget exists
  to survive. The 30 s budget is also inconsistent with the 5 s budget every other host wait in the file
  uses (`:2393`, `:4084`, `:4145`).
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a - no illegal call order. The defect is a silent failure latch plus
  a half-minute stall inside `DxgkDdiPresent` while holding the adapter venus mutex.
- **Change**: Add `fn latch_fatal(&mut self, reason: FatalReason)` on `VenusClient` with
  `enum FatalReason { HostStatusFatal, HeadWaitTimeout }`; it sets `self.fatal` and records
  `record_named_bytes(b"VnRingFt", 1)` / `record_named_bytes(b"VnRingWd", elapsed_ms)` respectively.
  Route all three assignments through it and make the field private to the impl by convention (a
  `grep -n 'self.fatal = true' venus.rs` gate returning only `latch_fatal`'s body). Purely additive:
  control flow is unchanged. Separately, either document `RING_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` against the
  dxgkrnl DDI timeout it is chosen for and state that a Present-path caller may block that long, or
  raise it as an owner question - do **not** shorten it without measurement: a bounded wait on a real
  ring-head watermark is a safety contract, and the constant is deliberately separate from the 5 s
  fence budget.
- **Static guarantee**: Modest but real: after this commit no site can transition the client to fatal
  without naming a reason, because the field is only written inside `latch_fatal`. No claim beyond that
  - the budget consistency is a documented decision, not a type.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit (`FatalReason` + `latch_fatal` + three call sites + two counters). The
  budget decision is a separate, documented commit or an owner question, not part of this one.
- **Risk**: low. `record_named_bytes` writes the registry, so it must not be called above PASSIVE -
  verified: all three latch sites are on PASSIVE ring paths (`ring_wait_until` calls
  `ctrl::sleep_ms`, which is `KeDelayExecutionThread`).
- **Validation**: `VnRingWd` and `VnRingFt` must be **absent** from the service key after a full boot +
  DWM composite + Present run (this is the tranche's ring-fatal gate). Force a wedge by pausing the host
  renderer (`SIGSTOP` on the qemu process) during a Present and confirm `VnRingWd` appears with a
  plausible elapsed value *before* the DDI returns, and that resuming leaves the client fast-failing as
  it does today.

### R604. Split the full-waiter-table condition out of `FENCE_WAIT_TIMEOUTS`

- **Finding**: k-ctrlsubmit-10. BUG (the counter the project uses as fence evidence conflates two
  conditions).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:1545-1553` (`wait_fence`, the `FenceWaitPrep::TableFull`
  arm) and `:1583` (the real timeout arm) - both increment `FENCE_WAIT_TIMEOUTS`.
  `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:490` (`MAX_FENCE_WAITERS = 64`), `:1623-1625`
  (`fence_wait_prepare` returns `TableFull` only for that condition). Consumers:
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/submit_command.rs:972` (the fixed `[u32; 35]` CollectDbgInfo report - **index 25**,
  not 26; version word is index 1 and currently `4`) and `:133` (diag-ring mirror `0x0F16_NNNN`).
  Template to copy: `gpu.rs:1673-1676` (`FENCE_EVENT_OVERFLOWS` + an explicit `FenceEventReg::TableFull`
  outcome).
- **Today**: with 64 waiters parked, the 65th polls `1_000` times at 1 ms and then reports
  `WaitFenceOutcome::TimedOut` while incrementing the same counter as "the host did not complete this
  fence". Note the poll is nominally 1 s but `KeDelayExecutionThread` with a 1 ms relative timeout
  rounds up to the system timer granularity, so it is up to ~16 s of thread residency. That counter is
  dumped into the TDR report and the diag ring, so post-mortem evidence cannot distinguish a wedged host
  from a 64-slot table that needs resizing - and the ICD applies its forward-progress policy to a
  condition that waiting on the right thing would have satisfied.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: 65 concurrent blocking-escape venus waiters (dwm plus several apps
  plus WUDFHost - which `gpu.rs:491-495`'s own comment says is expected) makes the 65th return
  `TimedOut` with the host perfectly healthy, and the TDR report blames the host.
- **Change**: Behavior-preserving counter split. Add `pub static FENCE_WAIT_TABLE_FULL: AtomicU32` next
  to `FENCE_WAIT_TIMEOUTS` in `gpu.rs` and increment it - *instead of* `FENCE_WAIT_TIMEOUTS` - on the
  exhausted-`full_retries` path at `ctrl.rs:1548-1550`. Keep returning `TimedOut` so the ICD is
  untouched. Append it to the CollectDbgInfo array as **index 35** (`[u32; 35]` -> `[u32; 36]`,
  `size_of::<[u32; 36]>()` at `submit_command.rs:984`) and bump the version word at `:943` from `4` to
  `5` **in the same commit** - the report is decoded offline by index, so never renumber an existing
  word. Mark `WaitFenceOutcome` `#[non_exhaustive]` so a future variant cannot be silently folded into
  `TimedOut` at the escape boundary. Do **not** shorten the retry budget and do **not** add a new
  outcome value here: `escape_wait_fence` (`ddi/escape.rs:467-485`) reports only `out_completed` 1/0
  plus `STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER`, so a third state needs a paired ICD change.
- **Static guarantee**: The outcome enum already exists; the substance is the counter split, not a type.
  `#[non_exhaustive]` plus explicit per-variant mapping in `escape_wait_fence` is the real, small
  encoding: adding a variant becomes a compile error at the boundary instead of a silent collapse.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit: counter + `ctrl.rs` increment + report word + version bump +
  `#[non_exhaustive]`. A follow-on commit paired with an ICD change can add the distinct escape payload;
  that is not in this tranche.
- **Risk**: low. The one way to break offline tooling is bumping the array without the version word, or
  vice versa - both live in the same commit by construction.
- **Validation**: `FENCE_WAIT_TIMEOUTS` **and** `FENCE_WAIT_TABLE_FULL` must both read 0 after a healthy
  DWM session plus Fire Strike plus DOOM (this is the tranche's fence-timeout gate, and it only means
  anything after this split). Force the condition with a >64-concurrent-waiter escape test and confirm
  `FENCE_WAIT_TABLE_FULL` moves while `FENCE_WAIT_TIMEOUTS` stays 0. Decode a `CollectDbgInfo` dump and
  confirm word 1 reads 5 and word 25 still reads `FENCE_WAIT_TIMEOUTS`.

### R605. Make a memory-type downgrade a value the caller must acknowledge

- **Finding**: k-venus-09. BUG (silent property downgrade on a production path).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:1181-1199` (`choose_host_visible_memory_type` - fallback is
  `HOST_VISIBLE` without `HOST_COHERENT`), `:1201-1229` (`choose_device_local_memory_type` - three
  tiers, final fallback is the *first allowed* type whether device-local or not). Five call sites:
  `:1587`, `:4278`, `:4373` (device-local) and `:4280`, `:4458` (host-visible). Production exposure:
  `allocate_optimal_gdi_image_blob`'s own doc at `:4338-4344` asserts "device-local dedicated memory"
  and it is called from `ddi/create_allocation.rs:978`; `allocate_linear_scanout_image_blob` (`:4458`)
  creates a MAPPABLE scanout blob.
- **Today**: both selectors return `Option<u32>` and callers read `Some(i)` as "the requested property
  was satisfied". `choose_device_local_memory_type`'s final `fallback` is simply the lowest set bit of
  `memory_type_bits`, device-local or not. Defect class: fake success - the same class as
  ScanoutDiag=16 / SdgErr=2, where a memory-type choice that looked fine was not. Note the page-table
  bring-up does **not** use these selectors (it has its own explicit `HOST_VISIBLE|HOST_COHERENT` scan
  at `:4831-4854`), so the exposure is confined to the two blob allocators above.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: a host whose `memoryTypeBits` for an OPTIMAL GDI image contains only a
  `HOST_VISIBLE`, non-`DEVICE_LOCAL` type: the selector returns it, `allocate_optimal_gdi_image_blob`
  reports success, and the storage contract stated in its own doc comment is silently false with no
  breadcrumb anywhere. The host-visible sibling silently picks a non-`COHERENT` type for a MAPPABLE
  scanout blob, where only `SdgMf` would hint at it.
- **Change**: Change both selectors to return
  `#[must_use] enum MemoryTypeChoice { Exact(u32), Downgraded(u32) }` (`None` becomes
  `Option<MemoryTypeChoice>`, or add a third `Unavailable` variant - pick one and apply it to both).
  Each of the five call sites matches both arms and calls
  `crate::diag::record_named_bytes(b"VnMtDown", index)` on `Downgraded` before proceeding with the same
  index it uses today. Behavior is identical; only the silence is removed.
- **Static guarantee**: Real but modest: `#[must_use]` plus an exhaustive two-arm match forces every
  call site to acknowledge the downgrade at compile time and prevents a caller discarding the
  distinction. It does not prevent choosing a downgraded type - it prevents doing so silently.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit: two selectors plus five call sites.
- **Risk**: low. The only way to change behavior is to accidentally reorder the tier tests inside
  `choose_device_local_memory_type`; the three tiers must stay
  (device-local-and-not-host-visible) -> (device-local) -> (first allowed).
- **Validation**: A host-target unit test over synthetic `memory_type_flags`/`memory_type_bits` arrays
  asserts `Exact` for the NVIDIA-shaped case and `Downgraded` for a host-visible-only case (both
  selectors are pure functions of two struct fields, so they move into the T0 logic crate unchanged). On
  the guest: `VnMtDown` must be **absent** after a full boot plus DWM composite plus a GDI-accelerated
  workload - the exact-match arm is what today's host takes.

### R606. Wrap the ring mapping in a size-proving `RingMap` and make `read_byte` checked

- **Finding**: k-venus-05.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:619-624` (`struct KernelMap { va, size }`), `:626-646`
  (`new` - never validates `size` against any minimum), `:648-654` (`zero`), `:655-663`
  (`load_u32_acquire`), `:668-678` (`store_u32_seqcst`), `:681-702` (`write_ring_buffer`), `:702-708`
  (`read_byte`). Construction sites: `:4605-4608` (ring), `:4621-4624` (reply), `:4011-4017` (the
  Present-destination probe, gated on `adapter.present_probe` at `:3958`). Size constants at
  `:199-205` (`RING_BUFFER_OFFSET = 192`, `RING_BUFFER_SIZE = 131072`, `RING_SHMEM_SIZE`).
  *Dependency correction*: the source finding lists `k-venus-01` as a prerequisite; that finding is in
  T8 (file split) and is not needed - this item stands alone.
- **Today**: four **safe** fns dereference `va + offset` with no bounds check; `self.size` is carried in
  the struct and simply never consulted. Worse, the SAFETY comment on `load_u32_acquire` asserts a
  *different* invariant than the one required - "all ring header offsets are `< RING_SHMEM_SIZE`" only
  discharges the precondition if the mapping is at least `RING_SHMEM_SIZE`, which `KernelMap::new` never
  checks and `allocate_host_visible_blob` never asserts: it maps whatever `ring_prep.size` the blob
  tracker returns. A SAFETY comment that establishes a different invariant than the one depended on is
  worse than none.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: the cross-check that a recycled resource id could attach a stale
  smaller size is **refuted** - `gpu.rs:1870-1872` allocates resource ids with a monotonic `fetch_add`
  and never recycles them, and `blob_map_begin` (`gpu.rs:2087-2098`) rounds the tracked size up to
  135168 >= `RING_SHMEM_SIZE` (131268). The residual exposure is by construction, not by call order:
  nothing in the type system distinguishes a ring-sized mapping from an arbitrary one, so a second
  ring/reply mapping site, a re-map of an already-mapped blob (`blob_map_begin`'s `Mapped` arm returns
  the previously recorded `s.map_len` verbatim), or a host reporting a short `map_len` yields an
  undersized `KernelMap` whose ring accessors then write up to `RING_BUFFER_OFFSET + 131072` bytes past
  the mapping - with the SAFETY comment reading as if that were impossible.
- **Change**: Add `struct RingMap(KernelMap)` in `venus.rs` with
  `fn new(gpa, size, map_cache) -> Option<Self>` that proves `size >= RING_SHMEM_SIZE` (returning `None`
  with `record_named_bytes(b"VnRingSz", size_kib)` otherwise) and whose accessors take
  `enum RingWord { Head, Tail, Status }` instead of a raw `u64` offset, plus one checked
  `write_buffer(cur, src)` for the `[RING_BUFFER_OFFSET, RING_EXTRA_OFFSET)` window. `VenusClient::ring_map`
  becomes a `RingMap`. Keep plain `KernelMap` for the reply and probe paths, but change
  `read_byte(&self, offset: u64) -> Option<u8>`: `ReplyReader` (`:788-841`) already bounds-checks
  `self.pos + n > self.end` where `end = map.size`, so its per-byte loops absorb the `Option` with one
  `.ok_or(VirtioError::DeviceError)?`, and `probe_present_destination`'s four sample reads
  (`:4031-4044`) become checked (breadcrumb `PBPrF = 0xE6` on `None`) instead of argued about in a
  comment. Rewrite `KernelMap::new`'s SAFETY comment to state only what `MmMapIoSpace` gives.
- **Static guarantee**: Real for the ring: `offset < size` moves from a per-call caller obligation to a
  constructor postcondition, and the three header offsets become an enum with no other inhabitants -
  an out-of-range ring offset is no longer expressible. For the probe/reply path the guarantee is
  weaker but still real: `Option<u8>` converts an unchecked deref into a checked one. Do **not** claim
  the wrapper removes `unsafe`; it constrains which offsets can reach it.
- **Remaining unsafe**: `MmMapIoSpace`'s promise that `[gpa, gpa+size)` is host-backed (the venus blob
  was `RESOURCE_MAP_BLOB`'d into exactly this window range) cannot be encoded. After this commit that is
  the **only** surviving unsafe precondition of the type, which is the point.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit: `RingMap` + `RingWord` + checked `read_byte` + the two SAFETY comment
  rewrites. Must land before R608, which moves `ring_map` into the `VenusRing` typestate.
- **Risk**: medium. `write_ring_buffer`'s wrap arithmetic is the live producer for every ring command; a
  transcription error there is an immediate ring desync, not a graceful failure. Move the body verbatim
  and change only the bounds it is reached through.
- **Validation**: Boot to desktop; the venus bring-up breadcrumbs `0x0D00_0001`..`0x0D00_000C` must
  appear in the same order at `DiagLevel 1`, `page_table_window` must still be published (`DpInf`
  unchanged), `VnRingSz` must be absent, and no new refusal counter may appear. Host
  `/tmp/helios-qemu-stderr.log` must be free of venus decode errors and byte-comparable in command mix
  to a pre-change run of the same workload.

### R607. Give every Vulkan object class its own id type

- **Finding**: k-venus-04.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:918-923` (`alloc_handle` - one untyped `u64` counter for
  every object class), `:1834-1858` (`bind_image_memory`) and `:1861-1880` (`bind_buffer_memory`) -
  signature-identical `(&mut self, &AdapterContext, u64, u64)`, `:2484-2495`
  (`destroy_image_on_ring`) and `:2501-2508` (`destroy_buffer_on_ring`) - both accept any `u64`,
  `:2510-2524` (`cleanup_imported_source_alias(_, resource_id: u32, image_id: u64, memory_id: u64)`),
  `:280-308` (`pub struct PreparedImageCopy` - 12 pub fields, 7 of them bare `u64` ids). Mirrors that
  must be co-converted: `kmd_render/src/ddi/create_allocation.rs:58,61` (`venus_memory_id`,
  `venus_image_id`) and `:65-74` (nine `AtomicU64` plus one `AtomicU32` holding the same ids).
- **Today**: `alloc_handle` mints one untyped `u64` from a single counter for images, memory, buffers,
  pools, command buffers, fences, queues and the device. Because every id is a live handle in the same
  host object space, a swapped argument does not fail loudly - it destroys or rebinds the wrong host
  object, surfacing later as a corrupt frame or a host decoder abort. No such swap exists today (every
  call site of the four functions above passes correctly-typed ids), so this is defect prevention; it is
  nonetheless the highest-leverage compile-time win available in this file.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: a refactor that reorders the adjacent pair -
  `cleanup_imported_source_alias(adapter, resource_id, memory_id, image_id)` - compiles, and at runtime
  issues `vkDestroyImage` on a `VkDeviceMemory` handle and `vkFreeMemory` on a `VkImage` handle. Both
  are accepted by the encoder; only the host notices. Same for `bind_image_memory(memory_id, image_id)`.
- **Change**: Add `#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct VkImageId(NonZeroU64);` and
  siblings `VkDeviceMemoryId`, `VkBufferId`, `VkCommandPoolId`, `VkCommandBufferId`, `VkFenceId`,
  `VkQueueId`, `VkDeviceId`. `alloc_handle` becomes a private
  `fn next_raw(&mut self) -> NonZeroU64` with one typed constructor per class. Absent handles become
  `Option<...>` instead of the `0` sentinel, replacing the ~30 scattered `if x != 0` guards. `Writer`
  gains `fn handle(&mut self, h: impl Into<u64>)` so the encoded bytes are unchanged. `core::num::NonZeroU64`
  is `core`, so `Option<VkImageId>` is the same size as today's `u64` and the "0 means absent"
  convention becomes a type-level fact.
- **Static guarantee**: Real, not cosmetic: the newtypes are not interconvertible, so no
  image/memory/buffer/pool/fence argument can be passed where another is expected, and the null
  sentinel disappears from the value space. Depends on R602 so `Writer::handle` is added on top of the
  checked API, and on R601 so the desc structs are not being edited twice.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none in this file. The host still trusts guest-assigned ids, which is inherent
  to venus and not encodable here.
- **Atomic boundary**: Two commits. (1) Introduce the newtypes and convert only the private encoders
  (`create_*`/`destroy_*`/`bind_*`/`cmd_*`/`free_*`), keeping the `pub` signatures on `u64` with
  conversions at the module boundary - this is the large, purely internal diff. (2) Convert the `pub`
  structs (`PreparedImageCopy`, `ScanoutImageBlob`, `OptimalImageBlob`) and the `create_allocation.rs`
  mirrors; the atomics keep storing raw `u64` with conversion in one validating `restore()`.
- **Risk**: medium. Blast radius is every encoder in a 4994-line file plus the allocation mirrors. The
  specific thing that breaks is an encoder that writes a handle through `w.u64(..)` on a path the
  conversion misses, silently emitting `0`; the `NonZeroU64` niche makes that a compile error only where
  the value is typed, so commit (1) must convert *every* encoder, not a subset.
- **Validation**: Byte-identical encoded streams: host-target unit tests that encode
  `create_optimal_present_image_alias`, `bind_image_memory` and `queue_submit` before and after and
  assert equality (these are pure `Writer` functions once the ids are values). On the guest: DWM
  composite plus one Fire Strike run with `CpImgVr`, `CpMemVr` and `PBBufVr` unchanged (absent), and
  `/tmp/helios-qemu-stderr.log` free of "failed to look up object of type" lines.

### R608. Typestate the venus bring-up so a half-built client is unrepresentable

- **Finding**: x-ordering-06.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:4588-4994` (`allocate_host_visible_blob`), `:4627-4653`
  (the `VenusClient { .. }` literal, with `instance_id: 0, device_id: 0, queue_id: 0,
  memory_type_index: 0, memory_type_count: 0, fatal: false` at `:4639-4645`), `:4655-4676`
  (CreateRingMESA), `:4899-4974` (the three-tier CreateDevice ladder, which assigns
  `client.device_id = device_id` at `:4906` **inside** the retry loop), `:4977` (`get_device_queue`),
  `:4982` (`allocate_memory_blob`). Sole call site: `kmd_render/src/ddi/start_device.rs:197`, with
  `adapter.set_venus_client(Some(client))` at `:204`.
- **Today**: a fully-typed `VenusClient` is constructed at stage 2 and then mutated through seven more
  ordered stages. Between them the struct is a valid `VenusClient` whose `device_id`/`queue_id`/
  `memory_type_index` are `0`, and every one of its ~40 methods will happily encode `VkDevice 0` into
  the wire stream. The ordering is enforced only by the linear layout of one 400-line function.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: any refactor that hoists a helper above its stage - calling
  `client.allocate_memory_blob(..)` or `client.create_scanout_image(..)` before the CreateDevice ladder,
  for example as a capability probe - compiles and sends `vkAllocateMemory(device = 0)`, which the host
  answers by poisoning the ring (the documented fatal-decoder class). Not reachable from outside the
  module today: the client only becomes visible to other modules through `set_venus_client` after the
  full bring-up succeeds.
- **Change**: Split into three types with ownership-consuming transitions:
  `VenusRing { ring_id, ring_res_id, reply_res_id, ring_map: RingMap, reply_map, cur, notify_seqno,
  roundtrip_seqno, next_handle, ctx_id, fatal }` exposing only `submit_direct`, `ring_command_noreply`,
  `ring_command_reply` and `latch_fatal`; `fn into_instance(self, ..) -> Result<VenusInstance, ..>`
  adding `instance_id` + `phys_dev_id` and exposing only the enumerate/memory-properties queries;
  `fn into_device(self, ..) -> Result<VenusClient, ..>` adding `NonZeroU64` `device_id`/`queue_id` and a
  validated `MemoryTypeIndex`. The CreateDevice ladder must be restructured to compute the device id in
  a local and return it from the loop, then build the final type once - it cannot keep writing
  `client.device_id` mid-loop. All ~40 `&mut self` methods move to the final type unchanged.
- **Static guarantee**: Real typestate: each transition consumes the previous value, so no stage can be
  skipped or reordered and no method of a later stage is nameable earlier. `NonZeroU64` device/queue ids
  and a `MemoryTypeIndex` newtype make the "not yet valid" state unrepresentable rather than encoded as
  `0`. Depends on R606 (`RingMap` is `VenusRing`'s field) and R607 (`NonZeroU64` ids).
- **Remaining unsafe**: the `RingMap`/`KernelMap` raw VAs - their validity depends on the host honoring
  `RESOURCE_MAP_BLOB` for the window range, which no Rust type can witness.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit; it cannot be usefully split because the ladder restructure and the
  struct split are the same edit. Keep every `diag(0x00NN)` breadcrumb value and every
  `record_named_bytes` name (`SdgDevX`, `SdgDevR`) byte-identical - they are the owner's bring-up ABI.
- **Risk**: medium. The specific hazard is the ext-tier ladder: it currently records `SdgDevR` per
  knock-down and `SdgDevX` on success, and it mutates `client.device_id` before each attempt. Moving the
  id to a local must preserve the property that each attempt uses a *fresh* handle (`alloc_handle` per
  iteration at `:4905`) - reusing one handle across tiers would make a retry collide with the host's
  record of the failed device.
- **Validation**: Same-boot StartDevice diag sequence `0x0B00_0003`, `0x0D00_0001`..`0x0D00_000C`,
  `0x0B00_0007` unchanged and in the same order; `SdgDevX` reads the same tier as a pre-change boot
  (0 with `ScanoutDiag >= 4`, 1 with the display half, 2 render-only) and `SdgDevR` stays 0 on a clean
  full-tier success; `page_table_window` published; desktop composites.

### R609. Move the prepared-copy drain fence into the client, under the venus mutex

- **Finding**: k-venus-08. BUG (a stale-or-zero fence silently skips a mandatory drain).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:4133-4151` (`destroy_prepared_image_copy`'s
  `last_wire_fence_id: u64` parameter and the `if last_wire_fence_id != 0` skip at `:4144-4151`),
  `:4139-4143` (the doc stating why the drain is mandatory), `:3720-3755`
  (`submit_prepared_image_copy` returns the fence and retains nothing; note it takes
  `copy: &PreparedImageCopy`), `:550` + `:3956` (`PreparedPresentBlt::last_wire_fence_id`, the in-file
  precedent). Callers: `kmd_render/src/ddi/create_allocation.rs:505-508` (retarget - read inside
  `with_venus_client`), `:539-540` (the only `Release` store - inside the mutex), `:754-757`
  (`destroy_allocation_ctx` - read at `:755` **outside** the mutex, then `with_venus_client` acquired at
  `:757`).
- **Today**: the doc directly above the parameter says the drain is required because the reusable
  command buffer is submitted through an outer async `SUBMIT_3D` on a different Venus dispatch path than
  the ring marker, "otherwise the marker could be decoded first ... and let us destroy a
  still-referenced command pool". The client submitted that fence itself but does not remember it: the
  id round-trips through an `AtomicU64` in the caller's `AllocationContext` and comes back as a
  parameter. Passing `0` skips the drain silently with no counter, and the next steps free a command
  pool the host may still be executing.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: reachable today in `destroy_allocation_ctx`: `create_allocation.rs:755`
  loads `scanout_copy_last_fence` with `Acquire` **before** acquiring the venus mutex at `:757`, while
  the only writer (`:539-540`) performs its `Release` store **inside** the mutex right after
  `submit_prepared_image_copy`. A `SetVidPnSourceAddress` submit that has enqueued its outer
  `SUBMIT_3D` but whose store this thread has not yet observed therefore yields a stale-or-zero fence:
  with `0` the drain is skipped entirely and uncounted, the ring marker can be decoded ahead of the
  still-pending `SUBMIT_3D`, and `vkDestroyCommandPool` runs against a pool with in-flight work.
- **Change**: Add `scanout_copy_last_fence: u64` to `VenusClient` and have
  `submit_prepared_image_copy` store the fence it just obtained into it before returning. Drop the
  `last_wire_fence_id` parameter from `destroy_prepared_image_copy` entirely; it reads `self`. Both
  writer and reader are then inside `with_venus_client` by construction. **Do not** try to put the
  fence in `PreparedImageCopy`: that struct is `Copy` and caller-owned (submit takes it by shared
  reference), so a field there cannot be the source of truth. One client-wide field is correct and
  conservative: `copy_target_image_id` is a single-slot invariant (`venus.rs:2742` refuses a second
  target), wire fence ids are monotonic, and ring-1 submissions retire in order, so draining the highest
  prepared-copy fence drains every earlier one; never clear the field (waiting on an already-retired
  fence returns `Complete` immediately via `fence_wait_prepare`'s `!in_flight` arm). Keep
  `ctx.scanout_copy_last_fence` as a diagnostic mirror. Add
  `record_named_bytes(b"CpNoDrn", resource_id)` when the drain is skipped because no submit ever
  happened, so "nothing to drain" is distinguishable from "drain skipped by accident".
- **Static guarantee**: Real: removing the parameter removes both the invalid call (`0`) and the
  cross-mutex read - the value can only be written and read while holding the venus mutex, which is the
  invariant the doc asserts. The stronger `fn submit(self) -> InFlight<PreparedImageCopy>` typestate is
  possible but would force the atomic mirror to be reconstructed through a validating `restore()`; not
  in this commit.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none. The 5 s `ctrl::wait_fence` bound stays - it is a bounded wait on a real
  KEVENT-backed used-ring completion, i.e. a safety contract, not a delay hack.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit: the field, the store in `submit_prepared_image_copy`, the parameter
  removal, and both call sites (`create_allocation.rs:505-508` and `:754-757`). Land after R601 commit
  (3), which already reshapes the retarget block.
- **Risk**: medium. The behavior delta is that a teardown of allocation A may now wait on a copy
  submitted for allocation B. That is strictly more waiting and bounded by the same 5 s budget, but it
  means a wedged B can now delay A's `DestroyAllocation` - watch for a new `CpDrn=0xE` population.
- **Validation**: Allocation teardown during active scanout copies must still drain: on a fallback-copy
  boot the `CpCpy` / `CpFnc` / `CpDrn=1` sequence is unchanged and no `CpDrn=0xE` appears across a
  resolution change plus a DWM restart. `CpNoDrn` must be absent on a direct-primary boot (the copy path
  is never entered) and present-with-a-resource-id only on a fallback boot where a prepared copy was
  built but never submitted. Host log free of "destroying in-use command pool".

### R610. Destroy before forgetting in the Present-BLT teardown, and scope it to the resource

- **Finding**: k-venus-07. BUG (a mid-loop failure desynchronizes the KMD caches from host state and
  can manufacture a second `VkDeviceMemory` for one backing).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:4056-4126` (`release_present_blits_for_resource`): the
  fast-path guards returning `Ok(())` at `:4070` and `:4076`, the all-or-nothing prologue at `:4079-4101`
  (fence drain `:4082-4090`, queue marker `:4094-4101`), and the three pop-first loops at `:4103-4114`
  (blits), `:4115-4120` (images), `:4121-4126` (buffers). Contract violated:
  `OwnedMemoryBlob`'s doc at `:514-526` ("must never manufacture a second imported `VkDeviceMemory` for
  the same resource"). Correct order already implemented at `:4549-4571` (`free_memory_blob`: host free,
  then `swap_remove`). Caller: `kmd_render/src/ddi/create_allocation.rs:775-787`.
- **Today**: `pop()` removes the cache record first and the `?` operators bail out after it, in all three
  loops. The function otherwise goes to real trouble to be all-or-nothing - it drains every wire fence,
  then submits and waits a queue marker before touching anything, and its own comment at `:4079-4081`
  says "retain the complete cache ... rather than partially freeing live objects" - so the loops violate
  exactly the contract the prologue establishes, and no counter records a partial teardown. The loops
  also drain **every** cached entry regardless of `resource_id`, despite the entry gate at `:4061-4069`
  testing only for `resource_id`.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `DestroyAllocation(A)` -> the images loop pops B's
  `ImportedOptimalImage`, `vkDestroyImage` succeeds, `free_memory_blob` or `ctx_detach_resource` for B
  fails (a ctrl-queue error does not latch the venus ring fatal, so the client stays usable) -> `Err`
  returned -> the caller records `PBDrn=0xE` and **aborts** the teardown at
  `create_allocation.rs:780-787`, deliberately leaking A's host objects. B is still live and its cache
  record is gone: B's next Present re-enters `ensure_present_image` -> `import_optimal_present_image` ->
  `attach_resource_checked` on a resource that is still attached (`ctrl.rs:1022-1034` does no dedup) plus
  a fresh `allocate_imported_resource_memory`, and if the failing call was `free_memory_blob` a **second**
  `VkDeviceMemory` now names the same backing - precisely what `:514-519` forbids. Independently, the
  fast-path guard at `:4061-4069` now returns `Ok(())` for B, so B's own later teardown skips the fence
  drain and queue marker entirely.
- **Change**: Iterate by index and swap-remove only after every teardown call for that entry returns
  `Ok`, the shape `free_memory_blob` already uses; on failure record
  `record_named_bytes(b"PBTdErr", resource_id)` and return `Err` with the remaining cache intact.
  Separately, restrict each loop to entries whose `desc.resource_id == resource_id` (plus the blits that
  reference them) so a failure while tearing down A cannot forget B - this also makes the entry gate at
  `:4061-4069` and the fast path at `:4070` honest.
- **Static guarantee**: Encode the ownership transfer: give `ImportedOptimalImage` a consuming
  `fn release(self, client: &mut VenusClient, adapter: &AdapterContext) -> Result<(), (Self, VirtioError)>`
  that hands the value **back** on failure, so the cache reinserts it and "forgot the record while the
  host object survives" is unrepresentable. Same pattern for `BorrowedPresentBuffer` and
  `PreparedPresentBlt`. Real, and allocation-free: the `Vec` capacities are preallocated
  (`MAX_PRESENT_BLITS` at `:4651`), so reinsertion cannot allocate under any lock.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: Three commits, one per collection (blits, images, buffers), each independently
  revertible. Then a fourth for the per-resource scoping, which is the behavior-affecting half and must
  be reviewed against the "several swapchain sources may share one DWM destination" comment at
  `create_allocation.rs:772-774`.
- **Risk**: medium. The scoping change is the risk: if a blit's source and destination live in different
  resources, scoping the blits loop wrongly leaves a command buffer baked against a destroyed image.
  Derive the blit set from the images/buffers actually being released, not from a `resource_id` compare
  on the blit itself.
- **Validation**: Steady state - a normal swapchain destroy/recreate leaves `present_images` empty with
  `PBTdErr` absent and `PBDrn=1`; run DXVK app start/stop 20x and confirm `PBDrn=0xE` never appears.
  Forced failure - tear down an allocation while the venus context is being destroyed and confirm
  `PBTdErr` appears with the resource id and that a subsequent Present on a *different* surviving
  surface still works (that is the regression this fixes). Fire Strike plus DOOM plus a DWM-only idle
  period with no host "failed to look up object" lines.

### R611. Make the descriptor-chain shape one value and bounds-check the spans once

- **Finding**: k-gputransport-03.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:1075-1089` (`enqueue_sync` spans: `in0` / optional `in1` /
  `resp` at `in0_len + in1_len`), `:1153-1160` (`enqueue_async_control`: `input` / `response` at
  `in0_len`), `:1241-1250` (`enqueue_async_submit`: `hdr` / `stream` / `resp` at `hdr_len`),
  `:1311-1341` (`drain_used`'s hand re-derivation; the three-arm `pop_used` at `:1332-1340`),
  `:612-627` (`struct InFlight` - all fields module-private). Panic sites in the vendored dependency:
  `virtio-drivers-0.13.0/src/queue.rs:461,477` (`assert_ne!`), `:479`
  (`expect("Descriptor chain was shorter than expected.")`), `:501`
  (`panic!("Descriptor chain was longer than expected.")`).
- **Today**: four separate blocks of raw-pointer span arithmetic - three enqueue paths and the drain -
  must agree on the exact buffer list passed to `add`/`pop_used`. The agreement is expressed only by
  three independent length fields plus the comment "exactly the spans `add` was called with".
  virtio-drivers does not validate it: `pop_used` -> `recycle_descriptors` walks the chain against the
  caller-supplied list and panics on a mismatch, which with `panic = "abort"` and `wdk_panic` is a
  `KeBugCheck` from the interrupt DPC under the device spinlock. All four blocks agree today (sync:
  `in1_len` set / `venus` None; async_control: `in1_len` 0 / `venus` None; async_submit: `in1_len` 0 /
  `venus` Some), so this is drift prevention inside one module - `InFlight`'s fields are private to
  `gpu`, so only code in `gpu.rs` can desynchronize them.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: inside `gpu.rs`, a fourth enqueue path sets `in0_len = hdr`,
  `in1_len = 8`, `venus = Some(buf)`, `venus_len = 64` and calls
  `control.add(&[in0, in1, stream], ..)`; `drain_used` matches `venus_len > 0` **first** and calls
  `pop_used(token, &[in0, stream], ..)` - a two-element list for a three-descriptor chain ->
  `panic!("Descriptor chain was longer than expected.")` -> `KeBugCheck` from the DPC.
- **Change**: Add `struct DmaSpan<'a>` produced only by
  `DmaBuffer::span(&self, offset: usize, len: usize) -> Option<DmaSpan<'_>>` (one bounds check against
  the buffer's own length, replacing the ad-hoc `t <= meta.as_slice().len()` per arm) and store the
  shape on `InFlight` as `enum Chain { Meta1, Meta2, MetaPlusVenus }`. Give `InFlight` one private
  constructor per shape and one `fn spans(&self) -> (heapless::Vec<&[u8], 2>, &mut [u8])` (or a
  `[&[u8]; 2]` + count - it must be a fixed-size array, never a `Vec`, because it is built under the
  spinlock) used by **both** `add` and `pop_used`, so the two call sites are literally the same code.
  Two constraints the current code relies on and that the helper must preserve verbatim: the arm
  selection must be identical on the enqueue and drain sides, and the response offset must stay
  `in0_len + in1_len` (all three shapes depend on it, including `drain_used`'s `resp_type` read at
  `gpu.rs:1349-1350`).
- **Static guarantee**: Real: the chain shape becomes a single exhaustively-matched value instead of a
  three-field encoding, adding a shape is a compile error until both sides handle it, and the four
  `from_raw_parts` blocks collapse to one function.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the spans alias memory the device may write concurrently (the response span) -
  inherent to virtio, not encodable. It stays as one documented `unsafe` inside
  `DmaBuffer::span`/`InFlight::spans`.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit: `DmaSpan` + `Chain` + the three enqueues + the drain. No branch
  changes, so the diff must show no new `if`.
- **Risk**: medium. A wrong offset here corrupts the used-ring bookkeeping and the failure mode is the
  bugcheck this item exists to prevent. Convert one enqueue path at a time locally, but land as one
  commit so the drain is never half-converted.
- **Validation**: `ASYNC_SUBMIT_COUNT == ASYNC_COMPLETE_COUNT` and
  `ASYNC_CTRL_COUNT == ASYNC_CTRL_COMPLETE_COUNT` still track across a desktop session plus one Fire
  Strike run; `DRAIN_BAD_TOKEN`, `CTRL_TIMEOUT_COUNT` and `PARKED_LEAKS` do not move; escape round-trip
  latency (the existing submit/escape timing counters) unchanged.

### R612. Scope `SyncWaitBlock` so it cannot be registered uninitialized or moved

- **Finding**: x-ordering-09.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:544-551` (`new_zeroed`), `:558-562` (`unsafe fn init`),
  `:564-576` (`is_done`, `copy_resp`), `:1049-1056` (`enqueue_sync` - a **safe** fn taking
  `NonNull<SyncWaitBlock>`), `:1352-1373` (the drain writes `resp`, stores `done` `Release` and calls
  `KeSetEvent` through the raw pointer, under the device spinlock at DISPATCH). Call sites:
  `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:249-252` (`ctrl_roundtrip`) and `:1531-1534` (`wait_fence`).
- **Today**: both call sites do `new_zeroed()` -> `unsafe { init() }` -> `NonNull::from(&mut block)` and
  hand that pointer to the transport. Three invariants - initialized before registration, never moved
  after, always deregistered before the frame dies - are carried by comments. A KEVENT dispatcher header
  is self-referential, so a move after `init` corrupts the wait list silently.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: `let mut b = SyncWaitBlock::new_zeroed(); let p = NonNull::from(&mut b);
  enqueue_sync(.., p);` - registering an uninitialized dispatcher header - compiles today with **zero**
  `unsafe`, because `enqueue_sync` and `fence_wait_prepare` are safe fns. So does returning the block
  from a helper (moving it) between `init` and registration.
- **Change**: Replace the three-step dance with a scoped constructor
  `SyncWaitBlock::with<R>(f: impl FnOnce(&WaitBlockRef<'_>) -> R) -> R` that zeroes, `init`s in place on
  `with`'s own frame, and runs the closure with a `WaitBlockRef` exposing only `as_ptr()`, `is_done()`
  and `copy_resp()`. Make `new_zeroed` and `init` private. `ctrl_roundtrip`'s body moves inside the
  closure as-is; `wait_fence`'s body must move too, including its `full_retries` loop and its four early
  returns (all of which become returns from the closure, so the abandon/cancel epilogue must be the last
  statement of the closure rather than after it).
- **Static guarantee**: Real for use-before-init and for the move: the value is never nameable by the
  caller, so neither state is expressible. Deregistration still depends on the caller's control flow -
  keep the existing `abandon_sync`/`fence_wait_cancel`-on-timeout logic inside the closure epilogue so a
  single scoped API owns it.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the pointer handed to the transport is still raw and is written from DISPATCH on
  another CPU; that cross-IRQL aliasing is inherent and stays behind the transport's existing SAFETY
  note at `gpu.rs:1353-1359`.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit: add `with` + `WaitBlockRef`, convert both call sites, privatize
  `new_zeroed`/`init`.
- **Risk**: medium. `wait_fence` has four early returns and a retry loop; a return that escapes the
  closure without running the epilogue leaks a registered waiter pointing at a dead frame - the exact
  failure the type is meant to prevent. Verify by inspection that every `return` inside the new closure
  is preceded by (or falls through to) the cancel path.
- **Validation**: `CTRL_TIMEOUT_COUNT` and `FENCE_WAIT_TIMEOUTS` stay 0 across a full DWM session; an
  escape-heavy workload (DXVK app start, 20x) shows unchanged escape round-trip latency and
  `PARKED_LEAKS` 0.

### R613. Replace the sync token/bool pair with a `SyncTicket` and a three-valued outcome

- **Finding**: k-gputransport-13. BUG (a success verdict derived from the absence of evidence).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:1049-1118` (`enqueue_sync` returns `Result<u16, ..>`),
  `:1582-1595` (`abandon_sync`, with the fall-through `true` at `:1594`), `:1346-1373` (the drain
  signals then `swap_remove`s, which is why token reuse implies the waiter was signaled),
  `:517-526` + `:544-576` (`SyncWaitBlock`). Sole caller:
  `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:279-292` (`unwrap_or(true)` then unconditional `block.copy_resp`).
- **Today**: three values - the returned `u16` token, the `NonNull<SyncWaitBlock>`, and the block's own
  pinned stack storage - must be kept in sync by the caller across enqueue / PASSIVE wait / abandon.
  `abandon_sync`'s fall-through returns `true` ("already completed, treat as success") for **every** case
  that is not an exact `(token, Sync, same-waiter)` match, including a token now owned by a different
  command and a kind mismatch; the caller then runs `block.copy_resp(resp_out)` on a block that may
  never have been written. Today that is safe only because (a) a token cannot be re-issued until its
  chain is popped, which implies the old waiter was signaled, and (b) `new_zeroed` leaves `resp`
  all-zero and `0` is not a `RESP_OK` code, so `ctrl_roundtrip_ok` still errors out - i.e. correctness
  rests on a virtio-ring property and a zero-init accident, neither stated at this function.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: currently unreachable, but T1a's fail-fast transport policy is exactly
  what opens it: any change that removes or parks an in-flight entry **without** signaling its `Sync`
  waiter makes `abandon_sync` tell a timed-out waiter its command SUCCEEDED and hand it a never-written
  response buffer. Confirm T1a's implementation sets `done` + `KeSetEvent` for every `Sync` waiter it
  drops; if it does not, this item must land before it, not after.
- **Change**: `enqueue_sync` returns a non-`Copy`, non-`Clone` `SyncTicket { token: u16 }`;
  `fn abandon_sync(&mut self, ticket: SyncTicket, block: NonNull<SyncWaitBlock>) -> SyncOutcome` consumes
  it, and `enum SyncOutcome { AlreadyCompleted, Abandoned, NotOurs }` replaces the bool.
  `ctrl_roundtrip` maps `AlreadyCompleted` to today's success-plus-`copy_resp` path, `Abandoned` to
  `CTRL_TIMEOUT_COUNT` + `Err(VirtioError::Timeout)` (unchanged), and `NotOurs` to
  `record_named_bytes(b"CtNotOurs", token) + Err(VirtioError::DeviceError)` **without** `copy_resp` -
  that is the one behavior delta, and it converts a silent read of an unwritten buffer into a counted
  error. Also make `SyncWaitBlock`'s construction single-phase via R612's scoped constructor (land R612
  first: its closure epilogue is where `abandon_sync` is called from).
- **Static guarantee**: Real for both halves: the ticket cannot be duplicated or reused after
  abandonment (`SyncTicket` is move-only), and the ambiguous bool becomes three named cases the caller
  must match exhaustively. Rust cannot prove a stack value never moves without `Pin`, so the block's
  address stability stays a convention - R612 removes the "forgot to call `init`" state, which is the
  encodable part.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the registered pointer's validity across the PASSIVE wait still depends on the
  caller not returning before deregistering - a stack-lifetime property no token can encode (R612
  constrains it structurally, which is why the two land together).
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit: `SyncTicket` + `SyncOutcome` + `abandon_sync` + the single
  `ctrl_roundtrip` call site.
- **Risk**: medium. `NotOurs` is a new error population. If T1a's fail-fast policy *does* drop entries
  without signaling, this commit converts a silent bogus success into a visible `DeviceError`, which is
  correct but will surface as new escape failures - check `CtNotOurs` before concluding the transport
  regressed.
- **Validation**: `CTRL_TIMEOUT_COUNT` does not move across a desktop session; `CtNotOurs` must be
  **absent** after boot + DWM composite + Fire Strike + DOOM (the tranche's gate for this item); escape
  round-trip latency unchanged.

### R614. Express the PASSIVE-only contract of `virtio::ctrl` as a proof token

- **LANDED 2026-07-27 — its own tranche, its own KMD image (`22.22.186.0`, 8 commits), gate
  PASSED.** See `ROADMAP.md` item 7b for the result. Three parts of the "Change" and
  "Validation" text below were WRONG and were deliberately not followed; they are left in place
  so the reasoning is auditable, but do not copy them:
  1. `&PassiveLevel` → implemented **BY VALUE**. A reference to a ZST is a real 8-byte pointer
     per frame, and the token threads through the boot chain that had 368 bytes of headroom.
     Measured before/after on the built image: every frame byte-for-byte unchanged.
  2. `debug_assert!(KeGetCurrentIrql() == PASSIVE_LEVEL)` → implemented as a **counted refusal**
     (`IrqlBad`). `kmd_render`'s `[profile.dev]` does not disable debug-assertions and cargo-make
     ships that profile, so the assert would have been a live `KeBugCheck` inside a DDI — the
     class R601 spent four commits removing — and `verify-no-panics` greps only
     `.unwrap()`/`.expect(`, so it would not have caught it. The "a debug build with the
     assertion must survive…" validation line is therefore also wrong: the assertion is live in
     the SHIPPED build, and what the gate actually checks is that `IrqlBad` reads 0.
  3. "33 signatures plus caller groups; the compiler finds every site" → ~130 sites, and only
     after re-scoping from the venus layer outward per the note below. Straight from `ctrl`
     inward it is ~190.
- **RE-SCOPED, NOT DECLINED — owner decision 2026-07-27 (reversing the same day's decline):
  worth implementing, as its own tranche and its own KMD image.** The effort estimate below ("33 signatures plus caller groups; the compiler finds every site")
  is wrong by roughly 6x. Measured against the tree at KMD 22.22.184.0 the change is **~190
  sites**: 34 `virtio::ctrl` entry points, **95 `VenusClient`/`VenusRing` methods**, 64 external
  `ctrl::` call sites and 23 `with_venus_client` sites. The item's own "Where" section does not
  mention `venus.rs`, and that is the omission: `venus.rs` sits BETWEEN the DDIs and
  `virtio::ctrl`, and every one of its methods transitively reaches `ctrl::sleep_ms` through
  `ring_wait_until`, so the token has to thread through all of them. There is no shortcut —
  putting the token only on the `with_venus_client` gateway (the single gateway to
  `&mut VenusClient`) still leaves the 35 `ctrl::` call sites inside `venus.rs` without one, and
  minting a token at each of those is exactly the laundering the token exists to prevent.
  The change is pure type-level (identical counters, identical desktop), so the cost buys no
  behaviour — only the guarantee. Two findings from the T4a session that the item text does not
  have, and that make it tractable:
  (1) **All 34 entry points really are PASSIVE-only**, including the four `_async` ones — they
  look like fire-and-forget enqueues but every one calls `reap_parked` and `DmaBuffer::new`
  (`MmAllocateContiguousMemory`), so the token can be required uniformly with no exceptions.
  (2) The 95-method venus problem is avoidable: `with_venus_client` is the ONLY gateway to
  `&mut VenusClient`, so requiring the token THERE and storing one in `VenusRing` at bring-up
  replaces ~95 threaded parameters with one structural claim, taking the change from ~190 sites
  to ~130. Re-scope it from the venus layer outward, not from `ctrl` inward.
- **Finding**: k-ctrlsubmit-13.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:19` (the module comment "every function in this module MUST
  be called at PASSIVE_LEVEL"), `:147-153` (`sleep_ms` -> `KeDelayExecutionThread`), `:157-191`
  (`wait_block` -> `KeWaitForSingleObject`), `:240` (`DmaBuffer::new` inside `ctrl_roundtrip`);
  `kmd_render/src/virtio/hal.rs:36-39` (the type-level note that `DmaBuffer::new`/`drop` require
  PASSIVE: `MmAllocateContiguousMemory`/`MmFreeContiguousMemory`). 33 `pub`/`pub(crate)` fns in the
  module (`grep -c '^pub fn \|^pub(crate) fn ' ctrl.rs`). The hazard already hand-managed once:
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:880-905` defers `SetVidPnSourceAddress` to a PASSIVE continuation
  precisely for this reason, and that continuation calls `ctrl::set_scanout_blob` at `:1008`.
- **Today**: 33 public entry points sleep, wait on KEVENTs, or allocate contiguous DMA memory, and their
  only protection is one module-level prose comment. They are called from DDIs with mixed IRQL
  contracts - escape, BuildPagingBuffer, CreateAllocation, the HPD worker, StartDevice/StopDevice, and
  display paths whose own DDIs can be entered at DIRQL. There is no runtime assertion either, so a
  violation is not even loud.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: any code added to `dxgkddi_set_vidpn_source_address` (documented
  callable at DIRQL, which is why `display.rs` defers) that calls `ctrl::set_scanout_blob` or
  `ctrl::resource_flush` directly instead of going through the deferred PASSIVE worker: compiles,
  links, ships, and either deadlocks at DISPATCH on a KEVENT wait or calls
  `MmAllocateContiguousMemory` above APC_LEVEL.
- **Change**: New `kmd_render/src/irql.rs` with a zero-sized `pub struct PassiveLevel { _p:
  PhantomData<*const ()> }` (so `!Send`/`!Sync`), constructible only by
  `pub unsafe fn assume() -> PassiveLevel` carrying a `debug_assert!(KeGetCurrentIrql() == PASSIVE_LEVEL)`.
  Thread `&PassiveLevel` through `virtio::ctrl`'s public entry points (they already all take
  `&AdapterContext`, so it is one extra parameter) and through `DmaBuffer::new`, `sleep_ms` and
  `wait_block`. Each DDI whose MSDN annotation guarantees PASSIVE mints one at the top with a
  `// SAFETY:` naming that annotation.
- **Static guarantee**: Real, with an honest limit that must be stated in the module doc: the token does
  not *prove* the IRQL (only `KeGetCurrentIrql` can) - it relocates the assertion from one module-wide
  prose comment to one audited `unsafe { PassiveLevel::assume() }` per DDI entry point, and makes every
  PASSIVE-only helper unreachable from code that has no token. That is the same trade the codebase
  already accepts for `WddmNotifyGuard` (`adapter.rs:1228-1234`). Do **not** add a `DispatchLevel` token
  in the same change - the value is concentrated on the PASSIVE-only side.
- **Remaining unsafe**: `PassiveLevel::assume()` is irreducibly unsafe, one call per DDI entry point,
  each with a `// SAFETY:` citing the DDI's documented IRQL.
- **Atomic boundary**: Commit 1: `irql.rs` plus threading through the internal primitives only
  (`ctrl_roundtrip`, `ctrl_roundtrip_ok`, `sleep_ms`, `wait_block`, `reap_parked`) - no DDI churn.
  Commits 2..n: one caller group each (escape, paging, allocation, display worker, start/stop). Land
  after R611/R612/R613, which reshape `ctrl_roundtrip`'s body and `DmaBuffer`'s API.
- **Risk**: low mechanically (33 signatures plus caller groups; the compiler finds every site), but the
  effort is L and it touches every DDI file - schedule it last in the tranche so a partial revert does
  not strand other items.
- **Validation**: Pure type-level change: the driver must produce identical counters and an identical
  desktop. A debug build with the `KeGetCurrentIrql` assertion must survive a full DWM session plus Fire
  Strike plus a `pnputil /restart-device` cycle without firing - that is the real evidence, because it
  checks the `assume()` sites rather than the plumbing.

### R615. Name the "abandon the pending fence FIFO" operation and count what it drops

- **Finding**: k-ctrlsubmit-14. BUG (a TDR epoch discards N fences and nothing counts N).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/scheduler.rs:115-119` (`dxgkddi_reset_engine`: locked flush then
  `reset.LastAbortedFenceId = guard.completed_fence()`),
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/submit_command.rs:560-566` (`dxgkddi_preempt_command`: locked flush then
  `DMA_PREEMPTED`, and the only copy of the one-critical-section rationale at `:552-559`), `:580-582`
  (`dxgkddi_reset_from_timeout`: locked flush, no packet).
  `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:1850-1854` (`preempt_flush` returns the dropped count). All three call
  sites discard it: `let _`, `let _dropped`, `let _`.
- **Today**: three DDIs perform the same "take the notify lock, drop every pending WDDM fence" step and
  then do three different things afterwards, with the copy-pasted step named nowhere. The long comment
  explaining why the flush and the notification packet must be one critical section (bugcheck 0x119/1,
  "expected 0x17a, received 0x17b") lives only in `PreemptCommand`, where a reader of `ResetEngine` will
  not see it. And nothing counts how many fences a TDR epoch dropped, which is exactly the number a TDR
  post-mortem wants.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a for the duplication. For the reporting: `ResetEngine` with N
  pending fences discards all N, reports `LastAbortedFenceId` = the completed watermark *below* them,
  and returns `STATUS_SUCCESS`; nothing records N.
- **Change**: Add `fn abandon_pending_submissions(adapter: &AdapterContext, outcome: AbandonOutcome) -> u32`
  in `submit_command.rs` that takes the notify guard once, calls `preempt_flush(guard)`, records
  `record_named_bytes(b"AbnDrop", n)` (plus a monotonic `ABANDONED_FENCES` atomic so the count is
  cumulative), and then executes
  `enum AbandonOutcome { Silent, Preempted { fence: u32 }, ReportLastAborted<'a> { out: &'a mut UINT } }`
  **inside the same guard**. Move the one-critical-section rationale onto it. Call it from all three
  DDIs. Do **not** change the value written to `LastAbortedFenceId`: keep `guard.completed_fence()` until
  `DXGKARG_RESETENGINE`'s exact semantics are checked against the WDK header, and record that open
  question in the comment.
- **Static guarantee**: `AbandonOutcome` makes the three scheduler epochs exhaustive and forces any
  future TDR-adjacent DDI to declare which notification it owes; today the choice is invisible. The "one
  critical section" rule is already carried by `WddmNotifyGuard`, so this is about naming the operation,
  not re-proving the lock.
- **Remaining unsafe**: building and delivering the `DMA_PREEMPTED` packet stays unsafe (bindgen union
  arm plus the DIRQL callback through `DxgkCbSynchronizeExecution`).
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit; no signature changes outside `submit_command.rs` and `scheduler.rs`.
- **Risk**: low. The one thing that could break is passing `&mut reset.LastAbortedFenceId` into a
  closure that runs under the spinlock - it must be written inside the guard exactly as today, not after.
- **Validation**: `PREEMPT_COUNT` unchanged for the same workload; `AbnDrop`/`ABANDONED_FENCES` read 0
  on a clean DWM session and **move** under a deliberately induced TDR; no bugcheck 0x119/1 across a TDR
  test (kill the host renderer mid-frame), and `DMA_STALE_SKIP_COUNT` unchanged.

### R616. Express every retry budget in milliseconds (part A only)

- **Finding**: k-ctrlsubmit-07 part A. Part B (the progress event) is explicitly deferred.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:59` (`SYNC_ROUNDTRIP_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`), `:62`
  (`ENQUEUE_RETRY_MAX = 5_000`), `:65` (`WAIT_FENCE_MAX_MS = 120_000`), `:67`
  (`MAP_BUSY_RETRY_MAX = 30_000`). Four retry loops, not three: `:266-274` (`ctrl_roundtrip`),
  `:1428-1437` (`submit_venus_async` - missed by the source finding), `:1164-1178` and `:1234-1248`
  (the two map-busy loops), plus the unnamed `full_retries > 1_000` at `:1546-1553` (owned by R604).
  `sleep_ms` at `:147-153`. `wait_block` at `:157-191` is a bounded KEVENT wait with an
  interrupt-loss re-drain - **KEEP**, it is a safety contract.
- **Today**: two of the four sibling constants are millisecond budgets and two are bare retry counts
  that only *happen* to equal 5 s and 30 s because the sleep is hard-coded to 1 ms, and one budget is an
  unnamed literal. Worse, `KeDelayExecutionThread` with a 1 ms relative timeout rounds up to the system
  timer granularity (~15.6 ms by default), so "`ENQUEUE_RETRY_MAX` x 1 ms" is not a 5 s budget at all -
  it can be minutes of thread residency on a DWM present thread under sustained backpressure. Defect
  class: a units mismatch that makes every reader over-estimate how fast the driver gives up.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a.
- **Change**: Introduce `struct Budget { deadline_ms: u64 }` with `fn new(ms: u64)`,
  `fn expired(&self) -> bool` and `fn elapsed_ms(&self) -> u64`, and make the four loops take one.
  Rename `ENQUEUE_RETRY_MAX` -> `ENQUEUE_RETRY_MAX_MS` and `MAP_BUSY_RETRY_MAX` ->
  `MAP_BUSY_MAX_MS` keeping the same numeric values (5 000 and 30 000), and derive the iteration count
  from the budget rather than the reverse. State the timer-granularity caveat in one comment on
  `sleep_ms`. Behavior is preserved exactly: same numbers, same sleeps, same failure statuses. **Do not**
  land part B (an adapter-owned progress `KEVENT` set by `drain_used`) in this tranche: it changes wake
  ordering on the DWM present path and needs `QUEUE_FULL_RETRIES`, the UMD frame-gate average (~0.48 ms)
  and the DComp probe fps measured before and after.
- **Static guarantee**: A single `Budget` newtype means a retry count can no longer masquerade as a time
  budget, and the four loops share one expiry predicate. Modest and honest - the event replacement is a
  runtime change, not a type change.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit: `Budget` + the four constants + the four loops. R604 owns the fifth
  (`full_retries`) site and must land first so this commit does not touch `wait_fence`'s table-full arm.
- **Risk**: low. The failure mode is an off-by-one in the derived iteration count, changing when
  `VirtioError::QueueFull` is returned.
- **Validation**: `QUEUE_FULL_RETRIES` must show the same order of magnitude for the same workload (Fire
  Strike plus DOOM plus DWM idle); zero `QueueFull` escalations out of the escape path; the UMD's
  measured steady-state frame-gate average and the ~63 fps DComp probe must not regress - if either
  moves, this commit did more than rename constants.

### R617. Classify the allocation backing once, and build a complete descriptor

- **Finding**: k-alloc-01.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/create_allocation.rs:836-1303` (`create_one`), `:905-911` (the four
  booleans), the five-arm chain at `:911-939` (adopt), `:939-962` (linear primary), `:963-1005` (OPTIMAL
  GDI texture), `:1006-1043` (KMD standard blob), `:1043-1069` (raw HOST3D blob); the in-place patches at
  `:947-951`, `:987-993`, `:1024-1027`; the `venus_alloc_size` fallback at `:1086-1088`; the private-data
  write-back at `:1089-1119`; `AllocationContext` construction at `:1142-1179`; the segment/flag policy
  at `:1190-1244`. Mutual exclusivity today comes from
  `GetStandardAllocationDriverData`'s `if/else if` at `:1806-1812`.
- **Today**: the backing class is encoded as four booleans (`adopt_supplied_resource`, `is_primary`,
  `is_optimal_gdi_texture`, `ap.kind == STANDARD`) evaluated as an ordered `if`/`else` chain, and each
  arm mutates the shared `meta`/`ap` locals in place (`meta.pitch`, `meta.plane_offset`,
  `meta.venus_alloc_size`, `meta.memory_type_index`, `meta.dxgi_format`, `ap.size`). 100-470 lines later
  the same locals are copied into `AllocationContext`, written back into dxgkrnl's private-data buffer,
  and used to compute the VidMm segment policy. Nothing states which fields each arm must set. Defect
  class: the per-arm field obligation behind the historical pitch shear (`width*4` = 7584 vs the real
  7680) and the import-size mismatches, enforced only by prose.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: not constructible by any current caller - the arms are mutually
  exclusive. The failure is a maintenance sequence: add a sixth arm, or reorder the
  `is_optimal_gdi_texture` arm above `is_primary`, and forget `meta.venus_alloc_size = blob.size`. The
  code compiles, `CreateAllocation` returns `STATUS_SUCCESS`, and the write-back publishes a descriptor
  whose `venus_alloc_size` silently falls back to `ap.size` while the real `vkAllocateMemory` size
  differs - the cross-process opener then imports with the wrong exact size and the surface is refused
  or MMU-faults.
- **Change**: Add
  `enum AllocationBacking { AdoptedUmdResource { resource_id, take_ownership }, KmdLinearPrimary { width, height }, KmdOptimalGdiTexture { width, height, dxgi_format, bind_flags }, KmdStandardBuffer { size, primary }, RawHost3dBlob { ctx_id, blob_mem, blob_flags, blob_id, size } }`
  produced by one pure
  `fn classify(&HeliosWddmAllocPrivate, &HeliosWddmAllocMeta, resource_associated: bool) -> Result<AllocationBacking, NTSTATUS>`,
  and one `fn build(adapter, backing) -> Result<CreatedBacking, NTSTATUS>` whose return
  `struct CreatedBacking { resource_id, venus_memory_id, venus_image_id, pitch, plane_offset,
  dxgi_format, venus_alloc_size, memory_type_index, blob_size }` has **no `Option` fields and no
  `Default`**. Arms that do not change a field pass the incoming `meta` value through explicitly (the
  adopt arm returns `pitch = meta.pitch`) - that pass-through is the point: each arm must state its
  answer for every field. `meta`/`ap` are then updated at exactly one site, immediately before the
  write-back.
- **Static guarantee**: Real, but only under two conditions: `CreatedBacking` must have no `Default` and
  must not be field-wise mutated after construction. Then the compiler forces every `build` arm to
  produce a complete descriptor, and adding a class fails to compile until it is handled. `classify` is a
  pure function over `helios_protocol` types, so it is unit-testable in the Linux host build (the
  protocol crate already builds on both platforms) - that is what makes this tranche's biggest rewrite
  provable rather than argued.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the private-data pointer read that produces `ap`/`meta` (runtime-owned buffer,
  no alignment guarantee) stays unsafe; it is confined to the parsing module and already bounds-checked.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit. It is a ~470-line rewrite of the hottest allocation path and cannot
  be split without leaving `meta` half-patched in place. Every existing diag code must be byte-identical:
  `0x0C01_0010|kind`, `0x0C01_0020`, `0x0C01_00E0/E1/E3/E4/E5`, `GdiOFmt`, `GdiOImg` 0xE1/0xE2,
  `0x0C39_xxxx`, `0x0C3A_1000|resid`, `0x0C3B_xxxx`, and every returned NTSTATUS
  (`STATUS_NO_MEMORY`, not `STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL` - `0xC0000001` is not in the DDI's legal return set).
- **Risk**: medium. The specific breakage is a field the new `build` arm forgets to pass through where
  the old code left the incoming `meta` value untouched - which produces exactly the class of bug this
  change exists to prevent. Diff each arm's field list against the corresponding old arm line by line.
- **Validation**: Host-target unit tests for `classify` covering all five arms plus the
  `PRIMARY | OPTIMAL_GDI_TEXTURE` combination (which must remain unreachable). On the guest, boot with
  `DisplayHalf=1`: the S-ring must show the same `0x0C01_0010|kind` / `0x0C01_0020` / resource-id
  sequence per allocation, the same `GdiOImg` / `0x0C01_00E*` refusal codes for the same inputs,
  `ScSet`/`ScFlu`/`ScRid` still moving, `ScanoutDiag` absent with `VpSA=1`/`ScSet=1`, and
  `helios_paintcap` still capturing a composited desktop with a trail-free cursor.

### R618. Carry the provenance of the backing size, and cross-check it before trusting it

- **Finding**: k-alloc-17.
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/ddi/create_allocation.rs:1135-1140` (`bar_seg_id` + `bar_eligible`),
  `:1122-1134` (`size = round_up_page(ap.size)` plus the comment contemplating adopted BAR eligibility),
  `:297-302` (`PagingAllocInfo::size = ctx.size`), `:911-939` (the adopt arm leaves
  `venus_memory_id = 0`, which is the only thing keeping adopted allocations out today);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/cpu_host_aperture.rs:189` (`blob_pages` from `alloc.size`) and `:198-203` (the
  `n != blob_pages` refusal, `BAR_AP_ERR_PARTIAL`); `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:1220-1224`
  (`map_blob_at` derives `map_len` from `blob_lookup` - a **different** source).
- **Today**: `PagingAllocInfo::size` is `round_up_page(ap.size)`, and `ap.size` is ICD-supplied for
  adopted allocations - it is overwritten with a host-authoritative value only in the KMD-created arms.
  `MapCpuHostAperture`'s whole-allocation refusal computes `blob_pages` from that size while
  `map_blob_at` maps whatever length the *tracked blob* size implies, so the refusal compares dxgkrnl's
  page count against a number of different provenance. This cannot bite today only because
  `bar_eligible` requires `venus_memory_id != 0`, which only the KMD-created arms set - i.e. the safety
  of an aperture size check rests on an incidental property of an unrelated boolean.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: make adopted DEVICE_MEMORY allocations BAR-eligible - explicitly
  contemplated by the comment at `:1129-1134` - and a UMD reporting `ap.size` larger than the real blob
  receives an aperture assignment of `blob_pages` pages while the map covers only the real blob length;
  the CPU view's tail then addresses unbacked window offsets, the silent-content-loss class the
  `cpu_host_aperture` module doc exists to prevent.
- **Change**: Add `enum BackingSize { HostAuthoritative(u64), CreatorClaimed(u64) }` to the descriptor
  produced by R617's `build` (the KMD-created arms return `HostAuthoritative`, the adopt and raw-blob
  arms return `CreatorClaimed`), and set `bar_eligible` only for `HostAuthoritative` - which reproduces
  today's population exactly, because that is precisely the `venus_memory_id != 0` set. In
  `cpu_host_aperture`, **first** add a counter-only cross-check comparing `blob_pages`-from-`ctx.size`
  against `blob_lookup(resource_id)`'s page count (`blob_lookup` is already used on this path at
  `:162`, so it is DISPATCH-safe) recording `record_named_bytes(b"ChSzMm", pages_delta)` on
  disagreement. Do **not** switch the authoritative source until that counter proves the two agree on
  every boot: a host-rounded vs page-rounded difference would change the `BAR_AP_ERR_PARTIAL` refusal
  population and make this a behavior change.
- **Static guarantee**: Real: "this size came from the host" becomes a type-level fact instead of an
  inference from `venus_memory_id != 0`, and the aperture path can require `HostAuthoritative` in its
  signature. Depends on R617, which is where the descriptor is constructed.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none.
- **Atomic boundary**: One commit: the provenance enum threaded from R617's `CreatedBacking` into
  `AllocationContext`/`PagingAllocInfo`, plus the `blob_lookup` cross-check counter. Refusal behavior is
  unchanged for today's population.
- **Risk**: low, provided `bar_eligible`'s truth table is verified identical before and after: it must
  stay `HostAuthoritative && !is_optimal_gdi_texture && bar_seg_id.is_some()`.
- **Validation**: `ChSzMm` must be **absent** across a boot with GDI acceleration and the display half
  enabled; `BAR_AP_ERR_PARTIAL`, `BAR_AP_ERR_ALLOC`, `BAR_AP_IRQL_ACK`/`DEFER` and the `ChEp`/`ChMn`
  breadcrumbs unchanged; `helios_paintcap` still shows a composited desktop (the GDI executor is the
  consumer of this window).

### R619. Make the duplicate-map guard authoritative at commit time

- **Finding**: k-alloc-14. BUG (a TOCTOU across two lock acquisitions leaves a live user VA over an
  unbacked window offset).
- **Where**: `kmd_render/src/mapping.rs:101-109` (`contains` - O(n) under
  `KeAcquireSpinLockRaiseToDpc`), `:116-...` (`insert`), `:155-165` (`take_one_for`), `:169-182`
  (`take_for_resource`), `:39-47` (`MAX_MAPPINGS = 8192`);
  `kmd_render/src/ddi/escape.rs:535-537` (the check), `:542-572` (`map_blob_prepare` ->
  `map_io_pages_to_user` -> `insert`, the second acquisition, with the table-full undo at `:565-572`);
  `kmd_render/src/device.rs:96-100` (the O(n^2) drain loop). Idempotence facts:
  `kmd_render/src/virtio/ctrl.rs:1156-1201` (`map_blob_prepare` returns the existing mapping),
  `kmd_render/src/virtio/gpu.rs:2076-2086` (`blob_map_begin` returns `Mapped(existing offset)` or
  `Busy`, never re-places).
- **Today**: the duplicate-map guard is check-then-act - `contains` (lock 1), then
  `map_blob_prepare` + MDL + user map, then `insert` (lock 2). `DxgkDdiEscape` is not serialized by
  dxgkrnl, so two threads on one device handle can both pass `contains` and both `insert`. The
  consequence is **not** a moved window offset (`map_blob_prepare` is idempotent and
  `blob_map_begin` never re-places a mapped blob, so both threads get the same offset): it is a
  duplicate registration - two MDLs and two user VAs over one blob, two entries with the same
  `(owner, resource_id)`. Every operation except `insert` is also a linear scan at DISPATCH, and the
  `DestroyDevice` drain is O(n^2) comparisons plus n lock acquisitions.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: two ICD threads on one D3DKMT device call `HELIOS_ESCAPE_MAP_BLOB`
  for the same `resource_id` concurrently: both observe `contains == false`, both obtain the same gpa,
  both build an MDL and map a user view, and both `insert`. A later `RELEASE_BLOB` pops one via
  `take_for_resource` while `release_blob_for_owner` tears down the host window mapping, leaving the
  second user VA live over a window offset that is no longer backed - silent content loss until
  `DestroyDevice` reclaims it.
- **Change**: (a) Add
  `fn insert_unique(&self, owner, resource_id, user_va, mdl) -> InsertResult { Inserted, Duplicate, Full }`
  performing the scan and the push under **one** acquisition. `escape_map_blob` keeps the cheap
  `contains` pre-check but treats `Duplicate` at commit time as the authoritative refusal, unmapping the
  just-created view exactly as the `Full` path already does at `escape.rs:565-572`, and recording
  `record_named_bytes(b"MapDup", resource_id)`. (b) Add
  `fn drain_for(&self, owner, out: &mut [(u64, usize)]) -> usize` that pops several of one owner's
  entries per acquisition, and use it from `device.rs:96-100`.
- **Static guarantee**: Return a move-only `UserMapping { user_va: u64, mdl: PMDL }` from
  `blob_map::map_io_pages_to_user` and make `insert_unique` **consume** it, handing it back on refusal,
  so "unmap exactly what you failed to insert" stops being a manual pairing. It must be `#[must_use]`
  and must **not** implement `Drop`: `MmUnmapLockedPages` is legal only at PASSIVE in the creating
  process (`blob_map.rs:129-131`), so an RAII `Drop` could fire in the wrong context and bugcheck 0x76.
  The guarantee is therefore "the pair cannot be split or duplicated", not "it cannot be forgotten".
- **Remaining unsafe**: `MmUnmapLockedPages` must still run at PASSIVE in the creating process; the
  owning type can document but not enforce process context.
- **Atomic boundary**: Commit 1: `insert_unique` + the commit-time refusal in `escape.rs`. Commit 2: the
  batched drain. Commit 3 (optional): the move-only `UserMapping`.
- **Risk**: medium. Commit 1 changes an escape's failure population: a legitimate ICD that maps a blob
  twice (today refused by `contains`, tomorrow refused later and after the host round-trip) now performs
  a wasted map/unmap. Confirm `MapDup` stays 0 before assuming that path is dead.
- **Validation**: `out_mappings_high_water` / `out_mapping_full_rejects` (`escape.rs:369-373`) unchanged
  for a normal session, `MAP_PAGES_FAILS` unchanged, `MapDup` 0 in steady state (Fire Strike plus DOOM
  plus a DXVK app start/stop loop). For commit 2, measure `DestroyDevice` teardown wall time for a
  process holding >1000 mappings (the DOOM level-load case that forced `MAX_MAPPINGS` to 8192) before
  and after.

### Minor items

Low-severity items whose fix is small enough that the argument is the diff. Each is independent of the
others unless noted.

- **k-venus-13** - poison the reply word so an unwritten reply cannot decode as the previous one.
  **Where**: `kmd_render/src/virtio/venus.rs:1046-1066` (`ring_command_reply`), `:4622-4624`
  (`reply_map.zero()` runs exactly once, at bring-up); the five inconsistent echo checks at `:1433-1436`
  (nonzero-only), `:2373-2377` (strict compare), `:1946-1947` / `:1980-1981` / `:2030-2035` (adopt).
  **Change**: store `0xFFFF_FFFF` (not a legal `VkCommandTypeEXT`) into reply offset 0 via the existing
  `store_u32_seqcst` immediately before `publish_and_notify`, so an unwritten reply fails every caller's
  existing command-type check. Do **not** bundle uniform strict handle validation: tightening the three
  adopt sites is a real behavior change that could break bring-up on a host that legitimately returns a
  different handle - if wanted, add `record_named_bytes(b"VnEchoNe", cmd_type)` while still adopting, and

## T4b - Encode the caps, segment-topology, paging and handle invariants

- **Status**: **LANDED — gate PASSED** (2026-07-27, KMD `22.22.187.0`, 16 commits). 20 items, not
  22: **R716 and R717 were dead on arrival** because `ddi/gdi_blit.rs` no longer exists (T1b
  deleted the whole GDI path under the owner directive, R903 pulled forward), exactly as this
  section's own "Read before starting" note anticipated. **R904 landed FIRST**, per its
  cross-tranche note. Full gate evidence in `ROADMAP.md` item 7c.
  Three corrections this tranche establishes against hardware, all worth carrying forward:
  1. **R702's UB was LIVE, not latent.** This section left open whether 24H2 ever passes a
     short DRIVERCAPS buffer; the `0x01CF` breadcrumb reads **`0x240` = 576 bytes** against a
     592-byte struct, so the `&mut *(pOutputData as *mut DXGK_DRIVERCAPS)` was being constructed
     over a short referent on every AddAdapter. `CapTrunc` = 0 confirms all 540 written bytes fit.
  2. **R705's ordering premise is measured, not assumed.** Moving table construction into
     StartDevice is only sound if StartDevice precedes the first QUERYSEGMENT4. A `DiagLevel=1`
     ring read off the live box shows StartDevice entry/exit (`0x0B00_0001` .. `0x0B00_0004`)
     completing before the first QueryAdapterInfo (`0x0100_0001`), with the segment queries after.
  3. **R715's deciding measurement came back 0.** `PgSm` stayed 0 through a full Fire Strike run —
     the Present-time system-backing mirror never fires — so commit 2 should DELETE the mirror
     rather than build a VidMm page lease for it. That was the evidence this item gated on.
  Four deviations, each argued in its commit message: `KnobName` covers knob reads and the fault
  counter set but not the 478 `record_named_bytes` sites; R706 sub-commit (2) is deferred
  (count-only, by owner decision, since its evidence can only come from this image); R715 commit 2
  is owner-gated; R722's `diag::codes` sweep is skipped in favour of fixing the two collisions
  directly.

This tranche turns the AddAdapter-surface and paging-engine obligations that today live in comments into types: one `WddmSurface` value instead of a nested lever expression copy-pasted at five coupled sites, a per-field bounded writer instead of a `&mut DXGK_DRIVERCAPS` over a short versioned buffer, a validating `SegmentTable` that owns the "a SupportsCpuHostAperture segment must be LAST" rule instead of hand-ordered positional match arms over a `BarSegMode` DWORD, an `EscapeBuf` plus a first-ever read of `DXGKARG_ESCAPE.Flags`, a typed traversal for every dxgkrnl handle, and - on the paging side - a total parse of both command streams (`DXGKARG_BUILDPAGINGBUFFER`'s union and the RenderGdi batch), a guard-based spinlock, a `Passive` proof token, and a `PatchCapacity` token for the validate-before-host-work rule. It sits after T3 because T3 already reshaped `display.rs`'s Present path and installed the `WddmNotifyGuard` branding these items build next to, and after T1a/T1b because two of the defects those tranches fix live in the exact lines edited here (`k-paging-05`'s ungated registry dump at `build_paging_buffer.rs:918`, `k-paging-01`/`06`/`07`/`08` in `gdi_blit.rs`).
