`:1092-1230` (`allocate_memory_blob`, `choose_host_visible_memory_type` 1181, `choose_device_local_memory_type` 1201); `:1231-2538` (~30 object encoders, ending with `destroy_image_on_ring` 2484 / `destroy_buffer_on_ring` 2497 / `cleanup_imported_source_alias` 2510 / `cleanup_borrowed_present_buffer` 2526); `:2540-2803` (import/borrow/ensure caches); `:2805-3411` (five `record_reusable_*` recorders at 2805/2908/3014/3154/3264); `:3413-3756` (`prepare_optimal_scanout_copy`, `prepare_existing_linear_source_copy`, `submit_prepared_image_copy`); `:3757-3782` (`encode_command_buffer_submit`, a pure `Writer` builder); `:3784-3978` (`submit_present_blt`); `:3980-4054` (`probe_present_destination`); `:4056-4185` (`release_present_blits_for_resource`, `destroy_prepared_image_copy`); `:4345-4514` (`allocate_optimal_gdi_image_blob`, `allocate_linear_scanout_image_blob`); `:4516-4572` (`destroy_image`, `free_memory_object`, `free_memory_blob`); `:4588-4994` (`allocate_host_visible_blob`, breadcrumbs `diag(0x0001)`..`diag(0x000D)`). Layering evidence: `kmd_render/src/ddi/display.rs:460-462` reaches `submit_present_blt` through `with_venus_client` inside `DxgkDdiPresent`, and `submit_present_blt` reaches `probe_present_destination` at 3971, which calls `ctrl::map_blob_prepare` and `MmMapIoSpace` under the adapter venus mutex.
- **Today**: every layer of the venus stack is one `impl VenusClient` block (909-4572) in one file, so there is no boundary saying "below here nothing reads the registry, allocates, or blocks" and none saying "above here nothing touches a raw pointer". Verified consequences: the one-shot CPU readback probe runs from the Present DDI path; the memory-type choosers and the `vkCreateDevice` extension tier read `ScanoutDiag` at 4240/4274/4882 (all three of those reads are deleted by T6's x-dup-dead-15 / k-venus-14, so by T8 the diagnostics coupling is registry-free); and the five `KernelMap` accessors are nameable from every policy function in the file. Any new caller inherits the union of all preconditions - PASSIVE only, venus mutex held, bring-up finished, ring not fatal, copy target latched - with nothing recording which apply.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a - structural.
- **Change**: `venus.rs` becomes `venus/mod.rs` (path `crate::virtio::venus::*` unchanged) plus: `venus/protocol.rs` (48-236 constants + `Writer` 717-781 - genuinely adapter-free and the one piece a host unit test can cover); `venus/ring.rs` (`KernelMap` + accessors + `Drop`, `ReplyReader`, the ring layout constants, and 909-1090's transport methods including the `fatal` latch - this module owns the only unchecked MMIO); `venus/commands.rs` (the 1231-2538 encoders + 1092-1230 + `encode_command_buffer_submit` 3757-3782); `venus/present.rs` (the 241-617 present descriptors, the three bounded caches, 2540-2803, the five `record_reusable_*`, `submit_present_blt`, `release_present_blits_for_resource`); `venus/scanout.rs` (3413-3756 + `allocate_optimal_gdi_image_blob` + `allocate_linear_scanout_image_blob` + `destroy_prepared_image_copy`); `venus/diagnostics.rs` (`probe_present_destination` only - `gpu_clear_scanout_image` and `allocate_scanout_image_blob` are deleted by T6, so this module is ~75 lines, and if the owner prefers it can instead live at the bottom of `present.rs` behind the `adapter.present_probe` gate); `venus/bringup.rs` (`allocate_host_visible_blob`, `round_up_page`, `diag`). `ReplyReader` must move with `KernelMap` into `ring.rs` - it borrows `&'a KernelMap`, so it cannot sit in an adapter-free `protocol.rs`. The move commits use additional `impl VenusClient` blocks in the sibling modules with `pub(super)` fields (the encoders read `self.device_id`/`self.queue_id`/`self.reply_map` at ~40 sites); reshaping receivers to take `&mut Ring` is x-ordering-06's work, already done in T4a, and must not be redone here.
- **Static guarantee**: real but narrower than the source finding claims - corrected here. Three of the five `KernelMap` accessors seal to `venus/ring.rs` by module privacy: `load_u32_acquire` (used only at 944, 983, 1013, 1025), `store_u32_seqcst` (942) and `write_ring_buffer` (1016) become unnameable from present/scanout/diagnostics code, which makes k-venus-05's accessor-misuse class unreachable from policy code by construction. `read_byte` cannot be sealed - `probe_present_destination` calls it at 4031-4033 and 4041-4044 - and `KernelMap::new`/`zero` cannot be sealed either, because `allocate_host_visible_blob` constructs and zeroes both mappings at 4606-4624. Those three stay `pub(super)` to the `venus` module; the follow-up narrowing is to give `ring.rs` one `pub(super) fn sample_byte(&self, offset: u64) -> u8` for the probe and a `MappedBlob::new_zeroed` constructor for bring-up, after which `read_byte`/`zero`/`new` become private too. `Writer` in `protocol.rs` genuinely cannot reach `AdapterContext` at all after the move. `ReplyReader` stays coupled to `KernelMap` and gains nothing.
- **Remaining unsafe**: all of it, unchanged - `MmMapIoSpace`/`MmUnmapIoSpace` RAII, the volatile MMIO reads/writes whose bounds are the caller's invariant, the `compiler_fence`/`fence` ordering pairs that mirror `vn_ring`'s producer contract. Only reachability narrows.
- **Atomic boundary**: seven commits, in the order protocol → ring → commands → present → scanout → diagnostics → bringup. Protocol and ring first because everything else depends on their visibility; bringup last because it names types from every other module. Each commit: file move + `mod` declaration + `pub(super)` markers only. The M1 doc fix rides on the ring commit.
- **Risk**: medium. Two concrete hazards: (a) a `pub(super)` field that a sibling module needs is missed, which is a compile error, not a behaviour change - acceptable; (b) an accidental reordering of the `fence`/`compiler_fence` calls relative to the volatile access while re-indenting `write_ring_buffer` or `store_u32_seqcst`, which is a silent host-visibility bug. Diff those two bodies character-for-character.
- **Validation**: a boot with `DiagLevel=1` produces the identical bring-up breadcrumb sequence `0x0D00_0001` … `0x0D00_000D` in the same order (this is the single best proof the 400-line bring-up moved intact); `RING_SUBMIT_COUNT` and `RING_COMPLETE_COUNT` stay equal after a desktop session; `PBPrF` reaches `0x10` exactly once per boot when `PresentProbe` is on and is absent otherwise; the primary is visible via `helios_paintcap` → `Z:\tmp\screen_copy.png`; `ScanoutDiag` absent with `VpSA=1` and `ScSet=1`. Add the T0-style host unit test for `venus/protocol.rs`'s `Writer` (fixed-capacity LE encoding, `bytes_padded` alignment, `header`) in the same commit - it is the only part of this file that can be tested off the VM, and k-venus-02's bound check (T4a) needs it.

### R1105. Split dxvk_bridge.cpp into DXBC, ICD-exports and flip-wait translation units

- **Finding**: u-bridge-12. Sequenced after T7's u-bridge-13, which collapses the two DXBC wrappers and the six shader forwarders - split the deduplicated code, not the duplicated code.
- **Where**: `umd/bridge/dxvk_bridge.cpp:36-42` (DXVK + `dxbc/dxbc_container.h` includes), `:44-49` (D3D11 COM includes), `:51-53` (`dxbc_spv::dxbc::hashDxbcBinary` forward declaration), `:61-345` (loader spelunking `find_export_in_loaded_modules` 64, `find_helios_icd_export` 284, hand-rolled manifest JSON, `read_instance_venus_context_id` 321), `:346-359` (`HeliosVenusScanoutInfo` + its 40-byte `static_assert`), `:361-390` (`HeliosStubAdapter`), `:392-467` (`umd_log_file` 397, `umd_log` 408, `dump_shader_bytecode` 438), `:469-483` (`ShaderBytecode`, `write_le`), `:485-544` (the four venus ICD-export wrappers), `:546-849` (DXBC container synthesis: `encode_signature_entry` 560, `append_signature_chunk` 601, `prepare_shader_bytecode_with_sigs` 680, `…_with_tess_sigs` 738, `prepare_shader_bytecode` 798), `:853-996` (`HeliosCbSignalSyncFromCpu` 857, `HeliosFlipWaitCtx` 868 with the 64-slot latency ring and `latRecordPublish`/`latObserve`, `signalTo`), `:1000-1053` (`HeliosDxvkDeviceImpl`, `presentSyncDisabled` at 1014), `:1055-1393` (resource identity plumbing), `:1395-1585` and `:2112-2188` (shader forwarders; `prepare_shader_bytecode` called at 1400/1426/1452/2117/2143/2169), `:1587-2110` (present path: `present_frame_gate` 1755, `present_sync_publish` 1870), `:2012-2070` (`present_flip_wait_setup`, whose watchdog thread body is the lambda at 2039-2066), `:2072-2110` (`present_flip_wait_arm`); `umd/build.rs:107-127` (the single `cxx_build` with one `.file()` at 109 and the dxbc-spirv include at 118).
- **Today**: one translation unit mixes Win32 module/loader spelunking with a hand-rolled JSON parser, a logger, a registry-gated shader dumper, ~350 lines of DXBC container synthesis that touch no DXVK type and no COM object, a hand-declared WDDM kernel-callback ABI plus a 64-slot latency histogram whose watchdog thread body lives 1150 lines away, DXVK device construction, resource identity plumbing, eight shader forwarders and the present path. Consequences: the DXBC synthesis - the part with the real arithmetic and the real parsing risk (u-bridge-18) - cannot be exercised without linking libdxvk and libhelios_d3d11_static, so it is only ever run on the VM; any change to the loader/manifest code recompiles everything that includes `d3d11_device.h`; and reviewers cannot tell which functions may touch the immediate context (u-bridge-14) because everything is a peer method on one struct.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a - structural.
- **Change**: add three TUs to the existing `cxx_build` via extra `.file()` entries at `umd/build.rs:109` (they inherit every include and define from the same `cc::Build`, so no flag duplication): (1) `bridge/bridge_dxbc.cpp` takes `ShaderBytecode`, `write_le`, `encode_signature_entry`, `append_signature_chunk`, `is_patch_signature_chunk`, all three `prepare_shader_bytecode*` and `dump_shader_bytecode`; (2) `bridge/bridge_icd_exports.cpp` takes 61-345 plus the four venus export wrappers at 485-544, folding in u-bridge-04's resolve-once export table; (3) `bridge/bridge_flip_wait.cpp` takes 853-996 and the watchdog lambda from 2039-2066 (leave `present_flip_wait_setup` itself in the present half; move only the thread body into a named function `flip_wait_watchdog_main(std::shared_ptr<HeliosFlipWaitCtx>)` declared in the internal header). A new `bridge/bridge_internal.h` declares `umd_log`, `ShaderBytecode`, the `prepare_shader_bytecode*` signatures, `find_helios_icd_export`'s template (header-only), `HeliosVenusScanoutInfo` and `HeliosFlipWaitCtx` - all currently in anonymous namespaces, so this widens their linkage from internal-to-TU to internal-to-library. `HeliosStubAdapter` (361-390) stays with the device construction, not with the loader block; `HeliosVenusScanoutInfo` (346-359) goes with the resources half. Leave the DXVK-dependent halves (device/resources/present) in `dxvk_bridge.cpp` - the ownership findings (u-bridge-06/07/08, T5) already landed there and a further split buys nothing this tranche can validate.
- **Static guarantee**: the split is the guarantee. `bridge_dxbc.cpp` compiled without `d3d11_device.h`/`dxvk_device.h`/`dxvk_instance.h` makes "this code cannot touch the DXVK device or the immediate context" a link-time fact rather than a review convention, and the same holds for `bridge_icd_exports.cpp`. Honest limit: `bridge_dxbc.cpp` still needs `dxbc/dxbc_container.h` and `dxbc_spv::dxbc::hashDxbcBinary` from the dxbc-spirv subproject (`umd/build.rs:118`), so the firewall is against DXVK and COM, not against all third-party code - an off-VM test harness for the signature encoder must link or stub that one function.
- **Remaining unsafe**: unchanged C++ preconditions - `HeliosFlipWaitCtx::cpuVa` is a `const volatile std::uint64_t*` into the runtime's monitored-fence mapping and is only valid while `alive` is true under `mutex`; the hand-declared `HeliosCbSignalSyncFromCpu` layout is asserted against WDDM2 by comment, not by the compiler (the WDK header is deliberately not included in this TU). Both move verbatim; the second is why the struct's comment must move with it.
- **Atomic boundary**: four commits: (0) add `bridge/bridge_internal.h` with the declarations and change the anonymous-namespace definitions to named-namespace ones in place (no code moves - this commit alone proves the linkage change compiles and links); (1) `bridge_dxbc.cpp`; (2) `bridge_icd_exports.cpp`; (3) `bridge_flip_wait.cpp`. Each of (1)-(3) is a pure text move plus one `.file()` line.
- **Risk**: medium, and the risk is the build rather than the runtime: moving symbols out of an anonymous namespace can silently change overload resolution or ODR-merge two same-named helpers, and clang-cl's `/EHsc` + `_ALLOW_COMPILER_AND_STL_VERSION_MISMATCH` flags must apply identically to the new TUs (they do, via the same `cc::Build`, but verify the emitted command lines once). A missed `.file()` produces an unresolved-external at link, which is loud.
- **Validation**: byte-identical DXBC output for a captured shader - dump before and after with `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Helios!ShaderBytecodeDumpPath` and compare the `.dxbc` files bit-for-bit (this covers the MD5 stamp, the ISGN/OSGN/PCSG chunk offsets and the tess sysval remap in one check); identical `helios_umd_<pid>.log` line sequence for a DWM boot including the loader's `Venus instance-scoped ctx export returned ctx_id=…` line; `flip-kwait` log lines unchanged. Then the host-side unit test that this split exists to enable: build `bridge_dxbc.cpp` alone against a stubbed `hashDxbcBinary` and assert `append_signature_chunk`'s output offsets for a two-entry ISGN - that test is u-bridge-18's regression gate and cannot exist before this commit.

### R1106. Split umd/src/lib.rs into adapter, caps, knobs and log, and give the feature-level profile one owner

- **Finding**: u-core-20 (depends on u-core-04 and x-dup-dead-18 in T6, u-core-08 in T5, u-core-06 in T7 - all four delete or consolidate code this item would otherwise move).
- **Where**: `umd/src/lib.rs:12-15` (the four-module list); `:19-44` (HRESULT constants, `ddi_supported`, `SUPPORTED_DDI_VERSIONS`, `D3D12_SUPPORTED_DDI_VERSIONS`); `:46-190` (the seven hand-transcribed ABI structs - deleted by u-core-08); `:191` (`ADAPTER_COOKIE`); `:201-254` (the three `helios_umd_*` vehicle exports at 202/229/243); `:256-371` (`helios_umd_selftest` - deleted/`cfg`-gated by x-dup-dead-18); `:373-422` (`OpenAdapter10`, `OpenAdapter10_2`, `OpenAdapter12`); `:424-643` (the eight `d3d12_*` handlers - deleted by u-core-04); `:645-846` (`calc_private_device_size`, `create_device`, `close_adapter`, `get_supported_versions`); `:848-979` (`get_caps` - the whole D3D11 caps policy, with `feature_level_mode() >= 1` at 890, 920, 944); `:981-1016` (`umd_log_path` 981, `log_line` 992); `:1018-1310` (six knob readers: `trace_enabled` 1018, `feature_level_mode` 1080, `present_gate_us` 1127, `vehicle_flip_gate_us` 1177, `vehicle_kernel_flip_wait` 1235, `present_sync_publish_enabled` 1276); `:1312-1321` (`trace_line!`); `:1329-1364` (`log_self_module_path`). The other half of the caps contract: `umd/src/forward.rs:6433` and `:6637` (`feature_level_mode() != 1`), `:6722`, `:6735`, `:6763` (`== 1`).
- **Today**: one module holds the ABI struct copies, the adapter entry points, the D3D11 caps policy, six knob readers, the logging subsystem, an exported selftest and three vehicle exports. The concrete defect this hides is that the feature-level profile is a distributed contract with no owner: `feature_level_mode()` gates three caps in `get_caps` **and** five sites in `forward.rs`'s `check_format_support`/`CheckMultisampleQualityLevels`, and the comparison is deliberately asymmetric - `>= 1` in `lib.rs` versus `== 1` in `forward.rs` - because that asymmetry *is* the documented knob=2 diagnostic ("pipeline claims 11_0 but keeps the FL10 MSAA/format caps", `lib.rs:1078-1079`). Nothing in the code says so; it is discoverable only by grepping a 1364-line file and noticing that two files compare the same knob with two different operators on purpose.
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: a change to the FL11 profile edits `get_caps` and misses one of `forward.rs`'s five sites → the runtime rejects the device with `DXGI_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED` at `CDevice::LLOCompleteLayerConstruction`, which is exactly the failure `lib.rs:1070-1074` documents, with nothing preventing the partial edit. The symmetric hazard: a refactor "unifies" `>= 1` and `== 1` and silently deletes knob mode 2.
- **Change**: `umd/src/log.rs` (`umd_log_path`, `log_line`, `trace_line!`, `log_self_module_path`); `umd/src/knobs.rs` (the six readers, already reduced to one `reg_dword` helper plus typed accessors by T7's u-core-06); `umd/src/adapter.rs` (`OpenAdapter10`, `OpenAdapter10_2`, `OpenAdapter12`, `calc_private_device_size`, `create_device`, `close_adapter`, `get_supported_versions`, `ADAPTER_COOKIE`, `ddi_supported`, `SUPPORTED_DDI_VERSIONS`); `umd/src/vehicle_exports.rs` (the three `helios_umd_*` exports); `umd/src/caps.rs` (`get_caps`). `lib.rs` then holds the module list and the shared HRESULT constants. Separately - and this is the one commit in T8 that is not a pure move - `caps.rs` gains `struct FeatureProfile { pipeline_mask: u32, shader_caps: u32, options1: u32, levels_mask: u32, msaa: MsaaPolicy, format_mask: FormatPolicy }` with **three** constants: `FL10_0` (knob 0), `FL11_0` (knob absent or 1) and `FL11_PIPELINE_ONLY` (knob 2 - FL11 pipeline/shader/options1/levels with FL10 MSAA and format policy), selected once by `knobs::feature_level_mode()`. `get_caps`'s three branches and `forward.rs`'s five sites then read fields of the selected profile instead of each re-deriving a comparison. Two profiles would silently delete mode 2; three is the minimum that preserves behaviour.
- **Static guarantee**: a single `FeatureProfile` value makes "these caps move together" a data fact - adding a field forces every consumer to be updated, and the knob selects one of three named constants instead of eight independent comparisons using two different operators. That is a real guarantee against the partial-profile class the doc comment warns about, and it holds only if the third profile survives; otherwise the refactor is itself the partial edit.
- **Remaining unsafe**: none new. `get_caps` keeps its `unsafe { *(args.p_data as *mut u32) = caps }` writes behind the existing `args.data_size >= 4` per-arm checks; the profile change does not touch them.
- **Atomic boundary**: four move commits (log, knobs, vehicle_exports, adapter) then one non-move commit for `caps.rs` + `FeatureProfile` + the five `forward.rs` call sites. The `caps.rs` commit must land before R1107 so that the forward split relocates already-converted call sites rather than re-deriving them.
- **Risk**: medium for the `FeatureProfile` commit, low for the four moves. The specific hazard is mode 2: `feature_level_mode()` returns `1` when the knob is absent and the raw value otherwise, so `FL11_PIPELINE_ONLY` must be selected on exactly `2` and `FL11_0` on absent-or-1, with any other nonzero value falling into the same arm the current `>= 1` gives it. Enumerate all four settings in the match, do not use a range.
- **Validation**: for each of the four knob settings (`FeatureLevel11` absent / 0 / 1 / 2), the `GetCaps:` log lines from `caps.rs` and the `check_format_support`/MSAA answers from `forward.rs` are identical before and after - mode 2 in particular must still produce FL11 pipeline/shader/options1 caps with FL10 MSAA and masked format bits. DWM creates its device at the same feature level and the desktop composites; a 3DMark Fire Strike run still reaches the same feature-level path with no new noop-DDI hits. Note honestly that a host unit test is unavailable here: `umd` is `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` with a Windows-only `build.rs` that shells to clang-cl, so the `FeatureProfile` table cannot be exercised by `cargo test` without adding `rlib` to the crate type - a build-artifact change that belongs to T0, not here. The four-setting A/B on the VM is the proof.

- **Finding**: u-forward-a-01 (canonical; absorbs x-ordering-19). Depends on u-forward-a-08 in T5, which is what makes `handles.rs` a boundary rather than a folder.

- **Today**: one 10377-line file owns handle plumbing, format tables, WDDM allocation and residency, resource lifecycle, four view-descriptor translators, shaders, pipeline binding, state objects, binding-array collection, queries, caps and the whole DXGI present path. The defect class this hides is cross-subsystem handle reinterpretation: `store_com`/`load_com`/`handle_com_raw`/`load_resource`/`load_rtv` are in scope everywhere, so any DDI can apply the wrong decoder to a `pDrvPrivate` slot with no compiler objection (u-forward-a-08). The module header at 1-10 is also stale - it claims Create* errors are dropped, but `set_runtime_error` (444-463) exists and is used by `create_resource`, `open_resource` and `finish_wddm_tex2d` and by none of the view or state-object creates (u-forward-a-02, T2, fixes the behaviour; this item fixes the paragraph).
- **Invalid sequence permitted**: n/a - structural. The decode-confusion sequence itself is u-forward-a-08's, in T5; this item removes its reachability.
- **Change**: the tree is `umd/src/forward/` - **not** `umd/src/ddi/`, which the source finding proposed and which collides with the existing `umd/src/ddi.rs` bindgen module. `forward.rs` stays a file and gains child modules under `forward/` (Rust 2018 layout, so the parent need not become `mod.rs` and the diff stays a pure relocation). Modules, one commit each: `forward/handles.rs` (77-143, 412-639, 1044-1213, `set_runtime_error`, `env_flag`); `forward/format.rs` (194-338); `forward/alloc.rs` (147-150, 171-192, 342-408, and the allocation half of 1325-1710 - note `env_flag` at 152-155 belongs to `handles.rs` and `empty_present_private` at 157-169 to the present half, not to `alloc.rs`); `forward/resource.rs` (1301-2574); `forward/views.rs` (2576-2978, 4959-5401); `forward/transfer.rs` (2980-3463); `forward/shaders.rs` (3465-4391); `forward/pipeline.rs` (4393-4821); `forward/state_objects.rs` (4823-4956, 5469-5506); `forward/bindings.rs` (5403-5742); then the second half as `forward/queries.rs`, `forward/format_caps.rs`, `forward/present.rs`, `forward/tables.rs`. Two modules the source inventories list do **not** get created: `scanout.rs` (646-946) is deleted by T6's x-dup-dead-14, and `selftest.rs` (6781-7370) is deleted or `cfg`-gated by T6's x-dup-dead-18. Boundary rule: nothing but `handles.rs` may reinterpret a `pDrvPrivate` pointer; it exports `ResourceHandle`/`RtvHandle`/`ComHandle<T>` with private raw-pointer casts and every other module receives already-decoded typed references. One coupling must be resolved before the present half compiles: `dxgi_rotate_resource_identities` reaches into `ResourceState`'s private fields, so `handles.rs` must publish a rotation API (`ResourceState::swap_wddm_identity(&mut other)` or a free `rotate_identities(&mut [*mut ResourceState])`) - a `pub(super)`-only split will not compile. Rewrite the 1-10 module header in the same commit as `handles.rs`.
- **Static guarantee**: real. Today `unsafe { *(p as *const *mut RtvState) }` is legal anywhere in 10377 lines; after the split the constructor is private to `handles.rs`, so a caller in `views.rs` cannot manufacture an `RtvHandle` from a resource slot. Note the direction that does **not** work: a child module keeps full access to its parent's private items, so moving code *out* of `forward.rs` seals nothing by itself - the guarantee comes from the payload types' constructors being private to `handles.rs`, which is why u-forward-a-08 must land first.
- **Remaining unsafe**: the initial decode from the runtime-supplied `pDrvPrivate` stays unsafe - the runtime, not the driver, guarantees the pointer identifies the slot the matching `CalcPrivate*Size` sized, and that cannot be encoded in Rust types. Every DDI entry point also keeps its `*mut` argument null checks; those are runtime checks by necessity.
- **Atomic boundary**: fourteen commits, one per module, in the order handles → format → alloc → resource → views → transfer → shaders → pipeline → state_objects → bindings → queries → format_caps → present → tables. `handles.rs` first because every other module imports from it; `tables.rs` (the four `install()` function-table writers) last because it names every DDI in the crate. This is the largest single item in the tranche and the one most likely to need re-sequencing mid-flight; if a commit needs a body edit to compile, stop and split that edit into its own reviewed commit rather than folding it into the move.
- **Risk**: medium. The specific hazards: (a) the rotation API for `ResourceState` is a genuine signature addition inside a move-only tranche - review it alone; (b) the 26 `*_LOG_COUNT` statics are read by log budget checks scattered across the modules they gate, so each must move with its consumers or become `pub(super)` in `forward.rs` - do the latter, and do not renumber or rename any of them; (c) `cargo fmt` after a move of this size can reflow moved bodies, which defeats the move-only review - run `cargo fmt` as a separate commit at the end of the tranche, not inside each move.
- **Validation**: release UMD builds with no new warnings; the `helios_umd_<pid>.log` line sequence for a DWM boot is identical (same order, same budget cut-offs - the `|| allocation != 0` style escape clauses were already normalised by T2's x-dup-dead-26, so the line counts must match exactly); `pnputil /restart-device`, then DWM composites with `ScanoutDiag` absent, `VpSA=1`, `ScSet=1`; the DComp probe cadence stays near 63 fps and idle-to-active wake is at or better than the T0 baseline; Fire Strike and DOOM complete with no new noop-DDI hits and no new present-gate timeouts (`EXT_FLIP_GATE_TIMEOUTS` unchanged).

# 6. Registers

## Implicit-ordering register

Every row is one ordering contract the current code depends on. **Where** cites the sites that carry it
(line numbers re-opened against the tree at KMD 22.22.176.0). **Enforced today by** names the actual
mechanism and grades it: *a type* (marked "already witnessed" — the compiler rejects the violation),
*a lock or serialization that happens to cover it*, *statement order*, or *nothing but a comment*.
**Invalid sequence that compiles** is what `rustc`/`clang` accept today; where a verifier proved the
sequence unconstructible against the current call graph, the cell says so and the row is a
future-edit trap rather than a live defect — those still belong here, because the whole point is that
nothing stops the next edit. **Static enforcement** is the encoding that would make the violation a
build failure, stated with its honest limit; "cosmetic" appears where a type would only relocate a
runtime check. **Tranche** is where the work lands, with the canonical finding id.

Rows marked "already witnessed" are the precedents to point at: `WddmNotifyGuard` (KMD) and
`RuntimePagingQueue` (UMD) are the two places this codebase already got it right at the type level.
Patterns 1 and 4 below generalise them directly; patterns 2 and 3 have only convention-level
precedents in tree, which is exactly why their siblings diverged.

| Contract | Where | Enforced today by | Invalid sequence that compiles | Static enforcement | Tranche |

### Contracts that cannot be encoded

1. **dxgkrnl's DDI call order** (AddDevice → StartDevice → QueryAdapterInfo → CreateDevice/Context → SetVidPnSourceAddress → StopDevice → RemoveDevice). dxgkrnl re-enters through an untyped `*mut c_void` on every call, so a typestate *parameter* on `AdapterContext` would be erased at the boundary and only relocate the cast (`k-lifecycle-13` says so explicitly). Required instead: a magic word validated by every handle→context `from_raw`, plus a counted refusal. **Today: partial.** `AllocationContext`/`OpenAllocationContext` carry `ALLOCATION_CTX_MAGIC`; `DeviceContext`/`ContextContext` carry none, and `DxgkDdiDescribeAllocation` skips even the magic that exists (`k-alloc-02`). No refusal counter exists for either.

2. **The IRQL at the moment of use.** A `PassiveLevel` token records that the call site was reached from a PASSIVE entry point; a `KeAcquireSpinLockRaiseToDpc` between construction and use raises IRQL while the token stays live. Only `KeGetCurrentIrql` can assert the live level. Required: the runtime gate plus a named counter on every path that writes the registry or maps memory. **Today: one gate, one counter, wrong coverage.** `build_paging_buffer.rs:940` gates the content branch and increments `BAR_ERR_IRQL` (PgEi, never observed nonzero); the failure branch at `904-923` calls `dump_bar_counters()` with no gate at all.

3. **DIRQL entry from the ISR, and `DxgkCbSynchronizeExecution`.** The ISR reconstructs `&AdapterContext` from the raw miniport pointer, so no borrow relationship exists to constrain; and "no ISR may take `wddm_notify_lock`" is a whole-program property, because the DPC holds that lock across a DIRQL callback. Required: keep the ISR's reachable surface to a small atomics projection, and count DIRQL notification failures monotonically. **Today: no.** `DMA_SYNC_STATUS_LOW`/`DMA_SYNC_RET` are *last-value* stores, so a failed `DMA_COMPLETED` notification is not counted at all (`k-ctrlsubmit-01`); a `NOTIFY_FAILS` counter must be added.

4. **Host-side completion.** Whether the host actually finished a command is observable only through the used ring or a Venus feedback slot; no Rust type witnesses it, so the "Venus commands flush before fence signal" invariant rests entirely on the ring-1 completion path. Required: a named fault counter at every latch and refusal, surfaced through QUERY_STATS. **Today: no.** `ring_wait_until` sets `self.fatal` after a 30 s budget with **no** `record_named_bytes` (`k-venus-V01`); `publish_and_notify` latches on `RING_STATUS_FATAL` the same way; async ctrl response errors accumulate in statics nothing reads (`x-dup-dead-22`); and `RbRid`/`RbFail` can never move because their branch is dead (`k-lifecycle-02`).

5. **Cross-FFI same-thread call order** (Mesa ICD → UMD: `set_present_source` → `Present` → `get_present_result`/`wait_last_present`). The caller is another codebase; returning an opaque ticket from `set_present_source` would enforce it but is an ICD ABI change, out of scope for a behaviour-preserving refactor. Required: the existing violation counters as the acceptance signal, plus a device-liveness refusal counter. **Today: partial.** `EXT_OVERWRITES`, `EXT_RESULT_OVERWRITES` and `EXT_RESULT_MISSES` exist and sit near zero — keep them; the liveness refusal counter does not exist.

6. **Non-recursive acquisition of the two PASSIVE KEVENT mutexes.** A `ScanoutGuard` proves the lock is held but cannot stop code holding it from calling the acquiring wrapper, and a `SynchronizationEvent` records no owner, so the kernel cannot assert either (a real `KMUTEX` would — that is a behaviour change and its own decision). Required: a debug-only owner-thread field asserted in `with_scanout_lifecycle`, and a bounded acquire whose timeout is a counted refusal that never runs the closure unlocked. **Today: neither.** The wait is a NULL-timeout, non-alertable `KeWaitForSingleObject` (`adapter.rs:1074-1082`).

7. **The `vidmm_reserved` ↔ `DXGK_CPUHOSTAPERTURE` span agreement.** Two numbers produced by two different DDIs; a type can make the reserve immutable but cannot tie it to what the segment descriptor declares. Required: a StartDevice-time equality check with a named refusal. **Today: nothing compares them** (`k-gputransport-14`).

8. **Prefix compatibility of the three `as *mut` device-funcs reinterpretations.** `offset_of!` const asserts can police named anchor fields, but full prefix compatibility of a bindgen-regenerated header is not provable in the crate. Required: the anchor asserts plus a runtime null-slot audit. **Today: half.** `audit_wddm1_3_device_funcs` exists and is called from one filler; the asserts do not exist, and `build.rs` disables bindgen's layout tests (`u-core-08`).

9. **A declaration-order release rule between sibling fields of one struct.** Encoding it needs a lifetime borrowed from a sibling — self-referential, not expressible. Required: an explicit `release_com_state()` so teardown never depends on drop order, plus a released-entry count. **Today: no.** Only `ia` is explicitly released in `ddi_destroy_device` (`device_funcs.rs:471`); the other three caches rely on drop order and nothing counts them.

10. **"dxgkrnl captured the escape buffer before we read it" and "the OS interface pointer is valid for this call only."** Both are dxgkrnl guarantees asserted in SAFETY comments with no citation and no way to witness — `k-capsescape-13` was dropped for exactly this reason, and `k-display-15` is the VidPn twin. Required: a refusal counter on every escape and mode-set path so a violated guarantee is at least visible. **Today: no.** Every escape refusal except the fence-event arms increments nothing — unknown verb, bad magic, BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and swallowed `with_virtio` errors are all silent (`k-capsescape-10`).

### The four enforcement patterns

**1. Proof tokens for lock and level authority.** A non-Copy, `!Send` zero-sized value that only the acquiring wrapper can mint, demanded by every function whose contract depends on that lock or level. Done right in tree: **`WddmNotifyGuard`** (`adapter.rs:434-441`, minted only inside `with_wddm_notify_lock` at `1229`) — private field, no Copy/Clone, cannot escape the closure. Should adopt it: the two PASSIVE mutexes (`ScanoutGuard`/`VenusGuard`, x-ordering-05), `virtio::ctrl`'s PASSIVE-only surface (k-ctrlsubmit-13), the venus ring API (k-venus-19), the paging registry dumps and Mm mappings (k-paging-13), `PatchCapacity` (k-paging-16), `RenderGdiPlan` (k-paging-01), and the `SpinTable` guard (k-paging-12). Sharpen the precedent itself while generalising it: today the guard is not adapter-branded and does not witness notify-before-virtio, so move `with_virtio` onto it (k-lifecycle-05) — and do **not** introduce a combined `with_notify_then_virtio` for the paths that legitimately need only the transport lock. State the limit at every token definition: a token is *authority*, not a live IRQL assertion and not a recursion proof.

**2. Typestate for lifecycle phases.** Each phase is a distinct type; the transition consumes the previous value, so a skipped or reordered stage does not compile. There is no full example in tree yet — the nearest thing is `validate_patch_capacity(self)` consuming its descriptor (`present_packet.rs:232`), which is the shape at one-stage scale. Should adopt it: the VenusClient bring-up (x-ordering-06, the sharpest case — seven ordered stages in one 400-line function with zeroed ids in a live struct), `AdapterContext` Added→Started (k-lifecycle-13 and k-lifecycle-04), `Transport { Live, Failed }` (k-gputransport-02), the device-funcs fill levels (u-core-07), the flip-wait `Unprobed \| Disabled \| Ready` (u-forward-b-01), the vehicle present state machine (u-forward-b-05), `Powered::D0 \| D3` (k-lifecycle-17), and `Option<ScanoutTarget>` with a consuming `retarget` in place of the one-shot latch (k-venus-03). Two mechanical constraints found while verifying: `VirtioGpu` is reached only through `&mut` behind an `UnsafeCell<Option<..>>`, so a self-consuming transition needs `core::mem::replace` with a placeholder variant; and the `Failed` arm still has to service the WDDM FIFO, so it needs its own drain API rather than being a dead end.

**3. Ownership-consuming APIs for in-flight objects.** If a value is in flight, the API that ends its flight takes it *by value* and hands it back on failure, so "popped but neither delivered nor requeued" and "record dropped while the host object lives" stop being writable. Done right in tree: the `Err((DmaBuffer, ..))` hand-back convention across the enqueue paths (k-gputransport-05) and `free_memory_blob`'s destroy-then-remove order (k-venus-07) — both conventions rather than types, which is exactly why their siblings diverged. Should adopt it: `ReadyFence` with `signal(..) -> Result<Retired, ReadyFence>` (k-ctrlsubmit-01), the non-Copy sync ticket plus `AbandonOutcome` (k-gputransport-13), `InFlight<PreparedImageCopy>` (k-venus-08), `release(self) -> Result<(), (Self, VirtioError)>` for the three venus cache loops (k-venus-07), the `ParkedReap` drop guard (k-ctrlsubmit-08), `PreparedCopySlot::take` (k-alloc-04), the mode-set guards' consuming `assign()` (x-ordering-15), the deferred-programming guard's `defer_to_completion()` (k-display-02), `PublishedOpens` (k-alloc-09), `FreshComObject::release_to` (u-bridge-02), and the defusable drop guard in UMD CreateDevice (x-ordering-13). One blocker to plan for: `WddmReady` is `#[derive(Clone, Copy)]` and the DPC builds its batch as `[WddmReady { .. }; 8]`, which requires Copy — the batch API changes shape or the token cannot be non-Copy.

**4. Validated-once descriptors for multi-field contracts.** One constructor checks the whole field group and yields a value whose members cannot subsequently disagree; partial publication and partial reads stop being representable. Done right in tree: **`RuntimePagingQueue`** (`device_funcs.rs:54-64`). Should adopt it: `ScanoutBinding` for the five scanout publish words with a `NonZeroU32` pitch and a `VirtioFormat` newtype (k-lifecycle-02 — the exact state that silently disabled the async re-bind arm), `SeqPublished<PrimaryScanout>` for the torn escape read (k-capsescape-11), `ScanoutMode` owning mode plus EDID (k-lifecycle-20), the sealed `SegmentTable` builder (x-ordering-16), `WddmSurface` as one `const fn` (k-capsescape-03), `VersionedOut` for the short-buffer caps write (k-capsescape-09), `RuntimeContext` (u-core-09), `AllocationPlan` (k-alloc-01), `RingMap` (k-venus-05), the paging union enum (k-paging-18), `SortedByKey` (k-paging-11), and `DeallocateForm` (u-forward-a-17).

**A fifth mechanism would be ceremony** in these places, and the register should say so rather than let an implementer add ritual: a `SingleThreadedDeviceModel` token (u-core-12 — `HeliosDevice` is already `!Sync`, and the token cannot stop someone editing both sites); a `CsThreadToken` on the four bridge context methods (`u-bridge-14` — the invalid sequence is unconstructible and the deliverable is a counter plus one comment on `impl->context`); an `EnvConfigured` token around a single `_putenv_s` call site (u-bridge-20); a generic typestate *parameter* on `AdapterContext` (dxgkrnl hands the pointer back untyped, so it is erased at the boundary — see cannot-encode #1); `PhantomPinned` presented as a no-move guarantee (it only makes the type `!Unpin`; `Box::new(ctx)` and `*Box::from_raw(raw)` still compile — keep it as a doc marker, k-lifecycle-13); a type-level `Last<CpuHostSegment>` position over a three-slot array (x-ordering-16 — use the validating constructor); and wrapping today's `Vec<u64>` of PFNs in a newtype with a no-op `Drop` (k-paging-04 — cosmetic until a real page lease exists).

---

## Static-guarantee catalogue

The goal is a *small trusted boundary*: a handful of `unsafe fn` constructors that each perform one
documented check and hand back a value downstream code cannot corrupt, with everything else safe by
construction. It is emphatically not a wrapper layer. Helios already has dozens of places where a raw
`*mut c_void` is cast, checked against a magic word, and then trusted for 400 lines; adding a struct
around that cast while leaving the cast reachable from five other call sites buys nothing and costs a
week. Every mechanism below is scored on one question: after it lands, is the invalid state
*unconstructible*, or has the same unchecked cast merely moved? Where the honest answer is "moved",
the item is in **Rejected as cosmetic** — including several proposals the verifiers themselves
demoted. Two constraints bound everything: `kmd_render` is `no_std` with `panic = "abort"` and
`wdk-panic`'s `KeBugCheck` handler (so `Drop` only has to cover normal returns, and *any* `unwrap`,
`expect`, slice-index or `unreachable!` in a DDI is a bugcheck, not an error), and registry knob
names, counter names and diagnostic breadcrumb values are an ABI the owner debugs with — a mechanism
that changes an emitted value must say so.

---

### 1. Validated-once descriptors (parse, don't validate)

The single highest-leverage mechanism: ~45 findings are variations of "the constructor checked it,
then threw the parsed value away and re-derived it later" or "five arms patch a shared mutable
descriptor in place".

**Invariants encoded.** Allocation backing class completeness (`k-alloc-01`, 5 arms × 9 fields, 470
lines); private-data trailer layout (`k-alloc-03`, 2 layouts, one length check); aperture range
validity (`k-alloc-13`, DISPATCH ack path skips the PASSIVE consecutive-page check); backing-size
provenance (`k-alloc-17`); scanout identity (`k-display-05`, `k-display-11`, `k-lifecycle-02`,
`k-lifecycle-V01`, `x-ordering-V01`, `x-dup-dead-V01` — five independently published atomics, two of
which have **no writer at all**); display mode ↔ EDID cofunctionality (`k-lifecycle-20`); scan-out
format (`k-display-10`, `x-dup-dead-V02`, `k-alloc-16`, `u-bridge-08` — 4–5 divergent tables in 2
languages); Present pixel format (`k-venus-06`, two `.expect()` on the Present path);
`vkCreateImage`/`vkAllocateMemory` pNext chains (`k-venus-11`, `x-dup-dead-04`, 4+5 encoders);
MDL/blob copy windows (`k-paging-03`, `k-paging-19`); the RenderGdi command stream (`k-paging-09`,
`k-paging-06`, `k-paging-08` — 4 scattered bound checks, 6 arms each remembering its own);
`DXGKARG_BUILDPAGINGBUFFER` union arms (`k-paging-18`, 6 copies of `// SAFETY: union arm selected by
Operation.`); the versioned caps output buffer (`k-capsescape-09`, latent UB); the escape payload
(`k-capsescape-12`, hardcoded `buf[16..24]` offsets); the segment table (`k-capsescape-04`, `-07`,
`-08`, 5 near-identical writers); virtqueue descriptor spans (`k-gputransport-03`, 3 enqueues + 1
drain must agree or `virtio-drivers` panics at DISPATCH); the UMD's WDDM-allocation arguments
(`u-forward-a-07`, 12 positional scalars), scanout target (`u-forward-a-10`, 6 loose `Cell`s, 3
disagreeing writers), shader bytecode (`u-forward-a-16`, 10 duplicate `from_raw_parts`), open-identity
meta (`u-forward-a-05`), DDI arrays (`u-forward-a-04`), the runtime context (`u-core-09`), present
preconditions (`u-forward-b-02`), and DXBC signature entries (`u-bridge-18`).

**Shape.** Three recurring forms. (a) A class enum plus a total build:

```rust
// kmd_render/src/ddi/alloc/backing.rs
pub(crate) enum AllocationBacking {
    AdoptedUmdResource { resource_id: u32, take_ownership: bool },
    KmdLinearPrimary   { width: u32, height: u32 },
    KmdOptimalGdiTexture { width: u32, height: u32, dxgi_format: DxgiFormat, bind_flags: u32 },
    KmdStandardBuffer  { size: u64, primary: bool },
    RawHost3dBlob      { ctx_id: u32, blob_mem: u32, blob_flags: u32, blob_id: u64, size: u64 },
}

/// No `Default`, no `pub` fields, no post-construction mutation: only a build arm
/// produces one, and every arm must answer every field explicitly (the adopt arm
/// passes `meta.pitch` through — that pass-through IS the guarantee).
pub(crate) struct CreatedBacking {
    resource_id: u32,
    venus_memory_id: Option<VkDeviceMemoryId>,
    venus_image_id: Option<VkImageId>,
    pitch: Option<RowPitch>,
    plane_offset: u64,
    dxgi_format: DxgiFormat,
    size: BackingSize,
    memory_type_index: u32,
}

/// `bar_eligible` stops being an inference from `venus_memory_id != 0` (k-alloc-17).
pub(crate) enum BackingSize {
    HostAuthoritative(u64), // vkGetImageMemoryRequirements / vkAllocateMemory answered
    CreatorClaimed(u64),    // the ICD's private-data claim; never BAR-eligible
}
```

(b) A split of "geometry of some surface" from "the identity Windows paired with *this*
`hAllocation`", which today share one struct whose `primary_*` fields are meaningless zeros in two of
its three construction sites (`display.rs:79-92`, `:132-145`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct WindowsPrimary { alloc: NonNull<AllocationContext>, segment: u32,
                                   address: u64, flags: u32, extent: Extent2d }
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct ScanoutTarget { resource: ResourceId, extent: Extent2d, pitch: RowPitch,
                                  plane_offset: u64, size: u64, format: ScanoutFormat }
impl ScanoutTarget {
    /// Runs today's display.rs:951-964 checks plus the :980-984 pitch resolution.
    pub(crate) fn from_direct_primary(p: &WindowsPrimary, mode: Extent2d)
        -> Result<Self, ScanoutReject>;
    pub(crate) fn adapter_linear(blob: &ScanoutImageBlob, mode: Extent2d)
        -> Result<Self, ScanoutReject>;

```

(c) A bounds-checked view whose constructor is the only place a raw pointer becomes addressable:

```rust
// Replaces the `&mut DXGK_DRIVERCAPS` built over a deliberately-short buffer
// (k-capsescape-09: reference-validity UB independent of which field is written),
// plus the second raw write through args.pOutputData while that &mut is live.
pub(crate) struct VersionedOut<'a> { base: *mut u8, len: usize, _o: PhantomData<&'a mut [u8]> }
impl<'a> VersionedOut<'a> {
    /// # Safety: `base` is dxgkrnl's output buffer, valid for `len` bytes for this call.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn new(base: *mut c_void, len: usize) -> Option<Self>;
    pub(crate) fn set<T: Copy>(&mut self, off: usize, v: T) -> bool {
        let end = match off.checked_add(core::mem::size_of::<T>()) { Some(e) => e, None => return false };
        if end > self.len { CAPS_FIELD_TRUNC.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed); return false; }
        unsafe { core::ptr::write_unaligned(self.base.add(off).cast::<T>(), v) };
        true
    }
}

// Replaces `legacy = buf.len() < 32` + `buf[16..24]` + `buf[24..32]` (k-capsescape-12).
pub(crate) struct EscapeBuf<'a, T: bytemuck::Pod> { buf: &'a mut [u8], _t: PhantomData<T> }
impl<'a, T: bytemuck::Pod> EscapeBuf<'a, T> {
    pub(crate) fn new(buf: &'a mut [u8], hdr: &HeliosEscapeHeader) -> Option<Self> {
        let need = core::mem::size_of::<T>();
        (buf.len() >= need && hdr.size as usize >= need).then(|| Self { buf, _t: PhantomData })
    }
    pub(crate) fn read(&self) -> T { bytemuck::pod_read_unaligned(&self.buf[..size_of::<T>()]) }
    pub(crate) fn write_back(&mut self, v: &T);
    /// SUBMIT_VENUS ONLY — `hdr.size` covers the 40-byte fixed header while
    /// PrivateDriverDataSize covers header+stream, so the stream stays bounded by
    /// `buf.len()` exactly as today. Bounding it on hdr.size breaks every submit.
    pub(crate) fn trailing(&self) -> &[u8] { &self.buf[core::mem::size_of::<T>()..] }
}
```

Plus the small ones that pay immediately: `ScanoutFormat` (below, in the protocol crate so it is
host-testable), `MdlWindow { va: NonNull<u8>, len: usize }` with
`range(off, len) -> Option<NonNull<u8>>`, `BlobWindow` with the same accessor (which makes
`k-paging-19`'s clamp-vs-refuse divergence disappear by construction), `DmaBuffer::span(&self, off,
len) -> Option<DmaSpan<'_>>`, `ShaderBytes<'a>` replacing 10 hand-built slices, and
`DdiSlice<'a,H>::new(ptr, num) -> Option<Self>` where `None` means *null array* and `num == 0` means
*empty* — the distinction three DDIs currently get three different ways.

```rust
// protocol/src/scanout.rs — builds on Linux and Windows, so `from_dxgi` is unit-testable.
#[repr(u32)] #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ScanoutFormat { Rgba8Unorm = 28, Bgra8Unorm = 87, Bgrx8Unorm = 88 }
impl ScanoutFormat {
    /// TryFrom, not From: the value arrives from an untrusted UMD trailer.
    pub const fn from_dxgi(v: u32) -> Option<Self> { /* 28 | 87 | 88 */ }
    pub const fn virtio(self) -> u32;
    pub const fn bytes_per_pixel(self) -> u32 { 4 }
}
```

**Unrepresentable after.** A descriptor with a stale pitch from a sibling arm; a scanout binding with
a resource id but no pitch/format (the exact state that silently killed the async re-bind branch); a
`ScanoutTarget` with pitch 0 or an extent the mode rejects; a `WindowsPrimary` fabricated by the
fallback path (whose zeroed `primary_address` would be published as the displayed address); a
`&mut DXGK_DRIVERCAPS` over a short buffer; a queue span not backed by contiguous DMA memory
(`k-gputransport-18`'s precondition is then discharged at `DmaSpan`'s constructor, not restated in
`Hal::share`'s comment); a raster op holding a pointer into the command buffer; a format table that
disagrees with its four siblings; an `OptimalPresentImageDesc` whose format is unrepresentable
(deleting both `.expect()` on the Present path).

**Migration order.** `ScanoutFormat` and `DxgiFormat` first (protocol crate, no behavior, unblocks
five call sites in three files — keep the currently-unreachable `0 => B8G8R8X8` arm or delete it
deliberately in its own commit). Then `MdlWindow`/`BlobWindow`, `ShaderBytes`, `DdiSlice`,
`VersionedOut`, `EscapeBuf` — each self-contained, each one commit. Then `CreatedBacking` +
`classify` (L, 470-line rewrite; `k-alloc-10` and `-17` depend on it). Then `ScanoutBinding` in
adapter, which must precede the adapter.rs split or that split is cosmetic. `ScanoutTarget` /
`WindowsPrimary` last, sequenced with the two other findings that rewrite the same 196-line
`apply_vidpn_source_address_locked` so it is rewritten once.

### 2. Exhaustive enums replacing interdependent bools and sentinel integers

~45 findings. Same size as mechanism 1 but cheaper per item; several are single commits.

**Invariants encoded.** *WDDM surface level* — two booleans giving four states, one meaningless, with
the same nested `if` retyped at `lib.rs:96`, `query_adapter_info.rs:122`, `:287` and the outer bool
read at `:215`, `:889`; a partial raise is a documented AddAdapter rejection and the constants' names
already lie (both are `true`, so the adapter advertises WDDM **2.1**). Three findings
(`k-capsescape-03`, `x-ordering-08`, `x-dup-dead-02`) are the same item. *BAR segment topology* —
`BarSegMode` u32 carried across a module boundary and re-matched against literals `10 | 11 | _`, with
modes 1/2/5/11 documented as dxgmms-rejected yet reachable from a registry DWORD
(`k-capsescape-06`, `k-lifecycle-09`, `x-ordering-16`, `x-dup-dead-21`). *Refusal reasons* —
`ScanoutReject` (`k-display-12`), `EscapeRefusal` (`k-capsescape-10`, where every refusal except the
fence arms counts nothing), `PagingOpOutcome`/`PagingStatus` (`k-paging-02`, `x-ordering-17`),
`AbandonOutcome`/`SyncOutcome` (`k-ctrlsubmit-03`, `-10`, `-14`, `k-gputransport-13`,
`x-ordering-10`), `InsertResult` (`k-capsescape-15`), `PublishOutcome`/`GateOutcome` across cxx
(`u-bridge-10`, `-11`, `u-forward-b-15`). *Mode ladders* — `ScanoutDiagMode` (`k-display-08`: raw
1..16 through overlapping `mode >= 2/3/4/5`, `mode == 9 || 11`, `mode == 11 || 16` predicates,
duplicated in `venus.rs:4274`), `RetireDomain` replacing a `wait_gpu` bool the function's own nine-line
doc contradicts (`k-gputransport-15`), `ShaderStage` replacing `stage: &str` with a silent `_ => {}`
in two per-draw helpers (`u-forward-b-07`, `u-forward-a-13`), `NegotiatedInterface`
(`u-core-02`, `-V02`, `x-dup-dead-30`), `ResourceDimension` (`u-forward-a-12`: no `RES_TEX1D` arm, so
every Texture1D create silently returns a null handle), `DeallocateForm` (`u-forward-a-17`),
`RuntimeSubmission` (`u-forward-b-14`), `FlipWaitState` (`u-core-18`, `u-forward-b-01`,
`x-ordering-07`), `AllocationBytes` (`k-paging-14`: three content ops make three different implicit
residency choices), `SubmitAck` (`k-ctrlsubmit-V01`), `Powered` (`k-lifecycle-17`), `SchedulerHandle`
(`x-dup-dead-24`, `k-ctrlsubmit-16`).

**Shape.**

```rust
// kmd_render/src/ddi/caps/surface.rs — one value, five expansion sites collapse to accessor calls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum WddmSurface { Wddm1_3, Wddm2_1GpuMmu, Wddm3_2GpuMmu }
pub(crate) const SURFACE: WddmSurface = WddmSurface::Wddm2_1GpuMmu; // pinned: byte-identical today

impl WddmSurface {
    pub(crate) const fn ddi_interface_version(self) -> u32 { match self { /* exhaustive */ } }
    pub(crate) const fn caps_version(self) -> _DXGK_WDDMVERSION { match self { /* exhaustive */ } }
    pub(crate) const fn gpu_mmu(self) -> bool { !matches!(self, Self::Wddm1_3) }
    /// GpuMmu/VirtualAddressing pair ONLY — the cross-adapter bit stays runtime-knob-driven.
    pub(crate) const fn mem_caps_bits(self) -> u32 { match self { /* exhaustive */ } }
}
const _: () = assert!(SURFACE.gpu_mmu() == (SURFACE.mem_caps_bits() != 0));
```

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum ScanoutReject { BadAlloc, Extent, Layout, Format, SetFailed, NoTarget, CopyFailed }
impl ScanoutReject {
    /// Keeps today's ScSet=0xD / 0xE3 breadcrumb values byte-identical.
    pub(crate) const fn code(self) -> u32;
    pub(crate) fn counter(self) -> &'static AtomicU32;
    /// Counting is not separable from refusing: this is the only path to the NTSTATUS.
    pub(crate) fn refuse(self) -> NTSTATUS { self.counter().fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed); /* ... */ }
}

pub(crate) enum PagingOpOutcome { Executed, NotOurs, Failed(PagingStatus) }
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum PagingStatus { InsufficientDmaBuffer, InvalidParameter, NoMemory, DeviceNotReady }
impl From<PagingStatus> for NTSTATUS { /* only the DDI's legal return set — mirrors legalize_vidpn */ }
```

```rust
// umd — replaces flip_wait_state: Cell<u8> {0,1,2} + flip_wait_fence: Cell<u32>.
pub type WaitFromGpuCb = unsafe extern "C" fn(
    ddi::HANDLE, *const ddi::D3DDDICB_WAITFORSYNCHRONIZATIONOBJECTFROMGPU) -> ddi::HRESULT;
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct FlipWaitReady { pub fence: core::num::NonZeroU32, pub wait_cb: WaitFromGpuCb,
                           pub h_rt_device: ddi::HANDLE,
                           pub h_context: core::ptr::NonNull<core::ffi::c_void> }
// HeliosDevice: pub flip_wait: Cell<Option<FlipWaitReady>>, pub flip_wait_disabled: Cell<bool>,
```

`FlipWaitReady` is why this mechanism matters beyond tidiness: it deletes an `.unwrap()` on an
`Option<fn>` in the present path guarded only by a comment 900 lines away. Note bindgen's
`PFND3DDDI_WAITFORSYNCHRONIZATIONOBJECTFROMGPUCB` *is* the `Option`, so the token must spell the bare
`fn` type out.

**Unrepresentable after.** A mixed WDDM level (the caps analogue of the FAILED_ADD version-site
hazard); a `BarSegMode` value falling through `_ =>` into a documented Code-43 shape; a refusal with
no counter; a stage bind silently dropped; a "ready" flip-wait with no fence or no callback; a
`Present` variant that writes a refresh command.

**Migration order.** `WddmSurface` first — it is S, mechanical, provably byte-identical with `SURFACE`
pinned, and it retires three findings. Then `ScanoutReject` and `PagingStatus` (they are the exit
type the single-exit rewrites in mechanisms 1 and 5 need). Then `BarSegTopology`, but **producer and
consumer arms in one commit**: deleting `setup_bar_segment`'s mode-11 arm while
`query_segments4`'s `(Some((..,11)), Some(..))` arm survives kills the arm silently; deleting the
match arm first makes `BarSegMode=11` fall into `_ =>` and report the 3-segment shape documented as
Code-43-producing. `ScanoutDiagMode` only if `scanout_diag` is kept at all (see mechanism 9) — the
enum must carry *every* distinction the integers encode, including `mode >= 3` (the
`allocate_memory_blob` host-visible flag) and `mode >= 2` (the rebind pin), which a naive conversion
drops.

---

### 3. NonZero newtypes for object ids and ownership domains

~17 findings, one of which (`k-venus-04`) is the largest single type-safety win available in the KMD.

**Invariants encoded.** `alloc_handle()` mints one untyped `u64` for *every* Vulkan object class, and
`bind_image_memory(image, memory)` / `bind_buffer_memory(buffer, memory)` are signature-identical;
`cleanup_imported_source_alias(_, resource_id, image_id, memory_id)` takes three adjacent same-typed
ids; `PreparedImageCopy` exposes seven bare `u64` ids as `pub` fields; `0` means absent, tested by an
`if x != 0` at ~30 sites (`k-venus-04`, `k-venus-15` which was refuted precisely because it duplicates
this). Wire fence ids are bare `u64` restarted at 1 on every `VirtioGpu::init` with a purely ordinal
completion predicate, and the id crosses an *untrusted* escape buffer in both directions
(`k-ctrlsubmit-09`). Escape ownership: `owner == 0` is the sentinel meaning "KMD-owned", and
`RELEASE_BLOB`/`ALLOC_BLOB` accept it from a device-less escape (`k-capsescape-01`), while
`CTX_DESTROY`/`SUBMIT_VENUS` take no owner at all (`k-capsescape-02`). Plus `MappingOwner`
(`k-alloc-15`), `Pfn` (`k-paging-10`, where `checked_shl(12)` is a dead overflow guard and `>>12`/`<<12`
pairs are scattered at six sites), `RowPitch` (`k-alloc-06`, six divergent pitch derivations),
`VenusContextId` (`u-bridge-V01`), and `NonZero`/`NonNull` members for `RuntimeContext`
(`u-core-09`, `x-ordering-13`) and `DisplayMode` (`k-lifecycle-20`).

**Shape.**

```rust
// kmd_render/src/virtio/ids.rs
use core::num::{NonZeroU32, NonZeroU64, NonZeroUsize};
macro_rules! vk_id {
    ($n:ident) => {
        #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
        pub(crate) struct $n(NonZeroU64);
        impl $n {
            pub(crate) const fn get(self) -> u64 { self.0.get() }
            pub(crate) fn from_raw(v: u64) -> Option<Self> { NonZeroU64::new(v).map(Self) }
        }
    };
}
vk_id!(VkDeviceId);      vk_id!(VkQueueId);         vk_id!(VkImageId);
vk_id!(VkDeviceMemoryId); vk_id!(VkBufferId);       vk_id!(VkFenceId);
vk_id!(VkCommandPoolId); vk_id!(VkCommandBufferId);

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub(crate) struct ResourceId(NonZeroU32);
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub(crate) struct RowPitch(NonZeroU32);
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub(crate) struct WireFence(NonZeroU64);
impl WireFence {
    /// The ONE reconstruction point at the untrusted escape boundary.
    pub(crate) fn from_untrusted(v: u64) -> Option<Self> { NonZeroU64::new(v).map(Self) }
}
/// `None` = KMD-owned. The guest and kernel ownership domains stop sharing a
/// representation, so `take_blob_matching` cannot be handed the kernel sentinel.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub(crate) struct DeviceOwner(NonZeroUsize);
#[repr(transparent)] pub(crate) struct MappingOwner(usize); // ctor takes *const DeviceContext only
#[repr(transparent)] #[derive(Clone, Copy)] pub(crate) struct Pfn(u64);
impl Pfn { pub(crate) fn physical_address(self) -> Option<u64> { self.0.checked_mul(4096) } }
```

`Writer` gains `fn handle(&mut self, h: impl Into<u64>)` so the encoded bytes are unchanged, and
`Option<VkImageId>` is 8 bytes by the niche — so no struct grows and no wire layout shifts.

**Unrepresentable after.** Passing a memory id where an image id belongs (today `destroy_image_on_ring`
will happily encode one, and the failure surfaces later as a corrupt frame or a host decoder abort);
asking "is 0 valid?" at 30 sites; a forged escape fence id reported `Complete`; a device-less escape
unreffing an adopted allocation's blob; a page-frame number shifted by hand.

**Migration order.** Commit 1: the newtype module plus conversion of the *private* venus encoders
(`create_*`/`destroy_*`/`bind_*`/`cmd_*`), keeping `pub` signatures on `u64` with conversions at the
boundary. Commit 2: the `pub` structs (`PreparedImageCopy`, `ScanoutImageBlob`, `OptimalImageBlob`)
together with the eight `AtomicU64`/`AtomicU32` mirrors in `create_allocation.rs:65-73`, which keep
storing raw `u64` and gain one validating `restore()`. `WireFence` needs a companion behavioral commit
seeding `next_wire_fence` from a driver-global `AtomicU64` bumped by a large stride at each
`VirtioGpu::init`, otherwise the newtype does not make the ordinal predicate sound. `DeviceOwner`
before `OwnedCtx`, and note `venus.rs:4605` passes `Some(0)` today — that must become the KMD-owned
variant, not `None`-means-any.

### 4. Non-null, kind-typed wrappers over raw handles and COM pointers

~17 findings. Cheap, and it is the mechanism that closes an actual wild dereference.

**Invariants encoded.** `ContextHandleRef` exists precisely because "DDI handle types are all C
HANDLEs, so a direct cast can compile even when the callback received an hContext rather than an
hAdapter" — and it is used at *one* site while **five** others do the raw cast it was written to
prevent, one of which (`create_allocation.rs:1426`) chains
`&*(*(h_device as *const DeviceContext)).adapter` with no null check on the back-pointer while its two
siblings do check (`k-lifecycle-19`, `x-ordering-22`). `DxgkDdiDescribeAllocation` dereferences
`hAllocation` without the `ALLOCATION_CTX_MAGIC` check every other accessor performs
(`k-alloc-02`); `CreateAllocation` mints a new `ResourceContext` over a non-null input handle
(`k-alloc-V01`). In the UMD, one `pDrvPrivate` slot holds three incompatible payloads —
`*mut ResourceState`, `*mut RtvState`, or a bare COM pointer — discriminated only by which accessor the
caller picks, and `store_com` alone omits the null check its three siblings have
(`u-forward-a-08`, `u-forward-a-01`, `u-forward-b-17`). Thirteen bridge methods return a COM pointer as
`usize`: two borrowed, eleven owned, distinguished by a doc comment (`u-bridge-06`), and six cxx
declarations carry the *inverted* `unsafe` marking (`u-bridge-24`). `vidpn_interface` hands out a raw
`*const DXGK_VIDPN_INTERFACE` whose "valid for the call" lifetime exists only in prose, re-`&*`'d by
three callers (`k-display-15`). Plus `reinterpret_cast` where `static_cast` is available and checked
(`u-bridge-15`), `out_buffer<T>` for the ten `pOutputData` fillers (`k-paging-21`), and
`row_ptr -> Option<&mut [u32]>` replacing a null-sentinel raw pointer six call sites re-implement
(`k-paging-07`).

**Shape.**

```rust
// kmd_render/src/ddi/alloc/handle.rs — the ONLY place the cast+magic check exists.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct AllocHandleRef<'a> { ctx: &'a AllocationContext }
impl<'a> AllocHandleRef<'a> {
    /// # Safety
    /// `h` is an hAllocation this driver returned from CreateAllocation, which
    /// dxgkrnl keeps alive for the duration of the call.
    pub(crate) unsafe fn from_raw(h: HANDLE) -> Option<Self> {
        if h.is_null() { return None; }
        let ctx = unsafe { &*(h as *const AllocationContext) };
        (ctx.magic == ALLOCATION_CTX_MAGIC).then_some(Self { ctx })
    }
    pub(crate) fn paging(&self) -> PagingAllocInfo;
    pub(crate) fn primary(&self) -> Option<WindowsPrimary>;
    pub(crate) fn present(&self) -> PresentAllocInfo;
}
```

`AllocationContext` stays private to that module, so `DescribeAllocation` cannot obtain a field read
without the magic check — the missing check becomes a compile error rather than a review item.

```rust
// umd/src/handles.rs — P is fixed by the bindgen handle type, which is a distinct
// one-field struct per kind (`D3D10DDI_HRESOURCE { pDrvPrivate: *mut c_void }`, etc).
pub struct Slot<P> { cell: NonNull<*mut c_void>, _p: PhantomData<P> }
pub struct Com<T>(PhantomData<T>);
// Distinctly NAMED constructors, not an overloaded `of`: `Slot::of(h)` cannot infer
// Self from the argument, and a blanket generic over "any handle" defeats the purpose.
impl Slot<ResourceState> {
    pub unsafe fn resource(h: ddi::D3D10DDI_HRESOURCE) -> Option<Self>;
    pub unsafe fn load(&self) -> Option<&ResourceState>;
    pub unsafe fn store(&self, s: Box<ResourceState>);
}
impl Slot<RtvState> { pub unsafe fn rtv(h: ddi::D3D10DDI_HRENDERTARGETVIEW) -> Option<Self>; }
impl<T: Interface> Slot<Com<T>> {
    pub unsafe fn shader(h: ddi::D3D10DDI_HSHADER) -> Option<Self>;
    pub unsafe fn dsv(h: ddi::D3D10DDI_HDEPTHSTENCILVIEW) -> Option<Self>;
    pub unsafe fn raw(&self) -> usize;       // replaces the free `handle_com_raw`
}
/// The ONLY way to populate a create handle: stores on Ok, reports via
/// pfnSetErrorCb on Err. `Slot::store` becomes private to this helper, so a
/// VOID-returning Create* DDI cannot compile a path that neither stores nor
/// reports (u-forward-a-02 — currently 3 such paths, worst is the PRIMARY create).
pub fn finish_create<T>(h: Hdevice, slot: Slot<Com<T>>, r: windows::core::Result<T>, on_err: i32);
```

```rust
// umd/src/bridge.rs — the newtype is the ONLY seal: cxx generates the raw methods
// as *inherent* methods on the public opaque `ffi::HeliosDxvkDevice`, and inherent
// methods of a re-exported public type stay callable regardless of module privacy.
mod ffi { /* #[cxx::bridge], now private */ }
pub struct BridgeDevice { inner: cxx::UniquePtr<ffi::HeliosDxvkDevice> } // no Deref
impl BridgeDevice {
    pub fn open_ddi_texture2d(&self, /* .. */) -> Option<ID3D11Resource> {  // ADOPTS
        let raw = unsafe { self.inner.open_ddi_texture2d(/* .. */) };
        (raw != 0).then(|| unsafe { ID3D11Resource::from_raw(raw as *mut c_void) })
    }
    pub fn d3d11_device(&self) -> Option<ManuallyDrop<ID3D11Device>>;        // BORROWS
}
```

For the two adjacent present APIs whose parameter order is *transposed* — `present_sync_publish(src,
dst, kwait)` vs `present_vehicle_copy(dst, src)`, called 30 lines apart — the expressible fix is cxx
**shared structs**, not Rust newtypes (a `#[repr(transparent)]` newtype over `usize` cannot appear in a
cxx signature):

```rust
#[cxx::bridge]
mod ffi {
    struct SrcRes { ptr: usize }
    struct DstRes { ptr: usize }
    unsafe extern "C++" {
        unsafe fn present_vehicle_copy(self: &HeliosDxvkDevice, dst: DstRes, src: SrcRes) -> bool;
        unsafe fn present_sync_publish(self: &HeliosDxvkDevice, dst: DstRes, src: SrcRes,
                                       kwait_ordered: bool) -> u64;
    }
}
```

**Unrepresentable after.** A cross-kind handle cast outside `device.rs`/`handles.rs`; a field read that
skipped the magic check; `load_com::<ID3D11RenderTargetView>(rtv_slot)` fabricating an interface over
an `RtvState` box; adopting a borrowed COM pointer (double release) or `ManuallyDrop`-ing an owned one
(leak); storing the VidPn interface pointer on the adapter; a transposed (src,dst) present call.

**Residual, stated honestly.** `from_raw`'s precondition — "this handle really is the value we
returned" — is dxgkrnl's contract and is not encodable; it stays one `unsafe fn` with a documented
precondition and a null check. Three UMD DDIs (`discard_11_1`, `clear_view_11_1`,
`tiled_barrier_child`) receive a bare `*mut c_void` plus a runtime `D3D11DDI_HANDLETYPE` tag, so their
payload type is chosen by a *value*: they need an explicit tag→`Slot` match, not a static overload.

**Migration order.** `AllocHandleRef` and `DeviceHandleRef` first (S each, six call sites, and
`create_allocation.rs:1426` gains its missing null check as a separately-flagged behavior change).
`Slot<P>` next, reimplementing today's free functions on top of it with **no call-site churn**, plus
`store_com`'s null check and the `clear_rtv` duplicate cast — then convert call sites module by module
as part of the forward.rs split. `u-bridge-24`'s six inverted `unsafe` markings before `BridgeDevice`
(they touch the same declarations). `u-bridge-15`'s two-line `static_cast` change immediately: zero
codegen difference today, compile-time protection if DXVK's `D3D11Device` ever gains a second base.

### 5. RAII guards for gates, locks, mappings, COM and kernel objects

~18 findings, and the mechanism behind three of the four `severity=high` display bugs.

**Invariants encoded.** The `vidpn_programming` display-engine gate is set at exactly one site and
cleared at **nine** hand-written `store(0)` calls inside a 196-line function plus one asynchronous
clear in the used-ring DPC through a raw `NonNull<AtomicU32>`; leaving it set permanently suppresses
CRTC_VSYNC and stops the display retiring flips, which is exactly what `k-display-01` /
`k-lifecycle-01` / `x-ordering-01` / `x-ordering-02` report as live defects (`k-display-02`,
`k-display-18`). Three hand-written spinlock tables with three different capacity-check spellings and
prose-justified `unsafe impl Sync` (`k-paging-12`: `PagingPteShadow`, `SystemBackingTable`,
`MappingTable`). GDI batch mappings released by one loop at the end of `execute()` with no other unmap
path (`k-paging-22`). VidPn mode sets acquired and released across eight numbered fail points, **two of
which leak a created set on every failed modality enumeration** (`k-display-13`, `x-ordering-15`).
Partial-failure unwind in `OpenAllocation`/`CreateAllocation` (`k-alloc-09`). UMD `CreateDevice`
constructing in place before validating `pDeviceFuncs`, leaking the DXVK device, runtime context and
paging queue on two late paths (`u-core-01`, `x-ordering-13`); a shared/present BUFFER leaking its
already-made WDDM allocation (`u-forward-a-03`); the zero-refcount COM construction window
(`u-bridge-02`); the HPD worker join that returns success-shaped on `ObReferenceObjectByHandle`
failure and then lets StopDevice tear down the transport underneath a live worker
(`k-lifecycle-12`).

**Shape.**

```rust
// kmd_render/src/sync.rs — one implementation replacing three hand-written copies.
pub(crate) struct SpinLock<T> { lock: UnsafeCell<KSPIN_LOCK>, value: UnsafeCell<T> }
unsafe impl<T: Send> Send for SpinLock<T> {}
unsafe impl<T: Send> Sync for SpinLock<T> {}
pub(crate) struct SpinGuard<'a, T> {
    owner: &'a SpinLock<T>, irql: KIRQL, _not_send: PhantomData<*const ()>,
}
impl<T> SpinLock<T> {
    /// 0 is the initialized+unlocked state of a KSPIN_LOCK (same rationale the
    /// three existing copies already rely on), so this is a const fn.
    pub(crate) const fn new(v: T) -> Self {
        Self { lock: UnsafeCell::new(0), value: UnsafeCell::new(v) }
    }
    pub(crate) fn lock(&self) -> SpinGuard<'_, T> {
        let irql = unsafe { KeAcquireSpinLockRaiseToDpc(self.lock.get()) };
        SpinGuard { owner: self, irql, _not_send: PhantomData }
    }
}
impl<T> core::ops::Deref for SpinGuard<'_, T> { /* &*self.owner.value.get() */ }
impl<T> core::ops::DerefMut for SpinGuard<'_, T> { /* &mut *self.owner.value.get() */ }
impl<T> Drop for SpinGuard<'_, T> {
    fn drop(&mut self) { unsafe { KeReleaseSpinLock(self.owner.lock.get(), self.irql) } }
}

/// The "push stays inside reserved capacity so it cannot allocate under the lock"
/// rule, in one place with one spelling (today: `len() == MAX`, `len() < capacity()`,
/// `len() < MAX_MAPPINGS`).
pub(crate) struct FixedVec<T, const N: usize> { buf: alloc::vec::Vec<T> }
impl<T, const N: usize> FixedVec<T, N> {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self { Self { buf: Vec::with_capacity(N) } }
    pub(crate) fn push(&mut self, v: T) -> Result<(), T> {
        if self.buf.len() >= N { return Err(v); }
        self.buf.push(v); Ok(())
    }
}
```

```rust
// kmd_render/src/adapter.rs — nine store(0) sites collapse into one Drop.
#[must_use]
pub(crate) struct ProgrammingInterval<'a> { gate: &'a AtomicU32, _ns: PhantomData<*const ()> }
impl<'a> ProgrammingInterval<'a> {
    /// ADOPT, not construct: the gate is raised in the DIRQL DDI, a different call
    /// stack, so the token cannot be carried across the deferral.
    pub(crate) fn adopt(gate: &'a AtomicU32) -> Self { Self { gate, _ns: PhantomData } }
    /// The ONE legitimate escape: ownership passes to the ring-1 completion DPC.
    pub(crate) fn transfer_to_completion(self) { core::mem::forget(self) }
}
impl Drop for ProgrammingInterval<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) { self.gate.store(0, Ordering::Release) }
}
```

```rust
// kmd_render/src/ddi/vidpn.rs — Drop releases, assign() transfers ownership to the OS.
pub(crate) struct SourceModeSet<'a> {
    vidpn: &'a VidPn<'a>, h: D3DKMDT_HVIDPNSOURCEMODESET,
    iface: &'a DXGK_VIDPNSOURCEMODESET_INTERFACE,
}
impl SourceModeSet<'_> {
    pub(crate) fn assign(self, src: D3DDDI_VIDEO_PRESENT_SOURCE_ID) -> NTSTATUS {
        let st = /* pfnAssignSourceModeSet */;
        if NT_SUCCESS(st) { core::mem::forget(self); }   // the OS owns it now
        st
    }
}
impl Drop for SourceModeSet<'_> { fn drop(&mut self) { /* pfnReleaseSourceModeSet */ } }
```

`VidPn::open` must resolve the interface function pointers once into non-`Option` fields — an
`.unwrap()` on a bindgen `Option<fn>` inside a `Drop` is a bugcheck, and that resolution is exactly
`k-display-15`'s `VidPn<'a>` wrapper.

```rust
// umd — panic = abort in both profiles, so Drop only has to cover normal returns,
// which is precisely the failure mode (two late returns after in-place construction).
pub struct PartialDevice<'a>(&'a mut core::mem::MaybeUninit<HeliosDevice>);
impl PartialDevice<'_> {
    pub fn commit(self) -> &mut HeliosDevice { /* mem::forget the guard */ }
}
impl Drop for PartialDevice<'_> { fn drop(&mut self) { /* today's teardown, in order */ } }
```

**Unrepresentable after.** A return path from `apply_vidpn_source_address_locked` that leaves the gate
armed (the only way is to call `transfer_to_completion`, which is the intended contract and becomes one
greppable call instead of an absence); an early return between spinlock acquire and release; an early
return that leaks system PTEs from the GDI batch; a mode set created and neither assigned nor
released; a `CreateDevice` early return that leaks the DXVK device.

**Two hard limits.** (i) `UserMapping { user_va, mdl }` from `k-alloc-14` must be `#[must_use]` and
must **not** implement `Drop`: `MmUnmapLockedPages` is legal only at PASSIVE in the *creating* process,
so an RAII drop could fire in the wrong context and bugcheck 0x76. The guarantee there is "the pair
cannot be split or duplicated", not "it cannot be forgotten". (ii) `ProgrammingInterval` cannot express
the DIRQL-set/PASSIVE-clear split or the `DestroyAllocation` cancel path — those stay explicit,
counter-backed handoffs, which is why `k-display-01` and `k-display-18` remain separate work.

**Migration order.** `k-display-01` and `k-display-03` (the two live bugs) **before** the
`ProgrammingInterval` conversion, so the refactor does not silently fix two bugs and destroy the
before/after evidence for both. `SpinLock<T>` + `FixedVec` one table per commit, `PagingPteShadow`
first (smallest surface). The two missing `pfnRelease*ModeSet` calls (2 lines, S) land independently of
and before the mode-set guard tranche (L).
